바이브 코딩은 개발 경험이 적은 사람도 자신에게 필요한 프로그램을 만들어: Vibe coding attracted attention for the possibility that even people with little development experience could build programs they needed. Describing features in natural language, running generated programs, inspecting their results, and requesting revisions lowers the effort required to turn an idea into an implementation. This led to testing ideas through prototypes, creating tools for personal needs, and sharing building experiences. These examples do not, however, quantitatively establish the causes of vibe coding’s spread. This section distinguishes reasons people could try it from signs of widening interest. Reducing the burden of code knowledge. Building programs usually requires learning a language’s syntax, a development environment, and libraries. Connecting external services also requires understanding APIs, application programming interfaces through which programs exchange requests and data. For someone unfamiliar with this process, implementing even a simple feature involves learning. A clearly understood problem may remain unaddressed because its implementation is unfamiliar. Natural language requests allow participation before all this knowledge has been acquired. People who understand their field’s needs and what makes a result useful can begin by turning that understanding into requirements. For a webpage searching local support organizations, for example, they can explain the intended users, searchable information, and presentation of results, then try the screen and request missing features. Domain knowledge helps define requirements and judge usefulness. Willison likewise argued that automating a specific personal task should not necessarily require a computer science degree or programming education [14]. Lovable, a service for building web apps through natural language, provides another example of broader participation. Reporting in July 2025 put its active users at 2.3 million and daily project creation above 100,000 [5]. These figures describe one service’s usage, rather than proving that every user was a nondeveloper or demonstrating vibe coding’s effectiveness. They do show a substantial audience for tools that help turn ideas into screens and features. Testing ideas with working prototypes. Reducing implementation time broadens what people can attempt. They can first build a prototype to test essential features, then identify needed functionality and revisions through use. A written proposal can leave people imagining different screen layouts or user journeys. A clickable screen makes missing features and points of friction easier to discuss concretely. If an idea seems unnecessary, they can change direction or try another. Lower initial effort makes such iteration easier. Willison described vibe coding as useful for prototyping to test whether an idea could work [15]. Prototyping and iterative improvement existed in earlier development, but natural language requests can offer people with less experience a way into that process. When building requires considerable time and money, there is a stronger incentive to fix requirements early and minimize changes. When an initial result is easy to obtain, it becomes easier to build first and discover or adjust goals through the resulting behavior. Speed also motivated experienced developers. In March 2025, TechCrunch reported that 25% of startups in Y Combinator’s winter batch had generated approximately 95% of their codebases with AI [6]. This concerns a particular cohort as reported; it is not a measurement of time saved or evidence of the overall performance of vibe coding. Building small tools for personal needs. A clearly felt inconvenience in work or daily life may still be too costly or time-consuming to justify a dedicated program. Lower implementation effort can make these small needs worth addressing directly. A planner can build a screen demonstrating an idea; a student can devise a calculator or visualization for studying. Their activities supply the program’s purpose and criteria for judging results. New York Times reporter Kevin Roose described building an app suggesting packed lunches from refrigerator photos in about ten minutes, connecting it to the idea of software for one person [16]. Linus Torvalds’s audio effects project AudioNoise also illustrates creating a needed supporting tool. He said he wrote the core audio processing code himself while using vibe coding mainly for Python visualization tools to inspect results [13]. From addressing one person’s inconvenience to supporting professional work, the amount delegated to AI can vary with the features and risks involved. One researcher’s experience: building a tool for an experiment. A researcher without a programming degree found checking and saving sensor data during experiments cumbersome. Needing a tool suited to the experiment, the researcher began building one by describing desired features to AI. They requested graphs and file storage for sensor data, ran the program, and reported errors and inconveniences to guide revisions. Performance testing with actual equipment and further development were still needed, but the researcher could envision the needed functions and attempt their implementation. Understanding the experimental process provided the starting point. Turning a domain-specific inconvenience into requirements and improving a result through direct use illustrates why someone might become interested in vibe coding.
제작 경험의 공유와 용어의 확산 누군가 제작 과정이나 프롬프트, 결과물을: Sharing building experiences and the spread of the term. When someone publishes their process, prompts, or results, others can adapt them to their own purposes. Articles and videos showing the process encourage experimentation; prompts illustrate how to explain needed information and conditions. A runnable or reproducible result lets newcomers begin by examining existing features and changing some of them. Shared experiences can reduce the next user’s initial effort, and newly shared results can carry applications into other fields. Tool growth also indicates widening interest. In July 2025, Tech.eu reported that Lovable had 2.3 million active users, more than 100,000 projects created daily, and annual recurring revenue of $100 million approximately eight months after launch. ARR annualizes recurring revenue such as subscriptions. These figures describe the service’s usage and revenue at the time of reporting [5]. Interest in the term itself also increased. In March 2025, Willison cited coverage by the New York Times, Ars Technica, and the Guardian, together with online discussion, noting that ‘vibe coding’ was beginning to describe AI-assisted development more broadly [14]. Collins selected it as its word of the year, and Merriam-Webster also explains it in a slang entry [10] [8]. Service usage, news coverage, and dictionary inclusion measure different phenomena. Together they indicate widening interest, but cannot establish how much each factor contributed to the spread. Changing entry barriers gave people reasons to try vibe coding; published building experiences and media introductions made its possibilities more widely known. As participation broadened, so did the work covered by the name. Section 2.4 distinguishes its definitions and scopes of use.
앞선 두 절에서는 Prompt Engineering(프롬프트 엔지니어링): The preceding two sections examined using prompt engineering to convey intentions and examples, and agentic coding in which agents continue working through tool use. But when an agent reads code, modifies it, and makes new decisions based on execution results, can it refer to all available information at once?
LLM은 학습을 통해 형성된 지식과 현재 입력으로 제공된 Contex(컨: An LLM generates responses using knowledge developed through training and the context supplied in its current input. Context includes not only conversation with the user but also system instructions, relevant code, retrieved materials, and tool results. There is an upper limit on how much input a model can process at once. Even information included in that input may not be used equally well, depending on its position and other factors. The answer to the preceding question is therefore closer to ‘no’.
다시 말하자면, 사람과 협업할 때 필요한 자료나 이전 작업의 결과가 공유: Just as human collaboration stalls when necessary materials or earlier results are not shared, an agent needs information appropriate to the current goal. Even with the same revision request, omitting relevant code or a previously observed error can prevent appropriate work.
따라서 에이전트의 각 작업 단계에서 어떤 정보를 제공하고, 이전 작업의: We therefore need to design what information each stage receives, how earlier results are retained, and how new findings are incorporated. This section examines context engineering: designing how necessary information is assembled and updated for successive task stages, how the concept arose, and how it differs from related forms of engineering.
앞서 살펴보았듯, <v0>Context(컨텍스트)</v0>는 모델이 응답: As discussed earlier, <v0>context</v0> is information a model refers to as input when generating a response. It includes not only the user’s question but system instructions, examples, relevant conversation, retrieved documents, tool descriptions, and execution results. Anthropic describes it as the set of tokens supplied at inference time (<v1>Anthropic, 2025, ‘Effective context engineering for AI agents’, section ‘Context engineering vs. prompt engineering’</v1>).
이어서 등장하는 개념인 <v0>Context Window(컨텍스트 윈도): A <v0>context window</v0> is the range of information a model can reference while generating one response, usually understood as an upper limit measured in tokens, the units in which the model processes input. Beyond conversation history, it includes system instructions, loaded files, retrieved material, tool descriptions, and execution results. In some APIs, generated output shares the same window with input, so room for the response must also be reserved. The context window is distinct from storage for all the data on which the model was trained (<v1>Anthropic, n.d.-a, ‘Context windows’, section ‘How the context window works’</v1>).
이를 바탕으로, 모델이 어떤 정보를 얼마나 활용할 수 있는지를 고려하여: <v0>Context engineering</v0> assembles and manages context with regard to which information a model can use and how much. Two considerations explain its necessity: models have a limit on the information they can process at once, and even information within that limit is not always used equally well.
먼저, 언어 모델이 한 번의 처리 과정에서 다룰 수 있는 정보의 범위에는: First, a language model can process only a limited amount of information in one pass. Processing more input tokens generally increases computation and memory use. Dai and colleagues explained that Transformer language models face computational constraints when handling long contexts. Window size is therefore determined by factors including model architecture, training methods, and available computing resources (<v0/>).
LLM 설계와 반도체 기술이 동시에 발전하면서 컨텍스트 윈도의 크기도 점: Advances in LLM design and semiconductor technology have gradually expanded context windows. The 2019 GPT-2 research increased context size from the earlier GPT’s 512 tokens to 1,024; the models in the 2020 GPT-3 research used 2,048 tokens (<v0/>; <v1/>). By November 2026, GPT-6.1 Sol’s context window reached 1,050,000 tokens (<v2/>). Regardless of growth, actual models and services retain an upper limit on information usable at once.
다음으로, 컨텍스트에 포함된 정보를 모델이 실제로 얼마나 활용하는지도 고: Second, we must consider how effectively a model uses information included in its context. In 2018, Khandelwal and colleagues deleted, replaced, and reordered earlier words in LSTM language models and measured changes in perplexity, a prediction-performance measure. On Penn Treebank and WikiText-2, the studied models used approximately 200 past tokens on average and treated the most recent roughly 50 differently from distant context. This was an early quantification of contextual contributions for particular models and datasets (<v0>Khandelwal et al., 2018, ‘Sharp nearby, fuzzy far away: How neural language models use context’, §5 and §8</v0>).
Input length and effective use also differ in recent long-context LLMs. Liu and colleagues changed the position of an answer-bearing document and compared question-answering performance. In a 20-document experiment, GPT-3.5-Turbo achieved 75.8% accuracy when that document came first, 53.8% when tenth, and 63.2% when last. Relevant evidence was present in every case, but position affected the result (<v0>Liu et al., 2023, ‘Lost in the middle: How language models use long contexts’, Appendix G.2, Table 6</v0>).
따라서 “AI가 한 번에 다룰 수 있는 정보량은 얼마인가?”라는 질문에는: The question ‘How much information can AI handle at once?’ therefore requires distinguishing capacity from effective use under a particular arrangement. A larger window creates room for longer material but does not find missing evidence or update obsolete information automatically. Reducing input alone does not automatically improve freshness or accuracy either. Current information requires appropriate retrieval and updating, and organizing input must preserve evidence needed for the task. Context engineering addresses both conditions to find an appropriate quantity and arrangement of information for the current task.
이 문제를 다루는 기술은 용어가 널리 퍼지기 전부터 발전해 왔다. Lew: Techniques addressing this problem developed before the term became widespread. Retrieval-augmented generation, proposed by Lewis and colleagues in 2020, supplements knowledge stored within a model by retrieving external evidence and combining it with generation (<v0>Lewis et al., 2020, ‘Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks’, §2 and Figure 1</v0>). In 2023, Packer and colleagues introduced MemGPT, a memory-management architecture distinguishing the context window from external storage and moving information between them as needed (<v1/>). These studies provide technical background for constructing context through retrieval and memory management, respectively.
이처럼 여러 이름으로 발전하던 작업을 하나의 설계 문제로 바라보게 하는: Developer discussions in June 2025 popularized a name treating work previously developed under several labels as one design problem. On June 19, Tobi Lütke wrote on X, formerly Twitter, that he preferred ‘context engineering’ to ‘prompt engineering’, emphasizing the ability to supply enough relevant context for an LLM to solve a task (<v0/>). The central concern was to examine whether the model received the conditions needed to answer, alongside refining the question itself. Repeating ‘Fix it accurately’ cannot supply omitted code or expected behavior.
이에 더해, 바이브코딩의 아버지라고 불리는 Andrej Karpathy: On June 25, 2025, Andrej Karpathy, often called the father of vibe coding, quote-posted Lütke’s original message on X. Opening with <v0/>, he endorsed the name and explained that while an everyday prompt suggests a short task description, industrial LLM applications require assembling information appropriate to the next step within the context window (<v1/>). This was a public explanation of the name’s suitability to industrial system design, rather than academic approval of the term <v2>context engineering</v2>.
Simon Willison의 2025년 6월 27일 글은 <v0>이름이: Simon Willison’s June 27, 2025 article focuses on <v0>what work a name makes people imagine</v0>. He had hoped prompt engineering could encompass the complex work of constructing reliable inputs, but observed that people interpreted it as simply typing sentences into a chatbot. He saw ‘context engineering’ as a more intuitive way to convey the actual scope of the work (<v1/>).
Philipp Schmid는 6월 30일 글에서 <v0>그 작업을 어떤: In his June 30 article, Philipp Schmid emphasizes <v0>the system through which that work is implemented</v0>. He describes context engineering as designing dynamic systems that provide appropriate information and tools in the right format and at the right time. This includes system and user instructions, current history, long-term memory, retrieved material, available tool definitions, and structured output formats (<v1>Schmid, 2025, ‘The new skill in AI is not prompting, it’s context engineering’, sections ‘What is the Context?’ and ‘From Prompt to Context Engineering’</v1>). The comparison suggests Willison emphasizes terminology and public understanding, while Schmid emphasizes the structure and timing of information delivery.
학술 문헌에서도 개념을 체계화하려는 시도가 뒤따랐다. 2025년 7월 1: Academic attempts to systematize the concept followed. Mei and colleagues’ survey, first released on July 17, 2025, proposes a definition in §3.1 and classifies related techniques as context retrieval, generation, processing, and management (<v0/>). The DSBC paper published at IJCNLP-AACL that December also explicitly uses context engineering in its evaluation design (<v1/>).
프롬프트 엔지니어링과 컨텍스트 엔지니어링은 <v0>설계하는 대상과 범위<: Prompt engineering and context engineering can be distinguished by <v0>the object and scope of design</v0>. Here, prompt engineering means designing and improving the instructions, examples, input structure, and output requirements through which a task is conveyed to a model. This includes specifying goals, clarifying constraints, and arranging examples and required formats.
Context Engineering은 이러한 지시를 포함해 <v0>모델이: Context engineering designs <v0>the selection, organization, delivery, and updating of all information a model needs for its current task</v0>, including those instructions. It considers where to find relevant files and literature, which history to retain, when to provide tool descriptions and results, and what should replace outdated material. Anthropic emphasizes this difference in scope by describing prompt engineering as writing and organizing instructions and context engineering as strategies for curating and maintaining the full token context during inference (<v1>Anthropic, 2025, ‘Effective context engineering for AI agents’, section ‘Context engineering vs. prompt engineering’</v1>).
프롬프트 자체도 컨텍스트의 일부이므로 두 영역은 겹친다. 예시의 내용과: Because prompts form part of context, the two overlap. Improving examples and their order is both prompt design and context construction; deciding which tasks should retrieve those examples concerns information delivery. It is therefore inappropriate to distinguish the concepts simply as short versus long instructions, manual versus automatic work, or one call versus multiple calls.
이에 등장한 개념인 하네스(Harness)는 컨텍스트 구성을 지원하고 모: A harness is the surrounding execution system that supports context construction and connects models, tools, and execution results. Designing and implementing it is harness engineering. The following chapter will examine its concrete components and uses.
3장은 AI에게 일을 맡기는 방법을 네 방향에서 살펴보았다. 3.1은 요: Chapter 3 has examined delegating to AI from four directions. Section 3.1 considered writing requests; 3.2, AI’s development toward editing files and executing commands; 3.3, selecting information for a task; and 3.4, preparing specifications and plans before generating code. This section asks the next question: where and in what form should a defined task be delegated to AI?
같은 요청을 여러 도구에 넣어 보면 이 질문이 왜 필요한지 드러난다. “: Trying the same request in several tools illustrates why this matters. Consider the hypothetical request ‘Fix the function whose tests fail.’ In general chat, users paste the code and error message, copy the suggested fix into their files, and rerun it themselves. In an AI editor, AI consults open files and users decide whether to accept proposed diffs. A terminal agent runs tests to reproduce the failure, locates and edits related files, reruns tests, and reports results. An agent working remotely performs this process out of the user’s view and returns changes in a branch or pull request, a request to incorporate changes into a repository.
네 경우 모두 요청은 같고, 같은 모델이 쓰였을 수도 있다. 달라진 것은: The request is identical in all four cases, and even the model might be the same. What changes is the human’s work. Initially, collecting information, running code, and checking results all fall to the person. Moving through the examples, the first two shift toward AI, leaving the person to define the delegation and review the returned result. Section 1.4 traced completion through conversational coding; 3.2 examined changes when AI began using tools directly. The execution structure outside the model that produces these differences is a harness, discussed in 7.1.
이 꼭지는 도구를 제품 단위로 비교하지 않는다. 제품의 기능은 몇 달 단: This section compares forms of work rather than individual products. Features change within months, and one company often provides a chat app, editor extension, command-line tool, and cloud agent. Product comparison tables age before publication. Instead, we use four ways humans and AI divide work: general chat, AI IDE, terminal agent, and background agent. An IDE, or integrated development environment, combines code editing, execution, and debugging in one program. Focusing on work forms distinguishes rapidly changing products and features from more enduring structures of responsibility.
네 형태를 가르는 기준은 세 가지로 정리할 수 있다. 첫째, AI가 무엇: Three criteria distinguish the four forms. First, what can AI see and change: pasted code alone, or the project and execution environment? Second, how does work proceed: with a person following each step, or through scoped delegation while the person does something else? Third, what comes back: explanations and snippets, diffs, or execution records and test results too? The change from conversational programming to coding agents in 3.2 also expanded these dimensions. New forms have not replaced earlier ones: all four coexist, and one person can switch between them within a project.
네 형태는 사람이 AI와 만나는 자리, AI가 보고 바꿀 수 있는 범위,: The four forms differ in where people interact with AI, what AI can see and change, what is returned, and the work remaining for humans. Product examples and feature descriptions below were checked against official documentation on October 28, 2026. Versions are omitted because those documents did not specify them.
General chat involves exchanging questions and answers through a web or app conversation. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are representative general-purpose services. Users ask questions, paste code or error messages as needed, read responses, and continue the conversation. In principle, AI sees what users provide there. Recent services can also accept files and run code in an isolated environment within the conversation (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-10-28)), but that environment is separate from the user’s computer and project. Returned results include explanations, code snippets, and comparisons of alternatives.
이 형태에서 사람에게 남는 일은 많다. 무엇을 보여 줄지 고르는 일, 받: Much remains for the person: choosing information to provide, putting returned code into real files, running it, and relaying results. This burden has advantages as well as disadvantages. AI does not directly modify the project, avoiding unintended changes, and reading and copying code offers an opportunity to understand it. However, AI’s information can diverge from the project’s actual state. Omitted definitions from other files or installed library versions invite plausible guesses.
AI IDE는 코드 편집기 안에 AI 기능이 들어간 형태다. Cursor: An AI IDE embeds AI capabilities in a code editor. Some, such as Cursor, were built around AI; others add extensions to existing editors, such as GitHub Copilot in VS Code. Users receive completion suggestions while viewing code or request changes in a side conversation. AI can consult open and other project files, and proposed edits appear as file-by-file diffs in the editor. Users accept or revert changes individually.
이 형태의 특징은 사람이 코드를 보는 자리에서 AI의 변경을 확인한다는: The defining feature is reviewing AI’s changes where the person views the code. Unlike general chat, no copying is necessary, and changes appear beside the original. Modern AI IDEs also have agents that edit several files or run terminal commands (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-10-28); <v1/> (accessed: 2026-10-28)), making capability alone insufficient to distinguish them from terminal agents. The distinction is where review occurs: in an AI IDE, the editor’s diff view is central.
terminal agent는 명령줄 인터페이스(command-line i: A terminal agent runs through a command-line interface, or CLI. Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex CLI are representative examples (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-10-28); <v1>OpenAI, Codex documentation</v1> (accessed: 2026-10-28)). Users start the agent and assign work conversationally. On their computer, it finds, reads, and edits repository files, executes commands such as tests and builds, and decides subsequent actions from the results. It returns changes and records of commands and outputs. Despite the name, the launch screen does not define the form: an agent running from a desktop app or editor still counts here if it reads the repository and executes commands on the user’s computer.
이 형태는 사용자의 실제 개발 환경에서 동작한다는 점이 핵심이다. 설치된: The key is operating in the actual development environment. Installed libraries, local data, and configuration files remain available, letting the agent check whether code runs there. For the same reason, its actions directly affect real files and settings. Most tools therefore request approval before editing or executing commands and let users configure which approvals can be omitted. Section 8.3 explains approval procedures and sandboxes, which isolate program execution from the surrounding environment. People decide approvals and read execution records to check results. The same tool may also run noninteractively through a single command in scripts or automation. Section 6.2 covers retry limits and stopping conditions during repeated execution and verification; 16.3 covers persistent agents triggered by schedules or events.
background agent는 작업을 맡기면 사용자가 지켜보지 않는 곳: A background agent accepts a task, works out of view, and returns a result. GitHub’s Copilot cloud agent, OpenAI’s Codex Cloud, Claude Code cloud sessions, and Cursor Cloud Agents operate this way (<v0/>; <v1/>; <v2/>; <v3/> (all accessed: 2026-10-28)). Users assign work through web interfaces, issue or pull request comments, editors, or terminals. The agent clones the repository into an isolated remote environment, installs dependencies, edits files, and runs tests. It then posts changes to a branch or pull request and reports changes and test results. Meanwhile, users can do other work or delegate several tasks concurrently.
이 형태에서 사람의 일은 작업 전과 작업 후로 몰린다. 작업 전에는 무엇: Human work concentrates before and after execution. Before work begins, people must specify what to do, its boundaries, and what counts as finished. Weak instructions can produce misguided results because redirecting work midstream is harder. Afterward, people review the changes and decide whether to accept them. Remote execution also matters: local-only data and settings are absent, while repository contents and task information move into that environment. Section 6.1 covers completion criteria; Chapter 10 covers verifying returned results; and 15.1 examines how delegating and waiting for several tasks changes individual and team routines.
첫째, 네 형태는 같은 축 위의 네 칸이 아니다. 일반 chat, AI: First, the forms are not four positions on one axis. General chat, AI IDE, and terminal agent describe interaction environments; background agent describes how work proceeds. They can overlap, as when a task assigned in an editor or terminal runs remotely. VS Code Copilot can hand work to a cloud agent, and Claude Code can start cloud sessions from a terminal.
둘째, 네 형태는 발전 단계가 아니다. 표의 아래쪽이 더 앞선 도구라는: Second, these are not stages of development. Lower rows in the table do not imply more advanced tools or the disappearance of forms above them. Just as spreadsheets and no-code tools remain useful after AI coding tools emerge, each form suits particular work and coexists with the others.
셋째, 제품과 형태는 일대일로 대응하지 않는다. Claude Code는: Third, products do not map one-to-one to forms. Claude Code is available through terminals, editor extensions, desktop apps, and the web; Codex through a CLI, editor extension, and cloud service. Cursor offers both in-editor agents and remote Cloud Agents. Product updates can add another form. Asking ‘In which form are we using this tool for this task?’ is more precise than assigning a product one category. Section 17.3 considers whether these forms may converge.
넷째, 터미널에서 동작한다고 자율성이 높은 것은 아니다. terminal: Fourth, terminal operation does not imply high autonomy. A terminal agent can require approval for every edit, while an AI IDE can edit multiple files without it. Settings and human intervention, more than form, determine independent progress. Intervention is examined further among the considerations below.
형태를 고를 때 살펴볼 것은 다섯 가지다. 지금 작업이 어떤 상태인가,: Five considerations guide selection: the task’s current state, what AI must see and change, when people intervene, what they receive for review, and where execution occurs. The first four concern how work proceeds; the last is a prior constraint. These are not scores to add together. They interact, and one can eliminate an option before the others are considered.
설명에는 하나의 작은 작업을 계속 예로 든다. 이미 있는 CSV 분석 스: We use one small hypothetical task throughout: adding missing-value handling and charts to an existing CSV analysis script. Here, we consider only the form in which to delegate it. Section 4.2 covers reproducible data analysis with AI.
Barke 등은 프로그래머 20명이 코드 생성 도구인 GitHub Cop: Barke and colleagues observed 20 programmers solving tasks with GitHub Copilot and identified two modes (<v0>Barke et al., Grounded Copilot: How Programmers Interact with Code-Generating Models</v0> (Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages 7(OOPSLA1), 2023)). In acceleration mode, programmers already know the next step and use the tool to reach its implementation faster. In exploration mode, they do not yet know how to proceed and use outputs to examine possibilities. Their treatment of suggestions differed: acceleration-mode participants quickly scanned for fit and accepted them, finding long multiline suggestions disruptive. Exploration-mode participants compared several suggestions or used them as starting points, inspecting them more closely before acceptance.
이 구분이 형태 선택에 중요한 이유는, 탐색 중인 작업을 실행 중인 작업: This distinction matters because delegating exploration as if implementation were already decided can harden unmade decisions into code. Asking an agent to ‘handle missing values’ before deciding whether to drop or fill them lets it choose and implement either. A working result may then make that choice seem the default. Conversely, conducting a clearly defined implementation entirely through chat wastes time repeatedly copying code, executing it, and reporting results.
그래서 형태를 고르기 전에 지금이 어느 상태인지부터 묻는 편이 좋다. 간: Before selecting a form, identify the current state. A useful signal is whether completion can be described in one sentence. ‘Fill missing values in every numeric column with its mean and print counts before and after treatment’ indicates readiness for execution. If the description cannot go beyond ‘Handle missing values appropriately’, exploration remains necessary. Exploration suits lightweight, disposable outputs; execution suits forms that directly apply and check changes. Barke and colleagues studied a completion-centered tool and did not prescribe particular forms for exploration or acceleration. That connection is this book’s interpretation.
같은 프로젝트에서도 상태는 바뀐다. 처리 방법을 정하는 동안은 탐색이고,: Task state changes within a project. Choosing a treatment method is exploration; applying the chosen method across files is acceleration. Work forms can change accordingly. Section 3.4 discussed preserving exploration decisions as specifications and plans.
AI가 다룰 수 있는 범위는 대략 네 단계로 넓어진다. 대화에 붙여 넣은: AI’s scope expands through roughly four levels: code pasted into a conversation, project files, the local execution environment with commands, tests, and libraries, and external systems such as remote repositories or services. The four forms provide different scopes.
범위가 좁으면 AI는 사용자가 준 정보만으로 판단한다. 사용자가 빠뜨린: With narrow scope, AI judges only supplied information and guesses what is missing: function names defined elsewhere, installed library versions, or actual data-column names. The result may be syntactically correct and plausibly explained but unusable in the project; Section 9.1 covers such errors. Broader scope lets AI locate files and execute code to reduce these mismatches, but also enlarges what it can change. Unrequested changes to files or settings are discussed in 9.2.
그러면 범위는 어디까지 열어야 하는가. 이 책이 제안하는 기준은 AI가: How broad should scope be? This book proposes granting enough for AI to check whether its task is finished. A new chart function may require only a conversational description of inputs and outputs. Integrating missing-value handling with an existing preprocessing module requires access to that module and its callers. Checking results on real data requires execution. Tasks spanning files, requiring execution to verify, or touching external systems are likely to exceed conversation-only work.
사람이 개입하는 방식은 세 수준으로 나눌 수 있다. 매 응답을 보고 다음: Human intervention has three levels: progressing together by reviewing each response before the next request; letting AI proceed but approving every file change or command; and defining scope, delegating, then reviewing the finished result. General chat, AI IDEs, and terminal agents mainly use the first two; background agents are closer to the third. As noted, a terminal agent can move between the second and third depending on approval settings.
개입이 줄어든다고 사람의 판단이 줄어드는 것은 아니다. 판단이 일어나는: Less intervention does not mean less human judgment; judgment shifts from during the task to before and after it. Working together allows immediate redirection. Delegating and waiting requires clearer scope and completion criteria beforehand and consolidated review afterward. Reducing intervention is therefore closer to postponing review. This is the book’s proposal, rather than a research finding.
함께 진행하는 쪽이 나은 경우는 진행 중에 방향이 바뀔 가능성이 클 때,: Working together is preferable when direction may change, changes are difficult to reverse, or criteria for correctness cannot be determined before seeing results. Refining chart axes and colors by looking at the chart is faster with immediate feedback than delegated waiting. Applying an already defined missing-value rule consistently across several scripts can instead be scoped, delegated, and reviewed afterward. Section 6.2 covers retry limits and stopping conditions.
네 형태가 돌려주는 것은 점점 많아진다. 일반 chat은 설명과 코드 조: The four forms return progressively more material: general chat offers explanations and snippets; an AI IDE, file diffs; a terminal agent, diffs and execution records; a background agent, a branch or pull request with a change summary and test results. These outputs provide evidence for judging completion. Selecting a form therefore requires asking both what AI can produce and whether you can verify it.
두 질문을 나누어야 한다는 점은 초기 연구에서도 드러났다. Vaithil: Early research illustrated the need to separate these questions. Vaithilingam and colleagues had 24 participants complete programming tasks with and without GitHub Copilot (<v0>Vaithilingam et al., Expectation vs. Experience: Evaluating the Usability of Code Generation Tools Powered by Large Language Models</v0> (CHI 2022 Extended Abstracts)). Copilot did not necessarily improve completion time or success, yet most participants wanted it for everyday programming because it provided useful starting points and reduced online searching. They also struggled to understand, edit, and debug generated code, substantially obstructing task completion. This study concerned an early tool, not current product performance. Its distinction between producing code and enabling human review remains relevant.
돌려받는 결과물이 많아지면 검토가 쉬워지기도 하고 어려워지기도 한다. 실: More returned material can make review easier or harder. Execution records and test results reveal what was checked without requiring line-by-line reading. But changes spanning several files and dozens of command records require deciding what to inspect first. What matters is what the material lets you judge, rather than its volume.
여기서 가장 흔한 함정은 끝났다는 보고와 끝났다는 증거를 혼동하는 일이다: A common trap is confusing a completion report with evidence of completion. ‘Missing-value handling is complete’ does not reveal which rules affected which columns, how row counts changed, or whether anything was actually executed. Reviewable results require specifying what should accompany the response: applied rules, missing-value counts before and after treatment, commands and their outputs, and anything not checked. The last item matters particularly. Section 9.1 discusses plausible but false output. Section 10.3 covers agents changing code merely to pass tests, misrepresenting their behavior, and using work records to verify what happened.
이 고려사항에서 형태 선택의 한 가지 조건이 나온다. 맡기고 기다리는 형: This yields a condition for delegated, out-of-view work: you must be able to define completion in advance and have a way to verify the result, such as tests or an executable checking procedure. If either is missing, working together while inspecting results is preferable. Sections 6.1 and 10.1 cover completion criteria and test design; 10.3 covers reconstructing decisions from agent records; and 12.3 covers controlling returned changes through branches and automated checks.
마지막 고려사항은 AI가 실행하는 코드와 읽는 데이터가 어디에 있는가이다: The final consideration is where the code AI executes and the data it reads reside. Terminal agents run on the user’s computer; background agents run in isolated remote environments, sometimes on an organization’s own servers. Content pasted into general chat and files consulted by AI IDEs also reach a service’s servers whenever the model is externally hosted.
로컬에서 실행하면 내 환경 그대로 결과를 확인할 수 있지만, 에이전트의: Local execution lets you verify results in your actual environment but directly exposes your files and environment to the agent’s actions. Remote isolation separates execution from your computer, keeping the impact of mistakes within that environment. However, the repository and necessary data must move there, and local-only data or settings are unavailable.
이 고려사항은 다른 네 가지보다 먼저 걸리는 경우가 많다. 분석할 CSV: This consideration often precedes the others. If a CSV contains personal information or unpublished research data, first determine whether that data may be supplied to the AI tool before considering convenience. If not, options narrow considerably. You may anonymize it, substitute synthetic data, or need an operating arrangement that sends no data outside. Section 9.5 discusses transmission, training use, and retention conditions; 5.3 covers model and hosting choices; and 17.2 covers operating models yourself.
이 꼭지는 이번 작업을 어떤 형태로 시작할지를 다룬다. 여러 작업을 오래: This section concerns which form to start with for the current task. Section 7.2 discusses establishing an agent environment for longer-term delegation, including session continuity, memory, and permission allocation.
다섯 가지를 따지는 순서에도 일정한 흐름이 있다. 먼저 실행 위치에서 걸: The five considerations suggest a sequence. First check execution-location constraints: restrictions on supplying data may eliminate options immediately. Then identify task state. If still exploring, begin with lightweight, immediately inspectable outputs and make necessary decisions first. Once the task is clear, choose scope and intervention together. Provide enough scope for AI to verify completion, and match intervention to the likelihood of redirection and difficulty of reversal. Finally, check reviewability. Delegated waiting requires both completion criteria and verification means; if either is absent, return to working together.
이 순서는 한 번 정하고 끝나는 절차가 아니다. 같은 결측치 처리 작업도: This is not a one-time procedure. For the same missing-value task, you might explore treatment methods in chat, apply a chosen method to existing code in an editor, move to an execution-capable environment to test real data, and delegate applying the rule across other scripts within a defined scope. As task state changes, choose the form again.
바이브 코딩 주변에서 태어나고 진화하는 개념들의 사전이다. 항목마다 정의: This dictionary records concepts emerging and evolving around vibe coding. Each entry gives a definition, origin, and current status. Because new concepts appear and meanings change, the appendix remains permanently unfinished and is the book’s most frequently updated part. Each entry is a contribution unit. New entries and assignments are managed in the repository’s TOPICS.md.
자연어로 AI 코딩 에이전트에게 지시해 소프트웨어를 만드는 방식이다. 좁: A way of building software by instructing AI coding agents in natural language. Narrowly, it describes iterating by inspecting execution results without directly reading generated code. Broadly, it refers to AI-assisted development in general.
Andrej Karpathy가 2025년 2월 트윗에서 만든 말이다. 원: Andrej Karpathy coined the term in a February 2025 tweet containing ‘fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists’ (<v0>original tweet</v0>). In his first-anniversary retrospective in February 2026, he called it a ‘shower of thoughts throwaway tweet’ (<v1>retrospective tweet</v1>).
2025년 11월 Collins 사전 올해의 단어로 선정되며 일반어가 됐: The term entered general usage and became Collins Dictionary’s word of the year in November 2025 (<v0>announcement</v0>, <v1>report</v1>). Simon Willison proposed distinguishing development without reading code from AI-assisted development overall (<v2>article</v2>), but actual usage mixes the two meanings.
원하는 출력을 얻기 위해 모델에 주는 입력, 즉 프롬프트를 설계하는 기술: The practice of designing the input, or prompt, given to a model to obtain a desired output. It includes discovering and systematizing techniques such as arranging few-shot examples and eliciting chain-of-thought reasoning.
프롬프트 한 줄이 아니라 모델이 보는 컨텍스트 전체, 즉 파일, 문서,: The practice of designing the full context a model sees, including files, documents, conversation history, and tool outputs, rather than one prompt alone. It reflects a shift in the bottleneck from how to phrase a request to what information to show.
Tobi Lütke(Shopify CEO)가 2025년 6월 19일 트윗: Tobi Lütke, Shopify’s CEO, named it in a June 19, 2025 tweet, and Karpathy posted an endorsement (<v0>Karpathy’s tweet</v0>). Simon Willison and Phil Schmid each wrote explanatory articles (<v1/>, <v2/>).
AI가 한 번 답하고 끝나는 것이 아니라 도구를 호출하고 코드를 실행하고: A way of working in which AI does more than answer once: it repeatedly calls tools, executes code, checks results, and chooses subsequent actions. It is the technical form that made vibe coding practicable.
Who first used ‘agentic coding’, and when, requires verification. Anthropic’s ‘Building Effective Agents’ from December 2024 provides a reference explaining the loop structure itself (<v0>link</v0>).
CLI형 코딩 에이전트(Claude Code 등)와 IDE 통합형 에이전: CLI coding agents such as Claude Code and IDE-integrated agents are representative implementations. Sections §2.3 and §8.2 discuss tool history and loop structure, respectively.
Steve Yegge가 바이브 코딩이라는 말이 나오기 전에 만든 용어다: Steve Yegge coined the term before ‘vibe coding’ appeared (<v0>O’Reilly podcast</v0>); its exact earliest use needs verification. Yegge coauthored the book ‘Vibe Coding’ with Gene Kim, but precise publication details also need checking.
바이브 코딩의 속도를 유지하면서도 결과물의 책임을 지는 작업 방식을 가리: A way of retaining vibe coding’s speed while taking responsibility for its results. It is effectively a proposal to reintegrate engineering practices such as verification, testing, and review into vibe coding workflows.
에이전트를 실제로 작동하게 만드는 실행 환경, 즉 도구 접근, 권한, 루: The execution environment that makes an agent operational, encompassing tool access, permissions, loop control, and context management. The formulation ‘Agent = Model + Harness’ expresses the view that harness design influences agent quality independently of model capability.
프롬프트 엔지니어링에서 컨텍스트 엔지니어링을 거쳐 하네스 엔지니어링으로: It has been described as the third stage after prompt engineering and context engineering (<v0>Faros AI blog</v0>). Who first used ‘harness’ for an agent execution environment before that article requires verification.
AI에게 바로 코드를 시키지 않고 먼저 명세, 즉 스펙을 함께 작성한 뒤: A development approach that begins by jointly writing a specification rather than immediately asking AI for code, then uses the specification to guide generation and verification. It is often presented as a response to the verification problem in vibe coding without reading code.
메인 에이전트가 특정 작업을 별도의 독립된 에이전트 인스턴스에 위임하는: A structure in which a main agent delegates a specific task to an independent agent instance, or an individual agent executing such a delegated task. A subagent typically has its own context window and tool-access scope and returns its result to the main agent when finished. Coordinating multiple subagents concurrently or sequentially forms a multi-agent system.
자동화된 시스템의 실행 과정에 사람의 확인이나 개입 지점을 명시적으로 두: A design that explicitly includes human checks or intervention points during automated execution. In AI coding agents, it means mechanisms requiring approval before actions such as file changes, command execution, or deployment that can be difficult to reverse.
언어 모델이 사실이 아니거나 존재하지 않는 내용을 그럴듯하게 생성하는 현: A language model’s generation of plausible content that is false or nonexistent. Typical coding examples include presenting nonexistent functions, libraries, or APIs as real.
품질 검토 없이 대량으로 생성된, 낮은 품질의 AI 산출물을 가리키는 말: Low-quality AI output generated at scale without quality review. ‘Workslop’ refers specifically to outputs colleagues or organizations must consume, such as reports, documents, or code.
AI 코딩 에이전트가 환각으로 만들어낸, 실재하지 않는 패키지명을 공격자: A supply chain attack in which an attacker registers a nonexistent package name hallucinated by an AI coding agent. A developer who installs the agent’s suggestion unchanged instead installs the attacker’s malicious package.
유래 확인 필요. 누가 언제 이 용어를 만들었는지 원 출처를 찾아 검증해: Origin needs verification. Primary sources are needed to identify who coined the term and when. It appears to derive from typosquatting, registering package names that exploit typing mistakes, but that lineage also requires checking.
AI 모델이 외부 도구, 데이터 소스, 서비스와 통신하는 방식을 표준화한: A protocol standardizing communication between AI models and external tools, data sources, and services. Implementing a compliant server allows different AI applications to reuse the same tool-integration code.
코딩 에이전트가 파일 시스템 바깥의 도구(브라우저, 데이터베이스, 사내: It has become a standard route for coding agents to access tools beyond the file system, such as browsers, databases, and internal systems. Some practical implementations are also replacing MCP servers with direct API calls.
모델이 답을 생성하기 전에 외부 문서나 데이터베이스에서 관련 내용을 검색: A technique that retrieves relevant material from external documents or databases and includes it in the prompt before a model answers. It enables responses to incorporate current information or private documents absent from training data.
토큰은 언어 모델이 텍스트를 처리하는 최소 단위로, 단어보다 작을 수도: A token is the smallest unit in which a language model processes text; it may be smaller than a word or span several words. A context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can reference at once.
코딩 에이전트가 다룰 수 있는 코드베이스의 크기, 대화의 길이, 컨텍스트: This limit affects the size of codebases agents can handle, conversation length, and the number of files included in context. Some observers argue that larger windows make context engineering (G3) more important. Section §5.3 covers practical management techniques.
AI 모델이나 에이전트의 출력을 정해진 기준에 따라 채점하는 절차, 또는: A procedure for scoring model or agent outputs against defined criteria, or the test collection used for that scoring. Analogous to software unit tests, evals quantitatively assess performance and regressions.
AI 시스템의 입력과 출력에 제약을 걸어 의도하지 않은 행동이나 위험한: Mechanisms constraining AI inputs and outputs to prevent unintended behavior or dangerous results. They operate at several levels, including prompt filtering, output validation, and execution-permission restrictions.
코딩 에이전트에서는 파일 접근 범위 제한, 위험 명령 차단, 실행 전 승: Coding-agent examples include restricting file access, blocking dangerous commands, and requiring approval before execution, overlapping considerably with human-in-the-loop design (G11). Sections §9.2 and §9.5 discuss security and responsibility, respectively.
소프트웨어 2.0은 사람이 직접 규칙을 코드로 짜는 대신 데이터로 신경망: Software 2.0 describes building programs by training neural-network weights on data instead of manually coding rules. Software 3.0 extends this lineage to programming model behavior through natural language prompts.
소프트웨어 2.0은 Andrej Karpathy가 2017년에 쓴 글에서: Andrej Karpathy introduced Software 2.0 in a 2017 article (<v0>link</v0>). Who formalized the subsequent Software 3.0 concept, and when, requires verification.

“인장 시험 데이터로 항복강도 구하는 코드 짜 줘.” 이 한 문장만 받은: ‘Write code to calculate yield strength from tensile test data.’ Given only this sentence, AI must make many assumptions. It does not specify the file format, whether strain is expressed as a percentage or decimal, whether yield strength should follow the 0.2% offset method or another criterion, or whether to return a number or a chart. Adding this information reduces guesswork and changes the code returned.
AI에게 주는 입력을 프롬프트(prompt)라고 한다. 프롬프트 엔지니어: Input supplied to AI is called a prompt. Prompt engineering means designing and revising that input to obtain a desired output. Here, it refers to designing the instructions, examples, input structure, and output requirements through which a task is conveyed to a model. Selecting and organizing the full set of reference information, including files, documents, and tool outputs, is discussed as context engineering in §3.3.
생성형 AI가 코딩에 쓰이기 시작한 초기에는 사람이 질문하고 AI가 한: When generative AI first entered coding, the basic interaction was a person asking a question and AI answering once. How the question was written strongly affected the result. Techniques discovered then remain in use, but some have been absorbed into models while others remain human responsibilities.
입력 문장이 모델의 동작을 정하게 되다: Input text begins to determine model behavior
2020년 OpenAI 연구진은 1,750억 개의 매개변수를 가진 언어: In 2020, OpenAI researchers introduced GPT-3, a language model with 175 billion parameters, and demonstrated that input text alone could elicit different tasks without changing its weights. The paper described using a pretrained language model’s ‘text interface as a form of task specification’. Given instructions and a few examples, the model performs the task by predicting what follows. The authors called this in-context learning. <v0>Tom B. Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners</v0> (2020; §1, §2).
그전까지는 새 과제를 풀게 하려면 그 과제의 데이터로 모델을 추가 학습시: Previously, adapting a model to a new task generally involved fine-tuning: further training it on task-specific data. With GPT-3, changing the input could make the same model do different work. Just as code changes program behavior, input text could change model behavior. As input took on this role, discovering and organizing effective formulations became a research topic in its own right.
few-shot 프롬프팅은 과제의 입력과 출력 예시를 몇 개 먼저 보여: Few-shot prompting supplies a few example inputs and outputs before asking a model to process a new input in the same form. The GPT-3 paper compared zero-shot prompting without examples, one-shot prompting with one, and few-shot prompting with several. Few-shot settings typically included 10–100 examples, as many as would fit within the 2,048-token input limit. The model’s weights remain unchanged. <v0>Tom B. Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners</v0> (2020; §2).
코딩 작업에서도 같은 원리를 쓸 수 있다. 규칙을 말로 길게 설명하기 어: The same principle applies to coding. When a rule is difficult to describe at length, input-output pairs can guide AI toward code following their pattern. The following hypothetical example requests a function that extracts experimental conditions from filenames.
“v 뒤의 숫자는 속도, t 뒤의 숫자는 두께”라고 설명할 수도 있지만,: One could explain that digits after ‘v’ indicate velocity and those after ‘t’ indicate thickness, but two examples also convey separators, units, and data types. Unrepresentative examples can instead make AI treat incidental features as rules. If both thicknesses have one decimal place, it might produce code that cannot handle a filename containing two, such as ‘t1.25’.
chain-of-thought(사고의 사슬) 프롬프팅은 모델이 바로 답을: Chain-of-thought prompting asks a model to write intermediate reasoning steps before giving its answer. In 2022, Google researchers reported that supplying eight worked examples enabled a 540-billion-parameter model to achieve then-leading performance on GSM8K, an elementary-school mathematical word-problem benchmark. It outperformed GPT-3 fine-tuned on GSM8K and equipped with a separate verifier. <v0>Jason Wei et al., Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models</v0> (2022; abstract).
같은 해 도쿄대학교와 Google 연구진은 예시 없이 답 앞에 “Let’: That year, University of Tokyo and Google researchers reported a similar effect from adding only ‘Let’s think step by step’ before the answer, without examples. For InstructGPT (text-davinci-002), accuracy rose from 17.7% to 78.7% on MultiArith and from 10.4% to 40.7% on GSM8K. <v0>Takeshi Kojima et al., Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners</v0> (2022; abstract). These findings showed that one sentence could multiply performance, drawing attention to the search for effective wording.
코드를 요청할 때 chain-of-thought는 “먼저 처리 순서를 설: For code requests, chain-of-thought prompting might take the form ‘First explain the processing steps, then write the code.’ This reveals the proposed approach before the code, helping people assess its direction. If a numerical-integration explanation omits boundary conditions, for example, one can address that omission before reading dozens of lines. However, research also suggests that written reasoning need not faithfully describe what determined an answer. Adding answer-biasing cues changed model answers without those cues appearing in their explanations. <v0>Miles Turpin et al., Language Models Don’t Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting</v0> (2023; abstract). A plausible explanation does not establish correct code: use it to examine the approach and run the code separately to verify it.
코드 생성에서 프롬프트가 무엇을 담아야 하는지는 코드 생성 모델의 평가: Code-generation evaluation also illustrates what a code request needs to contain. When OpenAI introduced the code-trained Codex model in 2021, it released the HumanEval evaluation set. Each problem provides a function name, arguments, and a docstring describing its purpose; hidden tests score the generated function body. With one generated solution, Codex solved 28.8% of problems, compared with 0% for GPT-3 and 11.4% for the publicly available GPT-J under the same conditions. Generating 100 candidates per problem and accepting a problem if any candidate passed raised Codex’s score to 70.2%. <v0>Mark Chen et al., Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code</v0> (2021; abstract).
이 결과에서 두 가지를 읽을 수 있다. 첫째, 코드를 요청하는 프롬프트는: Two points follow. First, a code-generation prompt effectively specifies a function: its name, inputs, outputs, behavior, and examples. Second, the same prompt can produce different results, and tests are needed to select correct code. Prompt design and result verification were linked from the outset.
이 꼭지 첫머리의 요청을 이 관점에서 다시 써 보면 다음과 같다. 역시: Rewriting the opening request from this perspective gives the following, again hypothetical, example.
이 요청에는 입력 형식과 단위, 계산 방법, 사용할 라이브러리, 예외 처: This request specifies input format and units, calculation method, permitted libraries, exception handling, and output format. The final line uses chain-of-thought prompting to request an explanation before the code. Compared with the original, fewer decisions are left to AI. Choosing the elastic range as 0.0005–0.0025, however, depends on the material and test conditions. The person making the request must make such judgments.
두 요청의 차이를 항목별로 나누면 다음과 같다. 표의 항목은 저자가 위: The following table compares the requests element by element. The author derived these elements from the example; not every request needs all of them. A short, disposable script may need only a goal and defined inputs and outputs.

교점이 없으면 예외 발생: Raise an exception if no intersection is found

무엇을 보면 맞았다고 판단할지: What evidence will establish that the result is correct
마지막 행의 완료 기준은 위 요청에서도 빠져 있다. 예를 들어 “항복강도: The completion criterion in the last row is missing even from the more detailed request above. Adding a condition such as “When tested on a dataset with a known yield strength, the result must agree within 1%” establishes in advance how the person will check the output. For the AI, this condition clarifies the target; for the person, it defines a verification procedure. Even after prompting techniques became widely known, this remained something people had to supply. We will return to this point when examining recent guidance from model developers below.
GPT-3와 ChatGPT가 널리 쓰이면서 프롬프트 작성은 하나의 기술로: As GPT-3 and ChatGPT became widely used, writing prompts came to be regarded as a skill in its own right. On January 24, 2023, Andrej Karpathy wrote on X, formerly Twitter, “The hottest new programming language is English” <v0>Andrej Karpathy, X post (archived by Thread Reader)</v0> (published: 2023-01-24). The remark succinctly expressed the observation that natural-language instructions determine a model’s behavior much as a program does.
같은 시기 기업들은 이 일을 맡을 사람을 따로 뽑기 시작했다. 2023년: Around the same time, companies began hiring people specifically for this work. In March 2023, Fortune reported that Anthropic had advertised a “prompt engineer & librarian” position paying $175,000–335,000 a year. The role involved finding effective ways to get Anthropic’s model, Claude, to perform a range of tasks, documenting those methods, and building collections of tools and tutorials. The posting explained that prompt engineering was less than two years old, making suitable candidates difficult to find <v0/> (published: 2023-03-09).
기법도 빠르게 늘어났다. 2024년에 공개된 프롬프팅 기법 조사 논문은: The number of techniques also grew rapidly. A survey of prompting techniques released in 2024 organized 33 related terms and classified 58 text-prompting techniques and 40 techniques for other input modalities, including images and audio <v0>Sander Schulhoff et al., The Prompt Report: A Systematic Survey of Prompting Techniques</v0> (2024; abstract). The proliferation of dozens of techniques showed how active the field had become, while also making it harder for users to judge which technique would work in a particular situation.
2년 뒤의 분위기는 달랐다. Microsoft가 2025년 4월 발표한: Two years later, the mood had changed. Microsoft’s April 2025 Work Trend Index surveyed 31,000 knowledge workers across 31 markets and listed the AI-related roles that leaders were considering hiring for within the next 12–18 months. The leading roles included AI trainers (32%), AI data specialists (32%), and AI security specialists (31%); prompt engineer did not appear among the top 10 <v0/> (published: 2025-04-23). An article by Korn Ferry discussing the survey reported that prompt engineering ranked second from the bottom <v1/> (published: 2025-04-29). This can be understood as a decline in the need for a separate role devoted solely to prompting, rather than a disappearance of the need to write good prompts. It had become closer to a basic skill for anyone using AI.
직무의 위상이 달라진 데에는 모델의 변화도 있었다. 2024년 9월 Op: Changes in models also contributed to the shift in the role’s standing. When OpenAI announced its reasoning model o1 in September 2024, it explained that the model was trained through reinforcement learning to produce a long internal chain of thought before answering <v0/> (published: 2024-09-12). Models were beginning to perform on their own the step-by-step reasoning that users had previously elicited through prompts.
모델 개발사의 안내도 이 변화를 반영한다. OpenAI의 추론 모델 안내: Guidance from model developers reflects this change. OpenAI’s guidance for reasoning models explains that because these models already reason internally, prompts such as “think step by step” may fail to improve performance and can even interfere with it. It also recommends starting without examples, since few-shot examples are generally unnecessary. Yet the advice to state the end goal clearly and specify the conditions and constraints of a successful response remains <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-15; publication date not provided). Anthropic’s prompting guidance likewise emphasizes clear, direct instructions, reasons and context for those instructions, and 3–5 relevant, varied examples. It recommends using the model’s extended thinking capability for step-by-step reasoning, presenting manual chain-of-thought prompting as an alternative when that capability is turned off <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-15; publication date not provided).
두 문서를 함께 보면, 특정 문구로 모델의 능력을 끌어내던 기법은 모델: Read together, these documents suggest that techniques for eliciting a model’s capabilities through particular phrases are being absorbed into the models themselves. What remains for people is to decide what they want, which conditions must be met, and what evidence will count as success. In the yield-strength example, these decisions include the calculation method, elastic region, and exception-handling behavior specified by the person.
프롬프트만으로 해결되지 않은 문제: Problems that prompting alone did not solve
프롬프트를 잘 써도 결과를 믿을 수 있는 것은 아니었다. 첫째, 같은 내: Even a well-written prompt did not make the output trustworthy. First, small changes in format could produce large changes in results, even when the content of the prompt stayed the same. A 2023 study reported that several open-source models were sensitive to formatting changes unrelated to meaning, such as separators, spacing, and capitalization. For LLaMA-2-13B, changing only the format produced accuracy differences of up to 76 percentage points <v0>Melanie Sclar et al., Quantifying Language Models’ Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design</v0> (2023; abstract). A prompt that worked once was therefore not guaranteed to work with another model or in another setting.
둘째, 문법적으로 그럴듯한 코드도 실행하면 틀리거나 안전하지 않을 수 있: Second, code that looked syntactically plausible could still be incorrect or unsafe when executed. A security analysis of code generated by GitHub Copilot found vulnerabilities in approximately 40% of 1,689 programs generated across 89 scenarios <v0>Hammond Pearce et al., Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot’s Code Contributions</v0> (IEEE S&P 2022; abstract). In research and engineering, calculations that silently produce incorrect results are more dangerous than programs that stop with an error. The yield-strength function above will still output a number if it misinterprets the units. Without checking the result directly, that incorrect value can be used as it stands.
셋째, 질문하고 답을 받는 방식에서는 실행과 검증이 모두 사람의 몫이었다: Third, in a question-and-answer interaction, people remained responsible for both execution and verification. AI returned code as text, leaving the person to copy it, run it, and paste error messages back into the conversation. As the HumanEval results showed, generating multiple candidates and selecting them through tests could improve the success rate, but it was still a person who repeated that process in the chat interface.
이 문제들 때문에 관심은 “어떻게 질문할까”에서 “결과를 어떻게 실행하고: These problems shifted attention from “How should we ask?” to “How do we run, verify, and fix the result?” Section §3.2 covers agentic coding, in which AI reads files, executes code, checks errors, and makes corrections itself. Section §3.3 covers context engineering, which selects and organizes the information an agent will consult. Section §3.4 covers agreeing on specifications and plans before generating code. Prompts do not disappear in these approaches. Task instructions given to an agent, repository instruction files, and specification documents are all inputs to AI. The principles discussed in this section, clearly stating goals, conditions, examples, and completion criteria, carry over into all of them.
토론: 처음부터 자세히 설명할 것인가, 대화하며 고칠 것인가: Discussion: explain everything at the start, or refine it through conversation?
앞의 항복강도 예시는 필요한 조건을 처음부터 모두 적은 요청이었다. 실제: The yield-strength example above specified all the necessary conditions from the outset. In practice, not everyone requests code from AI this way. Many people begin with a short request, inspect the result, and refine it through conversation. We made this question a discussion topic for the course’s midterm presentations and asked the Chapter 3 authors and other students how they make requests.
<v0>수강생 A</v0> “잘 모르는 코드는 함수 단위로 먼저 받아 보: <v0>Student A</v0> “For code I’m unfamiliar with, I first ask for individual functions, then gradually develop a plan. For code I know well, I tend to make a detailed request from the start, including even straightforward decisions about code structure.”
<v0>수강생 B</v0> “저는 먼저 전체 흐름을 설명하고, 이후에 대: <v0>Student B</v0> “I think I usually explain the overall flow first and then revise things through conversation.”
<v0>수강생 C</v0> “최대한 자세히 설명하고, 설정값이 필요한 경: <v0>Student C</v0> “I tend to explain as much as possible and ask the AI to tell me when it needs configuration values.”
<v0>수강생 D</v0> “저는 간단하게 설명하고 디테일을 잡아 가는: <v0>Student D</v0> “I usually start with a brief explanation and work out the details as I go. I mainly build the code through conversation, asking for suggestions.”
<v0>수강생 E</v0> “업무와 관련된 요청은 처음부터 자세하게 프롬: <v0>Student E</v0> “For work-related requests, I try to give detailed prompts from the outset. Sometimes I use another AI to help write those prompts. I want to prevent the AI from filling gaps in unclear instructions with its own guesses.”
(Comments from the Group 3 authors and other students were collected in November 2026 and lightly edited for readability.)
The five comments differ in how much detail they provide at the start, but they also share common ground. Even someone who writes detailed instructions asks the AI to request unknown configuration values (C), while someone who starts briefly still explains the overall flow first (B). E uses another AI to help write the detailed request itself, specifically to prevent uncertain instructions from being filled in with guesses. This is the same problem noted at the beginning of this section: a request with missing information forces the AI to make many assumptions. A switches between the two approaches depending on the task. The distinction has more to do with how well the person understands the task than with personal preference. For familiar work, people can specify inputs, outputs, methods, and completion criteria in advance. For unfamiliar work, they may not yet know what to specify, so they need to discover the conditions by considering the AI’s suggestions.
Research suggests that distributing conditions across a conversation comes at a cost. Laban and colleagues designed an experiment in which information that could be provided in a single request was split into fragments and delivered one per conversational turn. Across more than 200,000 simulated conversations with 15 models, performance on six generation tasks, including code generation, was on average 39% lower when information was distributed across turns than when it was provided all at once. The authors attributed the decline less to a small reduction in the models’ underlying ability than to a large increase in unreliability, with results varying widely under the same conditions. Lowering model temperature did little to reduce this conversational unreliability <v0>Philippe Laban et al., LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation</v0> (2025; abstract, §5, §7.2). However, the experiment used simulated users delivering predetermined information fragments in sequence. It cannot be treated as equivalent to real people revising their requirements in response to results.
논문은 사용자를 위한 대응도 제안한다. 대화가 엇나가면 그 대화를 계속: The paper also offers advice for users. When a conversation goes off track, start a new one instead of continuing to repair the old one. Ask the model to summarize the requirements stated so far, then use that summary as the first request in the new conversation <v0>Philippe Laban et al., LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation</v0> (2025; §7.4).
Considering the students’ experiences alongside this research, the author proposes using the two approaches at different stages of a task, rather than choosing only one. When you do not yet know what to build, start briefly and explore through conversation. Once the conditions become clear, consolidate them into a single request organized by goals, inputs and outputs, methods, and completion criteria, as in the table above. Turning conditions discovered through conversation back into a specification connects to the approach of agreeing on specifications and plans before generating code (§3.4). Section §3.4 revisits the same question as “How far should exploration go, and what should be agreed upon in a specification first?”

수강생들은 AI에게 코드를 어떻게 요청하는가: How students ask AI to write code
2022년의 AI는 코드를 작성할 수는 있었지만 실행할 수는 없었다. 따: In 2022, AI could write code but could not execute it. People therefore had to run the code and relay errors back to the AI. By 2025, given a goal, AI could execute and revise code on its own. The human role shifted toward reviewing the results and deciding whether further work was needed. This change came with the emergence of agentic coding. This section examines, in turn, the technical developments that made the change possible, the current performance of agents, and developers’ responses.
에이전틱 코딩이란 AI가 할당받은 목표를 이룰 때까지 도구를 쓰며 결과에: Agentic coding is an approach in which AI uses tools to work toward an assigned goal until it reaches a result. Simon Willison, a co-creator of the Django web framework (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-13)), defines an agent as follows: “An LLM agent runs tools in a loop to achieve a goal.” His definition highlights the current role of an agent: given a goal, AI repeatedly uses tools and works toward the result on its own (<v1/> (published: 2025-09-18)). Anthropic argues that we should distinguish workflows, which call models and tools in a predefined sequence, from agents, in which the model itself selects the tools for its next action (<v2/> (published: 2024-12-19)). In other words, even systems using the same AI should be understood differently depending on whether they choose their own next actions. Following this distinction, this section calls the period before agentic coding the conversation stage and the period after its emergence the agent stage.
2022년 11월 ChatGPT가 공개되면서 채팅 창에서 AI에게 코드를: After ChatGPT was released in November 2022, getting code from AI through a chat interface spread rapidly. Steve Yegge, then a developer at Sourcegraph, called this approach chat-oriented programming, or CHOP, describing it as “coding via iterative prompt refinement” (<v0/> (published: 2024-06-24)). This description of obtaining the desired code by refining prompts shows how much better results in early AI coding depended on people revising their instructions.
이 방식에서 AI는 자기가 쓴 코드가 실제로 어떻게 돌아가는지 알 수 없: In this approach, AI could not see how its own code actually behaved. People had to transfer both the code and its execution results. For AI to take over this work, observing execution results and making revisions itself, four things had to change together.
첫 번째는 AI의 출력이다. 2023년 6월 OpenAI는 모델이 미리: The first was AI’s output. In June 2023, OpenAI introduced a capability through which a model could output a function call in a predefined format for a program to execute (<v0/> (published: 2023-06-13)). In May 2024, Anthropic also made Claude’s tool-use capability generally available (<v1/> (published: 2024-05-30)). With this capability, an AI response could become a command that a program executed directly, rather than remaining text for a person to read. Section §8.3 explains how tool calls work internally.
두 번째는 한 번에 다룰 수 있는 정보의 양이다. 2020년의 GPT-3: The second was the amount of information a model could handle at once. In 2020, GPT-3 could accept only 2,048 tokens of input at a time (<v0>Brown et al., Language models are few-shot learners</v0> (NeurIPS 2020, Section 2.1)). By 2023–2024, models accepting 200,000 to one million tokens had appeared (<v1/> (published: 2023-11-21); <v2/> (published: 2024-02-15)). AI could now inspect large files and logs together. Section §3.3 discusses how to select useful information from this input.
세 번째는 AI가 일하는 작업 환경이다. 2024년 3월 Cognitio: The third was the working environment provided to AI. In March 2024, Cognition introduced Devin, an AI equipped with tools (<v0/> (published: 2024-03-12)). That same year, researchers at Princeton and Stanford built SWE-agent and made tools easier for AI to use: a file-viewing command displayed 100 lines at a time rather than entire files, and an editing command reverted changes that introduced syntax errors (<v1>Yang et al., SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering</v1> (NeurIPS 2024)). Anthropic likewise reported that, when building an agent, “we actually spent more time optimizing our tools than the overall prompt,” suggesting that agent performance depends as much on the tools provided as on the prompt (<v2/> (published: 2024-12-19)).
네 번째는 모델을 훈련하는 방식이다. 2025년 5월 OpenAI는 실제: The fourth was model training. In May 2025, OpenAI released codex-1, trained through reinforcement learning that rewarded successful performance on real coding tasks (<v0/> (published: 2025-05-16)). Producing a plausible answer was no longer enough: success meant passing tests.
이러한 변화들은 2025년에 제품으로 나타났다. Anthropic은 20: These developments took the form of products in 2025. Anthropic introduced Claude Code, which operates in a computer terminal, in February 2025 (<v0/> (published: 2025-02-24)). In May of that year, OpenAI released Codex (<v1/> (published: 2025-05-16)), and GitHub released its Copilot coding agent (<v2/> (published: 2025-05-19)). The agent stage thus began in research in 2024 and became established through products in 2025.
에이전트가 실제로 얼마나 일을 잘하는지 잴 때 많이 쓰는 시험이 SWE-: SWE-bench is a widely used test of how well agents perform practical work. It presents AI with 2,294 real bug reports from 12 open-source Python projects and scores the proportion it resolves. When the benchmark was first released in 2023, the best-performing model, Claude 2, resolved 1.96% of the issues (<v0>Jimenez et al., SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?</v0> (ICLR 2024)).
2024년 3월 Cognition은 Devin이 SWE-bench에서 1: In March 2024, Cognition reported that Devin achieved a 13.86% resolution rate on SWE-bench (<v0/> (published: 2024-03-12)). However, this result was measured on a randomly selected 25% of the full set of 2,294 issues. Since Devin’s underlying model was not disclosed, it is difficult to determine whether the difference came from the model or the tools. Later, Answer.AI assigned Devin 20 real tasks over a month, of which it completed only three (<v1/> (published: 2025-01-08)). This showed that published scores can differ from performance on actual work.
도구의 효과는 모델을 고정한 비교에서 더 분명하게 드러난다. 앞서 본 S: The effect of tools is clearer in comparisons that hold the model constant. The SWE-agent study discussed above used GPT-4 Turbo to attempt all 2,294 SWE-bench issues. The resolution rate changed from 1.31% without the tools to 12.47% with them (<v0>Yang et al., SWE-agent</v0> (NeurIPS 2024, Table 1)). With the same model, different tools produced a nearly tenfold difference in results.
이후 SWE-bench 점수는 빠르게 올랐다. 2024년 8월 OpenA: SWE-bench scores subsequently rose rapidly. In August 2024, OpenAI released SWE-bench Verified after 93 Python developers reviewed the original benchmark to filter out issues with ambiguous descriptions or tests that rejected correct fixes (<v0/> (published: 2024-08-13)). According to Vals.ai, the highest score on this test in September 2026 was 97.0% (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-13; update dated 2026-09-01; model: Claude Opus 5; execution environment: mini-SWE-agent)). Yet OpenAI had already stopped reporting this score in February 2026. Because the issues came from public repositories, newer models could reproduce the solution code verbatim. A review of issues that models failed unusually often also found defects in many of the tests (<v2/> (published: 2026-02-23)). When even the benchmark’s creators question its reliability, high scores alone become insufficient evidence of capability.
이처럼 SWE-bench 점수만으로는 기준이 모호하기 때문에, 에이전트의: Because SWE-bench scores alone provide an uncertain standard, other ways to measure agent progress have emerged. METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research), an AI evaluation organization (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-13)), asks AI agents to solve 228 tasks without human assistance. It measures how long a task with a 50% AI success rate would take a human expert (<v1/> (published: 2026-01-29)). The human baseline is the time taken by an expert with approximately five years of experience encountering the task for the first time (<v2>Kwa et al., Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks</v2> (Sections 2.2 and 3.1)). According to METR, this time horizon grew from roughly four minutes for GPT-4 in 2023 to roughly 12 hours for Claude Opus 4.6 in February 2026 (<v3/> (accessed: 2026-11-13; benchmark version: Time Horizon 1.1)). Since 2024, it has doubled approximately every 89 days (<v4/> (published: 2026-01-29)). However, fewer human measurements are available for longer tasks, and METR states that estimates beyond 16 hours are less reliable. These figures are therefore better understood as evidence of the rapid growth in the length of tasks agents can handle than as precise values.
성능은 빠르게 좋아졌지만, 개발자들은 아직 AI의 결과를 그대로 믿지 않: Although performance has improved rapidly, developers still do not accept AI output at face value. In the Stack Overflow 2025 Developer Survey, 32.7% of respondents trusted AI output (3.1% highly trusted it and 29.6% somewhat trusted it), while a larger 45.7% distrusted it (26.1% somewhat distrusted it and 19.6% highly distrusted it). The most frequently cited frustration, selected by 66.0%, was “AI solutions that are almost right, but not quite” (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-13)). This frustration helps explain why people cannot delegate entire tasks to AI and must ultimately assess the results themselves. Section §9.1 examines types of incorrect output.
AI 에이전트에게 일을 얼마나 맡길 수 있는지는 Anthropic 내부: An internal Anthropic survey offers an indication of how much work can be delegated to AI agents. When Anthropic surveyed 132 of its engineers and researchers, they reported using Claude for approximately 60% of their work but being able to delegate only 0–20% of it completely. They primarily delegated tasks whose results were easy to check or whose failure would cause little harm (<v0/> (published: 2025-12-02)). Even those who build agents at close quarters fully delegate only work whose results they can readily verify.
에이전틱 코딩의 등장으로 AI는 실행 결과를 직접 보고 고칠 수 있게 됐: With the emergence of agentic coding, AI became able to inspect execution results and make corrections itself. People intervene less at each individual step, but they still decide what to delegate, assess whether the returned result is correct, and determine whether to request further work. Sections §3.3 and §3.4 discuss how to describe delegated tasks, while Chapter 10 covers tests and verification methods that support these judgments.
