대학원생 한 명이 연구실 공용 장비의 예약 도구를 만든다고 하자. 설명을: Suppose a graduate student is building a booking tool for shared laboratory equipment. This is a hypothetical example for illustration, not a report of an actual implementation. Until now, people have booked equipment by writing their names on a whiteboard beside it; the student wants to move this process to a web page. Asking an AI coding tool to “Build a lab equipment booking page” produces a page with an equipment list, a timetable, and a booking button. Clicking the button even creates a booking. But several things were left unspecified. What happens if two people book the same time slot? How many hours can one booking last? Who can cancel someone else’s booking? The person making the request decided none of these. The generated code nevertheless behaves in some way in all three cases, and the AI chose that behavior.
사용자는 페이지를 써 보다가 겹친 예약을 발견하고 “같은 시간에는 한 명: While using the page, the user discovers overlapping bookings and asks, “Allow only one person to book the same time slot.” A few days later, a booking that occupies equipment all day prompts another request for a time limit. The cycle of inspecting results and revising requests continues. Section 2.4 defined vibe coding in the narrow sense as repeatedly making requests based on execution results without reading the generated code. This section uses the term in the same sense.
이 반복을 줄이려는 방식이 스펙 주도 개발(spec-driven deve: Spec-driven development (SDD) seeks to reduce this repetition. In this section, SDD means documenting what to build before generating code, having a person review and agree on that document, and then asking AI to implement it. This document is a specification, referred to below as a spec. A spec describes the features to build and why they are needed, the rules to follow, and the conditions for determining completion. A plan describes the structure and sequence for implementing the spec. Specifications and plans have a cost. Even when AI writes a draft, someone must spend time reading and revising it. This section asks when that cost is worthwhile.
빠르게 만든 코드에 남는 불확실성: Uncertainty left in quickly generated code
요청에 빠진 내용이 있을 때 코드 생성 모델이 되묻지 않고 코드를 만드는: Several experiments have reported that code-generation models tend to generate code without asking follow-up questions when requests omit information. Wu and Fard took 164 problems from HumanEval, a code-generation benchmark, and modified them to make descriptions ambiguous, contradictory, or incomplete. Although these modified problems required clarification to produce correct code, more than 60% of model responses generated code without asking questions. The proportion of first-generated solutions that passed the tests (Pass@1) was generally 35–52% lower than for the original problems. These figures are relative decreases from the original pass rates (<v0>Jie JW Wu and Fatemeh H. Fard, HumanEvalComm: Benchmarking the Communication Competence of Code Generation for LLMs and LLM Agent</v0> (published in ACM TOSEM; arXiv version 3 posted: 2025-01-27)).
저장소의 이슈(issue, 버그나 개선 요청을 기록한 항목)를 해결하는: The same tendency has been reported in coding agents that resolve repository issues, entries recording bugs or requests for improvements. Vijayvargiya and colleagues removed information needed to solve tasks from SWE-bench Verified, a benchmark based on issues from real open-source repositories, and gave the modified tasks to agents. Unless explicitly encouraged, the models proceeded without asking the user. When questions were permitted, performance was up to 74% higher than when they were not (<v0>Sanidhya Vijayvargiya et al., Ambig-SWE: Interactive Agents to Overcome Underspecificity in Software Engineering</v0> (accepted at ICLR 2026; arXiv version 3 posted: 2026-02-21)). In both studies, researchers deliberately removed the information; in Ambig-SWE, a simulated user answered the questions. These findings do not establish how often real requests are incomplete. What they do show is a tendency for models to fill missing information with guesses rather than flagging the gap.
사람 쪽에서 일어나는 일은 바이브 코딩 영상을 분석한 연구에 기록되어 있: A study analyzing vibe-coding videos documents what happens on the human side. Chou and colleagues analyzed 20 videos. Some participants wrote detailed requirements before starting, but many developed new requirements after seeing the output. Two participants with limited technical backgrounds who relied heavily on AI spent nearly 40% of their prompts repeating the same requests or pasting error messages back without explanation (<v0>Yi-Hung Chou et al., Building Software by Rolling the Dice: A Qualitative Study of Vibe Coding</v0> (accepted at ESEC/FSE 2026; arXiv version 2 posted: 2025-12-30)). As this was a qualitative study of 20 videos, the proportion cannot be generalized to vibe coding as a whole. Section 3.1 discussed experimental findings that model performance falls when conditions are distributed across multiple conversational turns.
이 결과들을 예약 도구에 비추어 보면, 빠르게 만든 코드에 남는 불확실성: Applied to the booking tool, these findings suggest two kinds of uncertainty left in quickly generated code. First, the code contains decisions that no person has made. No one decided whether overlapping bookings should be allowed, but the code either permits or blocks them. Section 3.5 describes this same phenomenon as unmade decisions becoming fixed in code. Second, there is no criterion for determining completion. The request “Build a booking page” does not establish whether the returned page is finished; the user discovers problems only when unusual behavior becomes noticeable during use. This division into two kinds of uncertainty is this section’s synthesis, not a classification from the studies above.
Spec과 계획을 먼저 쓰는 방식의 등장: The emergence of specifications and plans before code
이 절이 확인한 자료 가운데 이른 것은 개인이 공유한 작업 요령이다. H: Among the sources examined for this section, an early example was a workflow shared by an individual developer. In February 2025, Harper Reed published his process: use a question-and-answer conversation with AI to organize an idea into <v0/>, derive a step-by-step prompt plan (<v1/>) and checklist (<v2/>) from that spec, and then generate code (<v3/> (published: 2025-02-16)). In April of the same year, Anthropic’s Claude Code best practices introduced the sequence of exploration, planning, coding, and committing, meaning recording changes in the repository’s history. It noted that without the first two stages, Claude tended to jump straight into coding a solution (<v4/> (published: 2025-04-18; the original article was later revised, so this was checked against an archived copy dated 2025-05-02)).
In the second half of 2025, tools incorporating this sequence into their procedures appeared one after another. Kiro, introduced in July, is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) with a specification-writing process. Its introduction highlighted problems that remain after repeated prompting produces a working app: users do not know what assumptions the model made, decisions made along the way are not documented, and vague requirements make it impossible to judge whether the app meets them (<v0>Nikhil Swaminathan and Deepak Singh, Introducing Kiro</v0> (published: 2025-07-14)). In September, GitHub introduced the open-source tool Spec Kit. Its announcement described explaining a goal and receiving a block of code as useful for quick prototypes but less dependable for important applications or work in an existing codebase (<v1/> (published: 2025-09-02)). On September 6 of the same month, the open-source tool OpenSpec made its first public release (<v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-16)).
문서를 여러 벌 남기지 않고 계획만 먼저 확인하는 가벼운 형태도 일반 코: A lighter approach, reviewing a plan first without producing multiple documents, also appeared in general coding tools. Cursor added Plan Mode in version 1.7, released on September 29, 2025 (<v0/> (published: 2025-09-29)). In Claude Code’s plan mode, Claude only investigates and writes a plan; file changes are blocked in principle until the user approves it (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-16; the documentation provides neither a publication date nor a product version)). This section calls this a plan-first workflow. It is lighter than SDD because it does not retain a separate spec, but shares the principle of having a person review a document before reviewing code.
SDD라는 말의 뜻은 아직 하나로 정해지지 않았다. Thoughtwork: The meaning of SDD has not yet settled. In its November 2025 Technology Radar, Thoughtworks placed SDD in the “Assess” category, for technologies whose organizational impact is worth investigating, noting that the term’s definition was still evolving (<v0/> (published: 2025-11-05)). Böckeler divided approaches called SDD into three levels: spec-first, where a spec is written before work begins; spec-anchored, where the spec is retained after the work and used for maintenance; and spec-as-source, where people edit only the spec and do not directly modify the code (<v1/> (published: 2025-10-15)). This section addresses the first level: writing and agreeing on a spec before generating code.
요구사항을 문서로 먼저 적는 일 자체는 새롭지 않다. AI 코딩 도구의: Writing requirements before implementation is not itself new. What differs in SDD with AI coding tools is that AI usually drafts the spec and also reads and implements it. The Spec Kit introduction explains that people primarily set the direction, while the coding agent writes most of the text. Section 6.1 covers how to structure requirements, and Section 12.1 discusses using specs alongside agile development and test-driven development.
Kiro, Spec Kit, OpenSpec은 Spec을 저장소 안의 M: Kiro, Spec Kit, and OpenSpec all retain specs as Markdown files in the repository. They differ in how they divide the documents and where people review them. The table below reflects their official documentation as checked on November 16, 2026. The latest versions at that time were Kiro IDE 1.4.178, Spec Kit 1.4.0, and OpenSpec 2.0.0. This is not a comparison based on running the three tools on the same task.

기존 시스템 전체를 Spec으로 다시 적지 않고, 저장소에 설치한 뒤 다: Install it in the repository and apply it from the next change onward, without rewriting the entire existing system as a spec
변경분만 적은 Spec을 쓰고, 작업을 마쳐 archive하면 프로젝트의: Write a spec covering only the changes; after completing and archiving the work, merge it into the project’s baseline spec
각 열의 출처는 차례로 다음과 같다. Kiro는 <v0/> (수정: 20: The sources for each column are as follows. For Kiro: <v0/> (updated: 2026-11-12), <v1/>, <v2/>, and <v3/>. For Spec Kit: <v4/> and <v5/>. For OpenSpec: <v6/> and <v7/>. All documents without a separately stated date were accessed on 2026-11-16.
세 도구 모두 공개 뒤에 절차가 달라졌다. Spec Kit의 현재 문서에: All three tools have changed their procedures since release. Spec Kit’s current documentation includes commands such as clarify and converge that were absent from the four stages in its introduction (Specify, Plan, Tasks, Implement). Kiro’s current documentation includes Quick Spec and Plan mode, neither of which appeared in its introduction. OpenSpec changed its command system in versions 1.0.0 (2026-01-26) and 2.0.0 (2026-11-11) (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-16)). The command names and stages in the table reflect the documentation as of the access date.
세 도구는 무엇을 만들지(요구사항), 어떻게 만들지(설계나 계획), 어떤: All three tools separate what to build (requirements), how to build it (design or plan), and the order of work (task list) into different documents, which people review before reviewing code. The Spec Kit introduction states that the human role includes verification as well as setting direction. Their requirements formats are also similar. Kiro uses EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax), following the pattern “WHEN [condition or event] THE SYSTEM SHALL [expected behavior].” Kiro’s documentation explains that requirements in this form can be translated directly into test cases (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-16)). OpenSpec likewise attaches WHEN/THEN scenarios to each requirement. By pairing conditions with expected behavior, both formats provide a way to document the completion criteria identified as missing earlier.
세 도구의 문서는 Spec 절차가 맞지 않는 경우도 직접 적고 있다. K: The documentation for all three tools also explicitly describes situations where a specification process is unsuitable. Kiro states that Feature Specs are unsuitable for exploratory coding without a clear goal and advises skipping planning for quick, familiar changes. Spec Kit provides a shorter path for small features. OpenSpec places explore before propose for situations where users do not yet know what to build, and states that creating specs for an entire existing codebase from scratch is a waste of time (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-16)). Even the tool developers do not recommend the full specification process for every task.
Spec이 값을 하는 경우와 탐색이 더 나은 경우: When specifications pay off, and when exploration is better
Spec의 초안은 대개 AI가 쓰므로, 사람이 치르는 비용의 큰 부분은: Because AI usually drafts the spec, much of the human cost is the time spent reading and revising generated documents. Böckeler reported that when she assigned Kiro a small bug fix, the requirements document expanded to four user stories, requirements written from a user’s perspective, and 16 acceptance criteria, conditions for determining whether those requirements were met. She likened this to using a sledgehammer to crack a nut and wrote that she would rather review code than multiple Markdown files (<v0/> (published: 2025-10-15)). Colin Eberhardt documented reimplementing a feature in a hobby app using Spec Kit. By the first implementation, it had produced 689 lines of code and 2,577 lines of Markdown, taking 3.5 hours to review. He estimated that working without SDD was about ten times faster, while acknowledging that he might be using the tool incorrectly (<v1/> (published: 2025-11-26)). Each article records one person’s experience with the tools as they existed in October or November 2025.
실제 사용자들은 작업에 따라 SDD를 골라 썼다. Agarwal 등은 R: Actual users applied SDD selectively according to the task. Agarwal and colleagues jointly analyzed Reddit discussions, interviews with 21 practitioners, and spec files from 266 public repositories. Most practitioners used SDD selectively, and only a minority used it for every task. They skipped SDD for small tasks, bug fixes, one-off scripts, and prototypes, deciding primarily on the basis of task size or complexity. Some used the cost of failure as their criterion, recommending SDD for high-stakes tasks with clear intent. Some participants built prototypes first when their ideas were still vague. On costs, the authors concluded that SDD shifts token consumption, time, and cognitive effort from implementation to planning; tokens are units of text processed by a model (<v0>Shyam Agarwal et al., Spec-Driven Development as Prescribed and as Practiced</v0> (version 4 posted: 2026-10-15)). This paper is a preprint available on arXiv.
Spec이 결과를 얼마나 개선하는지에 대한 근거는 아직 약하다. 같은 연: Evidence for how much specs improve results remains weak. In the same study, most practitioners felt that specs made agent work more reliable, but could not separate this effect from improvements in models over the same period. One team cited in the study wrote on Reddit that SDD used two to three times as many tokens and roughly twice as much time as direct prompting, and that even after several months they could not demonstrate an improvement in code quality. The authors likewise stated that the study established associations, not causal effects.
Hill은 오픈소스 저장소 119개의 풀 리퀘스트(pull request: Hill analyzed 88,052 pull requests, requests to incorporate changes into a repository, from 119 open-source repositories. Comparing pull requests with specification artifacts against those without them, the study found no support for any of five hypotheses, including that specifications reduce defects and rework (<v0/> (ESEM 2026, LIPIcs volume 394, 84:1–84:20)). However, 97.5% of what the study classified as specification artifacts were references to issues or tickets, and the sample contained no specs generated by SDD tools and committed to a repository. These results therefore do not directly measure the effectiveness of SDD tools. Within the scope of this section’s investigation, no study was found that compared the time spent writing specs with the resulting reduction in revision time on the same task (checked: 2026-11-16).
Spec을 먼저 쓰는 절차가 요구사항과 설계를 모두 확정한 뒤에 구현하는: Critics also argue that writing specs first is a return to waterfall development, in which requirements and design are finalized before implementation (<v0/> (published: 2025-11-12)). AWS engineer Marc Brooker counters that an SDD spec is a version-controlled document that continues to evolve, rather than one finalized at the beginning and then left untouched (<v1/> (published: 2026-04-09)).
이 자료들을 바탕으로 Spec이 값을 하는 경우와 탐색이 더 나은 경우를: Based on these sources, the following table distinguishes cases where specs are worthwhile from those where exploration is better. This is this section’s synthesis, not a measurement of effects under each condition.
요구사항이 복잡하거나 재사용, 협업이 필요할 때: Requirements are complex, or reuse or collaboration is needed
문제 자체가 불명확해 실험이 필요할 때: The problem itself is unclear and requires experimentation
여러 사람이나 에이전트가 같은 목표를 공유해야 할 때: Multiple people or agents need to share the same goal
한 번 쓰고 버릴 일회성 스크립트일 때: The work is a disposable, one-off script
완료 조건을 객관적으로 판정해야 할 때: Completion conditions must be assessed objectively
Spec을 쓰는 비용이 그것으로 얻는 확실성보다 클 때: The cost of writing the spec exceeds the certainty it provides
왼쪽 열의 조건은 도구들이 내세운 문제의식과 겹친다. Kiro 문서는 F: The conditions in the left column overlap with the problems the tools aim to address. Kiro lists complex features requiring structured planning and projects requiring documentation for team collaboration as suitable for Feature Specs. OpenSpec states that AI coding tool results are hard to predict when requirements exist only in conversation history. Because that history remains tied to the person and session involved, a document is needed for another person or agent to work toward the same goal. Assessing completion conditions is also why Kiro and OpenSpec require conditions to be paired with expected behavior. The right column overlaps with tasks for which practitioners in Agarwal and colleagues’ study skipped SDD. Piskala likewise argues that the effort put into specs is discarded along with throwaway prototypes, and that writing a spec before knowing what to build constrains learning during exploratory coding (<v0/> (published: 2026-01-30)). This paper is a practical guide and presents no original measurements.
오른쪽 열의 마지막 조건은 나머지와 성격이 다르다. 비용과 확실성을 견주: The last condition in the right column differs from the others. Comparing cost and certainty requires being able to estimate both, yet, as noted above, no study has measured them directly. The available basis for estimation is the criteria practitioners actually use: task size, the consequences of being wrong, and how clearly the intent is defined.
탐색은 어디까지 하고, 무엇부터 Spec으로 합의할 것인가: How far to explore, and what to agree upon in a specification first
앞 표의 두 열은 한 프로젝트 안에 함께 있다. 예약 도구에는 화면 구성: Both columns of the preceding table can apply within a single project. The booking tool combines elements that can be judged only after building them, such as the page layout, with elements that should be decided in advance, such as booking-conflict rules. A more practical question than choosing between vibe coding and SDD is therefore how far to explore and what to agree upon in a spec first. Section 3.1 passed the same question to this section when describing how to consolidate conditions discovered through conversation. The criteria below are this section’s proposal.
예약 도구의 첫 단계는 탐색이다. 만드는 사람 혼자 쓰는 프로토타입이고,: The booking tool begins with exploration. It is a prototype used only by its creator, and it is difficult to decide whether a weekly or daily timetable is better without seeing the page. Writing a spec at this point would mean filling unknowns with guesses. The nature of revision requests signals when to stop exploring. “Move the button to the top” may arise only after seeing the result. “Allow only one person to book the same time slot” is a rule that could have been established beforehand. When requests of the latter kind begin to appear, it is time to put those rules into a spec. The signal proposed in Section 3.5, whether a completion condition can be stated in a single sentence, can support the same judgment.
연구실 구성원 모두가 이 도구를 쓰기로 하면 Spec으로 합의할 대상이: Once all lab members decide to use the tool, there are matters to agree upon in a spec. To determine what to document first, apply the left column of the table to each decision. Add the cost of failure, a criterion used by some practitioners in Agarwal and colleagues’ study. Everyone must understand the booking-conflict rule in the same way, compliance must be objectively assessable, and a mistake could leave two people standing at the same equipment at the same time. Cancellation permissions and maximum booking duration meet the same criteria. Page colors and layout meet none of them, so they remain open to exploration.
다음은 이 규칙들을 적은 Spec의 가상 예시다. 완료 조건은 앞에서 본: The following is a hypothetical spec documenting these rules. Completion conditions pair conditions with expected behavior, as in the EARS notation discussed above. This document was not generated by a particular tool, nor has an implementation been carried out using it.
이 Spec은 스무 줄이 되지 않는다. 도입에서 AI가 대신 정했던 세: This spec is fewer than 20 lines long. It replaces the three decisions made by AI in the introduction with decisions made by a person and specifies conditions for checking compliance with each rule. Details of the interface are deliberately excluded. Piskala recommends writing a spec only to the minimum level needed to remove ambiguity in one’s situation; the example above applies that recommendation to the booking tool.
탐색에서 Spec으로 넘어가는 경로는 도구에도 있다. Kiro 문서에 따: Tools also offer a path from exploration to a spec. According to Kiro’s documentation, users can hold a free-form vibe session and then request spec generation; requirements are created from that conversation’s context (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-16)). OpenSpec guides users to begin with explore when they do not yet know what to build and move to propose once they decide. Nor must users fill in a blank spec alone. With Spec Kit’s clarify command and Kiro’s Plan mode, AI asks questions and people answer. Some participants in Agarwal and colleagues’ study said that answering an agent’s questions and revising its draft helped clarify their own intentions.
이 기준의 한계는 근거의 종류에 있다. 이 절이 조사한 범위에서는 Spe: The limitation of these criteria lies in the type of evidence supporting them. Within the scope of this section’s investigation, no experiment was found comparing work with and without specs on the same task. The criteria above are interpretations drawn from practitioner studies, individual accounts, and tool documentation. The booking tool is also hypothetical, so it does not demonstrate that using a spec actually reduced the number of revisions.
Spec을 쓸지는 프로젝트 전체가 아닌 개별 결정마다 따로 판단할 수 있: Whether to write a spec can be decided for individual decisions rather than for an entire project. Use exploration to decide what can only be understood by building it. For decisions that must be shared, require objective completion judgments, or carry a high cost of failure, document and agree on them in a spec before writing code. Section 6.1 covers structuring requirements into goals, constraints, and completion criteria, while Section 10.1 explains how to turn completion conditions into tests. The next section, 3.5, examines which forms of tools to use for the work defined this way.

프로그램을 만드는 작업에서는 결과물을 실행해 보면 원하는 동작을 하는지: When developing a program, running the result generally reveals whether it behaves as intended. In the work covered by this section, the outputs are numbers and conclusions. Give a table or database to an AI agent and ask it to explore, clean, and visualize the data, and graphs and interpretations can come back within minutes. But successful execution does not mean that the conclusion is correct. An incorrect aggregation can run without errors, and an incorrect graph can still be drawn.
이 절의 질문은 두 가지다. AI가 낸 분석을 믿으려면 무엇을 확인해야: This section asks two questions: what must we check to trust an AI-generated analysis, and what must we retain to reach the same conclusion again later? Here, reproducibility means that applying the same procedure to the same inputs yields the same results, and that someone else can verify this.
범위는 표와 데이터베이스를 다루는 분석으로 한정한다. 물리 모형이나 몬테: The scope is limited to analyses involving tables and databases. It does not cover simulations using physical models or Monte Carlo methods. However, the need to record seeds for steps that involve randomness also applies to general data analysis, so it is discussed below. Evaluation of autonomous research systems themselves is left to Section 18.5.
실행에 성공한 분석도 틀릴 수 있다: An analysis that runs successfully can still be wrong
AI가 생성한 분석 코드는 문법 오류 없이 실행되면서도 사용자가 물은 것: AI-generated analysis code can run without syntax errors yet calculate a value different from what the user asked for. The following example was created to explain this point. In response to the question, 'How many products were returned?', counting rows in the return records, counting distinct product types, and summing the quantities returned all produce a single number. The output number alone gives no way to distinguish which of the three was calculated.
Gu 등은 전문 분석가 22명이 AI가 보조한 분석을 검증하는 과정을 관: Gu and colleagues observed 22 professional analysts verifying AI-assisted analyses and reported two approaches to verification. One is procedure-oriented: following what the AI did through explanations and code. The other is data-oriented: checking whether the resulting data make sense in light of common sense and domain knowledge. When analysts noticed something unusual, they shifted from procedures to data. Even participants unfamiliar with Python continued verifying the analysis by translating it into a familiar data-manipulation language or by examining intermediate tables alone <v0/>. Participants in this study verified analyses prepared in advance by the researchers rather than instructing the AI directly, so the conditions differ from developing an analysis by writing prompts.
검증을 돕는 방향으로 도구를 바꾼 연구도 있다. Kazemitabaar: Other studies have redesigned tools to support verification. In a formative study of 15 participants, Kazemitabaar and colleagues identified two limitations of conversational interfaces: both steering AI in the intended direction and verifying the results were difficult. The researchers implemented one approach that divided work into subgoals, each paired with assumptions and code, so that people could edit the assumptions directly. A second approach divided the overall task into three phases: assumptions about inputs and outputs, an execution plan, and code. In an experiment with 18 participants, both approaches were reported to make intervention, revision, and verification easier than a conversational interface <v0/>.
Xie 등의 WaitGPT는 AI가 작성한 분석 코드를 실시간으로 데이터: WaitGPT, developed by Xie and colleagues, converts AI-written analysis code into data-flow diagrams in real time. Instead of reading the source code, users can see which data operations occur in which order and modify individual steps. The user study reported that participants detected errors more effectively and had greater confidence in the results <v0/>. Increased confidence must, however, be distinguished from increased accuracy.
세 연구를 모으면 검증에 두 가지 경로가 있다. 하나는 AI가 세운 가정: Taken together, the three studies suggest two paths to verification. One makes the AI's assumptions and data-processing steps visible to people; the other compares the resulting data against an external reference. In either case, verification concerns more than a single final number.
AI는 가능한 분석 중 하나를 고른다: AI chooses one of several possible analyses
분석 과제를 자동으로 푸는 능력을 측정한 벤치마크(benchmark)들은: Benchmarks measuring the ability to solve analysis tasks automatically show that current capabilities remain far from complete.
Chen 등의 ScienceAgentBench는 네 분야의 동료심사 논문: Chen and colleagues' ScienceAgentBench extracted 102 tasks from 44 peer-reviewed papers across four fields, with validation by nine domain experts. With three attempts allowed per task, the best-performing agent independently solved 32.4% of tasks, rising to 34.3% when given expert-provided knowledge. A model with extended reasoning time achieved 42.2%, but the authors reported that result for reference only because its execution conditions differed <v0/>. Majumder and colleagues' DiscoveryBench collected 264 tasks across six fields by reconstructing discovery processes from published papers. Across the reasoning frameworks evaluated, the best system achieved a hypothesis-matching score of 25% <v1/>. The two figures use different metrics and cannot be compared directly. The former is the proportion of tasks solved; the latter scores how closely the derived hypotheses match the reference hypotheses.
BLADE는 성능 대신 선택을 본다. Gu 등은 연구 논문과 통계 교과서: BLADE examines choices rather than performance. Gu and colleagues collected 12 research questions and datasets from research papers and statistics textbooks, then had multiple analysts independently analyze the same questions. This established a reference in which several defensible analyses coexist. The researchers reported that agents' analytical decisions were less diverse than the distribution of experts' decisions and tended to converge on basic analyses <v0/>. The risk is not that AI produces an arbitrary analysis. It is that AI chooses the most obvious analysis without telling the user which alternatives it skipped.
이 수치들은 각 논문이 평가한 시점의 모델과 과제 구성에 해당한다(확인:: These figures reflect the models and task configurations evaluated in each paper (checked: 2026-11-16). Later tools may achieve higher scores, so this section draws the following implication rather than focusing on score magnitude: an AI-generated analysis is one of several possible analyses, not a uniquely correct answer. What must be retained, then, is not only the result but also the choices that produced it.
아래 세 사례의 성격은 서로 다르다. data-to-paper는 동료심사: The following three cases differ in the kinds of evidence they provide. The data-to-paper study is a peer-reviewed paper; the other two are accounts written by the people who performed the work. Firsthand accounts describe the process and tools used, but do not independently establish the quality of the results. Read each case with a distinction between the facts it documents and this section's interpretation.
미국의 투표구 단위 선거 결과는 집계가 끝난 뒤 제각각의 형식으로 공개되: Precinct-level election results in the United States are released in various formats after counting is complete, and many are image-based PDFs. Derek Willis of the OpenElections project published an account of using Gemini 2.5 Pro to convert these PDFs into CSV files <v0/>.
이 사례에서 프롬프트는 변환 규칙 그 자체다. 목표 CSV의 열 구성과: In this case, the prompt itself specifies the transformation rules. It includes the target CSV columns and example rows, conditions for excluding rows, a mapping from office titles to standardized names, rules for quoting values, and an instruction to read two-column pages starting from the left. These rules existed only in the instructions, not in code. Without the prompt, there would be no way to determine which cleaning criteria had been applied.
검증 방식도 기록되어 있다. 짧은 문서는 표본 점검과 수동 수정으로 처리: The verification method is also documented. Short documents were handled with spot checks and manual corrections. A document of more than 600 pages was processed in batches of 100 pages, and the resulting tables were compared against officially published totals <v0/>.
여기서 눈여겨볼 것은 외부 기준점이다. 공식 집계라는 독립적인 숫자가 있: The external reference is the point to notice here. Independent numbers in the form of official totals made it possible to catch aggregate-level errors without reviewing the code. But matching totals is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one. If errors in two precinct-level rows cancel each other out, the total can be correct while the individual rows remain wrong. Where a reference is available, this approach provides the quickest verification, but the level of errors it can detect depends on the reference's level of aggregation.
탐색과 시각화: 코딩 에이전트를 쓰는 작업 흐름: Exploration and visualization: a workflow using coding agents
Simon Willison은 데이터 저널리스트를 대상으로 한 NICAR: Simon Willison published materials for a NICAR 2026 workshop aimed at data journalists. They cover exploring, analyzing, and cleaning data with Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Topics include querying databases, exploring data with agents, cleaning data using geographic codes in tree records as an example, generating visualizations, and scraping <v0/>.
이 자료에서 가져올 것은 환경 구성이다. 작업은 GitHub Codesp: The useful lesson from these materials is the environment setup. The work took place in GitHub Codespaces, a service that launches a shared development environment in the browser from an environment definition stored in the repository. All participants therefore start with the same libraries and data. The data were stored in SQLite, a database that operates as a single file, and some exercises also used Datasette to explore the database through the web. One configuration described in the materials sets up Datasette to serve static files from the <v0/> folder and has the agent create visualizations there. The example is a heatmap of tree locations made with the Leaflet mapping library, with source code also published <v1/>.
In this setup, the analysis outputs remain as repository files rather than just a conversation history. The environment definition, database file, and visualization source are collected in one place, so someone opening the same repository can begin from the same starting point. However, the materials do not cover a procedure for verifying agent-generated queries against known results. Read this as a case of preserving the environment, and obtain verification methods from other sources.
재현을 설계에 넣은 분석 도구: data-to-paper: An analysis tool designed for reproducibility: data-to-paper
Ifargan 등은 주석이 달린 데이터셋에서 출발해 가설 수립, 분석 코: Ifargan and colleagues built and evaluated data-to-paper, a platform that starts with an annotated dataset and proceeds through hypothesis formulation, analysis-code writing and debugging, interpretation of results, and paper writing <v0/>. What makes this case important is its record-keeping approach more than its performance.
플랫폼은 각 단계가 앞선 산출물 가운데 정해진 일부만 받도록 정보 흐름을: The platform restricts information flow so that each stage receives only a specified subset of earlier outputs. The researchers explain that this constraint reduces hallucinations and makes the sources of numerical results traceable. Data-chaining creates a chain that can be followed backward from numbers in the paper. Algorithmically verified hyperlinks connect appendices containing formulas and explanations for transformed values, the tables those values came from, the code output files that produced the tables, and the specific code lines that generated those outputs. The retained artifacts include analysis code in the supplementary materials, output files and tables, literature-search queries and citations, conversations with the model, and execution logs <v0/>.
보고된 결과와 한계는 함께 읽어야 한다. 공개 데이터셋에 목표를 열어 두: The reported results must be read alongside their limitations. Of ten manuscripts generated autonomously from public datasets with open-ended goals, eight contained no major analytical errors, while two contained fundamental errors in analysis or interpretation. The authors estimate a major-error rate of roughly 10–20% for simple goals and datasets. With a complex infection dataset, however, data-processing errors included incorrect file merges and incorrect aggregation over time intervals. In a co-piloting mode in which a person provided review comments on the same dataset, the authors reported obtaining an accurate analysis with about 15 comments in one run <v0/>.
Most relevant to this section is the relationship between two facts stated by the authors. Execution logs allow the same manuscript to be recreated. At the same time, execution is non-deterministic: even with the same inputs and instructions, the responses differ from run to run. A fresh run on the same dataset therefore produces a different analysis and a different manuscript <v0/>.
두 사실이 모순은 아니다. 가리키는 작업이 다르다. 기록된 응답을 되감아: These facts are not contradictory; they refer to different operations. Reassembling the same output by replaying recorded responses is replay. Starting over and reaching the same conclusion is reproduction. With tools whose generation process involves randomness, replay may be possible without reproducibility being guaranteed. We therefore cannot rely on the tool to reach the same conclusion on a fresh run; the choices made at the time must be recorded. This distinction explains why the fourth and fifth items below are needed.
재현을 위해 남길 다섯 가지: Five things to retain for reproducibility
입력이 바뀌면 같은 코드도 다른 결과를 낸다: Different inputs produce different results even with the same code
분석에 쓴 입력 파일을 다시 지목할 수 있는가: Can the input files used in the analysis be identified again?
라이브러리와 실행 순서가 달라지면 코드가 아예 돌지 않거나 다른 값을 낸: Different libraries or execution orders can prevent the code from running or produce different values
다른 기계에서 같은 코드가 같은 값을 내는가: Does the same code produce the same values on another machine?
어떤 집계를 했는지는 출력된 숫자로 구분되지 않는다: The output number does not reveal which aggregation was performed
저장된 코드를 처음부터 실행해 보고서의 숫자가 나오는가: Does running the saved code from the beginning reproduce the numbers in the report?
처리 규칙이 코드가 아니라 지시문에만 있는 경우가 있다: Processing rules sometimes exist only in instructions, not in code
당시 어떤 규칙이 적용되었는지 판정할 수 있는가: Can we determine which rules were applied at the time?
타당한 분석이 여럿이므로 선택이 결론을 바꾼다: Several analyses may be valid, so the choices affect the conclusion
결론을 바꿀 선택이 무엇이었고 왜 그렇게 정했는지 글로 남아 있는가: Is there a written record of which choices could change the conclusion and why those choices were made?
<v0>데이터 버전.</v0> 분석에 들어간 입력 파일의 시점과 내용을: <v0>Data version.</v0> Fix both the point in time and the contents of the input files used in the analysis. Keep separate copies, or record a hash, a fixed-length string computed from the contents, to check whether a file is the same. For externally maintained data that are continually updated, also record when they were retrieved. The official totals served as a reference in the OpenElections case because the point in time to which those totals applied was identifiable.
<v0>실행 환경.</v0> 언어와 라이브러리의 버전, 그리고 코드가 실: <v0>Execution environment.</v0> Record the language and library versions, along with the order in which the code was executed. Pimentel and colleagues studied 1,159,166 Jupyter notebooks collected from GitHub and attempted 863,878 executions of notebooks with identifiable Python versions and cell execution orders. Of these attempts, 24.11% ran without errors and 4.03% reproduced the saved outputs. Module-import errors caused 29.23% of all attempts to fail, while references to undefined names caused 14.53% to fail. The researchers executed cells in their recorded order and explained that unrecorded state and cell execution order could contribute to the latter type of error <v1/>. This 2019 study examined human-written notebooks, so its findings do not apply directly to AI-generated analyses. The shared lesson, however, is that preserving an analysis in files does not by itself make it reproducible. Include seeds here for any steps involving randomness. When splitting training and validation data, sampling, or bootstrapping, failing to fix the seed means the same code produces different values on each run.
<v0>코드.</v0> 대화창에만 있는 코드를 파일로 옮긴다. 앞의 반품: <v0>Code.</v0> Move code that exists only in the chat into files. As in the returns example above, an output number does not reveal which aggregation was performed. The data-to-paper system implements this principle by retaining analysis code and output files in supplementary materials and allowing numerical results in the paper to be traced back to the code lines that produced them <v1/>.
<v0>프롬프트.</v0> 어떤 지시로 그 처리 규칙이 만들어졌는지 남긴: <v0>Prompt.</v0> Record which instructions produced the processing rules. In the OpenElections case, exclusion conditions and mappings to standardized names existed only in the prompt <v1/>. The prompt is not, however, a record for rerunning the analysis. Reusing the same prompt does not produce the same code, and replacing or retiring the model can make the original environment unavailable. Retain the prompt as a decision record that allows the rules applied at the time to be determined. Record the model name and version and when it was run, and keep the prompt together with the code and outputs it produced.
<v0>분석 결정.</v0> 왜 이 변수와 이 모델과 이 제외 기준을 골: <v0>Analytical decisions.</v0> Write down why these variables, this model, and these exclusion criteria were chosen. As BLADE shows, agents converge on basic analyses without disclosing the alternatives they skipped <v1/>. Because generation is non-deterministic, a fresh run cannot be expected to make the same choices. Without a record of those choices, the conclusion cannot be explained.
다섯 가지를 갖추었는지는 하나의 질문으로 점검할 수 있다. 남긴 것만 가: A single question can check whether all five are in place: using only what has been retained, can someone else, or your future self several months later, recreate the same numbers? The data-to-paper system answers this through replaying recorded outputs, while OpenElections answers it through comparison against an external reference.
모든 분석에 같은 수준의 기록을 요구할 필요는 없다. 요구 수준은 그 결: Not every analysis needs the same level of documentation. The level required depends on how far its results will travel.
버릴 탐색에서는 프롬프트와 코드를 남기는 정도로 충분하다. 데이터의 분포: For throwaway exploration, retaining prompts and code is enough. Looking over a data distribution or trying a few aggregations before formulating a hypothesis does not require retracing the same path, because these activities are not reported as conclusions. Conclusions included in a report or presentation, and numbers that others use to make decisions, require all five items and, where possible, comparison against an external reference.
기록 자체가 틀릴 수 있다는 점도 함께 본다. 분석 결정의 설명까지 AI: The records themselves can also be wrong. If AI is asked to explain the analytical decisions as well, it may leave explanations that disagree with the actual code. In that case, the record supplies false support rather than helping reproduction. A person must check that the explanation and code agree.
데이터를 외부 서비스에 올리는 문제는 이 절의 범위를 넘는다. 표나 데이: Uploading data to external services is beyond this section's scope. Before handing an entire table or database to an agent, first establish where those data may be sent.
이 절은 AI 도구를 쓸 때 작업 시간이 어떻게 변하는지 측정하지 않았다: This section did not measure how using AI tools changes working time. It therefore does not assess how much faster analysis becomes, but only what to check and retain when analysis is accelerated. The cited benchmark figures also reflect the models and task configurations evaluated in each study, so they should not be generalized as success rates for current tools.
여기까지는 분석의 결과가 숫자와 그래프, 그리고 그것을 뒷받침하는 기록이: So far, the outputs of analysis have been numbers, graphs, and the records supporting them. Moving these results onto a page that other people can access adds data-access permissions and failure handling to what must be checked. Section 4.3 addresses that boundary.

앞선 장들에서는 AI 코딩 도구에 작업을 요청하는 방법과 이를 활용해 만: Earlier chapters examined how to request work from AI coding tools and what we can build with them. When we open a tool, however, we must decide which model and settings to use before writing the request. GitHub Copilot’s model comparison documentation alone lists more than 20 models in its task-based recommendations. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20). Many options may lead us to look for the best model first, but we can judge which model is suitable only after deciding what work to assign it.
여기서는 모델의 능력과 작업 적합성을 구분한다. 능력은 정해진 과제로 성: This section distinguishes model capability from suitability for a task. Capability refers to scores on benchmarks, tests that measure performance on predefined tasks, or to performance described by the provider. Task suitability means obtaining the result you need within an acceptable time and cost. This distinction is introduced for explanatory purposes. A model regarded as highly capable may still be unnecessarily slow or expensive for your work. In the experiments below, even the cheapest model met all the criteria for two small code-change tasks; the differences were in time and cost.
모든 작업에 같은 모델을 써야 할까?: Should every task use the same model?
친구 네 명이 여행 경비를 나누는 정산 앱 N빵을 만든다고 하자. 지출을: Suppose four friends are building Nppang, an app for splitting travel expenses. It records expenses, sorts them by category, and tells each person how much to send or receive. The work assigned to AI during development varies as follows.
지출 정렬 코드의 동작 설명: Explain how the expense-sorting code works
Trace the actual code to explain sorting rules and exception handling.
항목별 정렬 함수 추가: Add a function to sort expenses by category
Follow the specified order and exception-handling rules without modifying the original list.
같은 지출이 두 번 저장되는 오류 수정: Fix a bug that saves the same expense twice
로그와 코드로 중복이 생기는 경로를 찾고, 정상적인 지출은 남기면서 원인: Use logs and code to identify how duplicates arise, then fix the cause while retaining legitimate expenses.
1인당 금액 계산 규칙 변경 검토: Review a change to the rule for calculating each person’s share
Identify precisely where and under what conditions calculations fail, with supporting evidence.
정렬 코드는 함수 하나를 읽고 설명할 수 있지만, 중복 저장의 원인은 화: Explaining sorting code may require reading just one function, whereas finding the cause of duplicate saves may require tracing the flow from the interface to the server. Response speed matters when exchanging frequent, short explanations; sufficient analysis matters when connecting multiple files to find a cause. Begin by writing down what each task must satisfy to count as finished: its completion criteria.
같은 코드 수정이라도 오류의 영향과 확인 방법이 다르다. 버튼 문구는 바: Even code changes differ in the consequences of errors and how those errors can be checked. Button text can be inspected and corrected immediately, but an incorrectly calculated share changes the amounts friends transfer. The greater the consequences or the harder verification becomes, the more clearly we should define the scope of human review. As with the output-specific review criteria in the preceding chapter, model-selection criteria depend on the task.
오류가 미치는 영향과 확인하기 쉬운지는 별개다. 정산 금액 계산은 틀리면: The consequences of an error and the ease of checking it are separate considerations. A mistake in calculating expense shares has serious consequences, but tests that automatically compare example inputs with expected results make it easy to detect. A slightly awkward layout may have limited consequences, yet a person must look at it to judge its usability. The code-change and interface-building tasks below were chosen to examine this difference.
모델 선택에서 무엇을 볼까?: What should you consider when choosing a model?
먼저 모델과 도구가 필요한 입력과 기능을 지원하는지 확인한다. 화면을 보: First, check whether the model and tool support the inputs and functions you need. Asking about a screenshot requires image input; modifying several files requires access to those files. Compare candidates that meet these prerequisites in terms of accuracy, speed, and cost.
Judge accuracy by whether completion criteria are met, rather than by how plausible an answer sounds. For sorting, check category order, descending amounts within each category, and handling of empty lists, for example. In a review, a comment identifying specific conditions and evidence, such as “Splitting KRW 100,000 among three people and rounding each share up to the nearest KRW 100 produces a total of KRW 100,200,” is more useful than general advice to “improve exception handling.” Section §6.1 covers writing completion criteria, and §10.1 covers verifying them with tests.
속도는 첫 답변까지 걸린 시간과 검토 및 수정을 마칠 때까지의 시간을 나: For speed, distinguish the time to the first response from the time until review and revisions are complete. A fast initial answer may still lead to a slow overall task if repeated revisions are needed. OpenAI’s model-selection guidance likewise recommends comparing how quickly you obtain a useful result, including the time spent checking and correcting it. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20). Cost also includes how much the model reads and writes and how often requests must be repeated, as well as unit prices. The relative importance of speed and cost depends on whether you are making immediate visual adjustments or repeating a task dozens of times a day.
일부 모델은 추론에 쓸 계산량을 조절할 수 있다. 이를 추론 강도(rea: Some models let users adjust the computation devoted to reasoning, called reasoning effort. Available levels and defaults differ by model and tool. Anthropic calls this setting effort and explains that adjusting it is often preferable to switching models. It also recommends evaluating the results on tasks suited to your own work. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20). When listing candidates, record both the model and reasoning effort, such as Haiku 5.5 / medium in the table below.
프로그램에서 모델을 직접 호출하는 API는 보통 토큰 사용량에 따라 요금: APIs that let programs call models directly generally charge by token usage. A token is a unit into which a model divides text for processing. The following are examples of Claude API base prices.

Cache reads and writes, batch discounts, and additional option charges are excluded. Haiku 5.5 prices apply when total input per request is at most 100,000 tokens. Above that threshold, the prices are $0.50 for input and $2.50 for output.
Opus 5.5의 단가는 Haiku 5.5의 40배지만, 작업당 비용도: Opus 5.5 has unit prices 40 times those of Haiku 5.5, but this does not mean its cost per task is also 40 times higher. Models and settings differ in the number of tokens needed to finish the same work. Nor do these prices represent the amount paid per task in a subscription app. For subscription tools, compare the usage and limits they display. Section §5.5 covers billing and usage management. A unit-price table alone cannot tell us the time or total cost of completing a task.
실제 작업의 시간과 총비용을 살펴보려고 N빵의 코드 수정과 화면 만들기를: To examine time and total cost on real tasks, I ran code-change and interface-building tasks for Nppang with different models and reasoning efforts. I assessed code changes using prepared tests and interfaces by opening the results myself. These observations apply to the tasks and conditions used here; they do not establish a general model ranking.
코드 수정: 기준을 통과한 뒤의 차이: Code changes: differences after meeting the criteria
코드 수정은 두 과제다. 정렬 함수 추가에는 항목 순서와 금액 내림차순,: There were two code-change tasks. For adding a sorting function, the request specified five completion criteria, including category order, descending amounts, handling of empty lists, and preserving the original list. For fixing duplicate records, I supplied app and server code, the repository, logs, and user reports, then asked the model to find and fix the cause. The logs showed the app resending a request after a save response took more than three seconds, as well as the save button being pressed twice 0.08 seconds apart. The reports also included a legitimate case of buying coffee twice separately for the same amount. The criterion was therefore to save only one record for retries or double presses while retaining newly entered expenses with identical content.
The table below selects four Claude Code configurations from the full experiment. Claude Code is Anthropic’s terminal-based coding tool. Each run completed the task from a single request without intermediate conversation. I used the estimated costs recorded in the execution logs, based on API unit prices. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20). Starting code, requests, and tool environments were held constant, and each configuration was run three times per task. Every run began in a fresh working folder without human intervention. The scoring tests, five for sorting and eight for the bug fix, were hidden from the models. All 24 runs in the table passed both the scoring tests and the existing tests.

이번 실험에서는 모두 테스트를 통과했지만, 시간과 비용은 달랐다. 정렬: All configurations passed the tests in this experiment, but time and cost differed. Haiku added the sorting function in 17 seconds for approximately $0.006. Haiku also had the lowest cost for fixing duplicate records, while Sonnet on low finished faster. Switching Sonnet to high increased bug-fix time from 36 to 66 seconds and estimated cost from $0.145 to $0.212, without changing whether it passed the tests.
실행 기록을 보면 Haiku는 더 많은 단계를 거쳤다. 턴은 모델이 한: The execution logs show that Haiku took more steps. A turn here means one step in which the model responds and reads or edits a file. Haiku averaged 18.7 turns on the bug fix, while Sonnet on low finished in four. Haiku also read and wrote approximately twice as many tokens as Opus. Thus, despite the 40-fold difference in unit prices, estimated costs on this task differed by approximately 20-fold. The most expensive model, Opus, took the longest of the four configurations on both tasks.
범위를 넓힌 실행에서도 모두 테스트를 통과했다. 같은 두 과제를 Open: The broader set of runs also all passed the tests. All 30 runs of the same two tasks using GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra in OpenAI’s Codex CLI 0.170.0 passed. GPT-6 Sol on low, the middle model, was fastest on both tasks. I did not compare figures across the two tools because they connect models to file access and command execution differently. Even when the bug-fix request omitted the completion-criteria list and described only the symptoms, all four Claude Code configurations passed in each of three runs.
이번 과제에서 비용이 중요하다면 Haiku, 오류 수정의 대기 시간을 줄: For these tasks, Haiku is a candidate when cost matters, and Sonnet on low is a candidate when reducing the wait for a bug fix matters. Passing tests, however, does not guarantee correctness for every input or the quality of explanations. In one symptom-only run, Sonnet high’s summary described two log entries approximately one hour and 36 minutes apart as nearly five hours apart. In one run, Haiku answered a Korean request in English. Both runs produced code that passed the tests, so their explanations needed separate checking. These observations come from two tasks in a small codebase, run three times per configuration; they cannot be generalized to larger projects.
화면 만들기: 사용 목적에 따라 달라지는 기준: Building interfaces: criteria depend on their purpose
앞의 비교에서는 준비한 테스트를 통과했는지가 기준이었다. 화면을 만들 때: The preceding comparison used prepared tests as its criterion. Interface calculations and interactions can also be checked, but judging which information is shown first and how easy an interface is to use requires examining the result. As with the layout example above, some aspects require human judgment even when their consequences are limited.
이를 살펴보려고 N빵의 정산 화면을 HTML 파일 하나로 만들어 달라는: To examine this, I submitted the same request to two new chats in the Claude web app, asking for Nppang’s settlement interface as a single HTML file. The request specified expense filtering and sorting, adding expenses, charts, settlement results, dark mode, and mobile support, and asked for a polished interface suitable for a real service. I supplied six sample expenses without prescribing a design. For one chat (A), I selected Sonnet 4.6 on low; for the other (B), Fable 5.2 on extra. Low and extra are the app’s reasoning-effort levels. Because both the model and reasoning effort changed, with one run each, this is a comparison of two combinations of settings.

같은 요청으로 생성한 N빵 정산 화면. A는 Sonnet 4.6 / 낮음: Nppang settlement interfaces generated from the same request. A used Sonnet 4.6 / low and B used Fable 5.2 / extra. Each shows the expense and settlement screens. Experiment date: 2026-11-20.
기능 점검에는 샘플 총액 764,400원과 1인당 금액 191,100원,: The functionality check covered eight items: the sample total of KRW 764,400 and per-person share of KRW 191,100, settlement results, updates after adding an expense, filtering and sorting, charts, dark mode, and mobile display. Both results passed. If the aim is to check calculations and interface structure quickly, even the result obtained in about two minutes can serve as a draft for review.
정보 배치는 달랐다. A는 총 지출과 1인당 금액, 최다 지출자, 카테고: The information layouts differed. A used four equally sized cards for total spending, the per-person share, the largest spender, and the category count, placing settlement results in the third tab. B gave the per-person share the most prominence. Its settlement screen showed who should send how much to whom, alongside each member’s payments, receivables, and amounts owed. Interfaces with the same functions can therefore differ in how users find the information they need.
추가 점검 기록에는 처음 점검표에 없던 차이도 있다. 18,001원짜리: Additional checks revealed differences absent from the initial checklist. After an expense of KRW 18,001 was added, A showed a one-won discrepancy between one person’s balance and the sum of transfers, while B identified who would cover the remaining won. A also interpreted HTML tags entered as an item name as markup rather than displaying them as text. Such differences are hard to detect from the initial screen alone. Add newly discovered issues to the checklist.
어느 설정을 쓸지는 화면의 용도에 따라 달라진다. 여러 배치를 빠르게 받: Which configuration to use depends on the interface’s purpose. Quickly generated drafts are useful when exploring and choosing among layouts. For an interface that others will continue using, allocate time to check and revise information layout, monetary calculations, input handling, and mobile interactions. Decide whether extra time and cost are worthwhile by examining how much the stronger configuration meets the criteria and reduces revision work. Increasing Sonnet’s reasoning effort for code changes raised only time and cost, whereas interface generation also differed in details such as layout and monetary handling. A single comparison, however, cannot establish a model’s general superiority or suitability for deployment.
후보를 좁히고 직접 비교하기: Narrowing the candidates and comparing them yourself
두 사례에서 보듯, 어떤 설정이 충분한지는 완료 기준과 시간, 비용의 우: As these cases show, an adequate configuration depends on completion criteria and the priorities assigned to time and cost. Provider comparison documents can help narrow the field to two or three candidates. OpenAI’s model-selection guide describes suitable tasks for eight combinations of models and reasoning levels and illustrates each model’s suitability for six types of work. For example, it recommends GPT-6 Luna on low for small file edits or field extraction when the expected result is clear, and GPT-6.2 Sol on Medium for bug fixes and feature additions in existing codebases. The same page states that these suitability ratings are approximate estimates based on benchmarks, independently run example tasks, and user feedback. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-21).
The comparison figure showing model-selection guidance will appear once its original image has been added.

이런 안내와 벤치마크 점수는 후보를 좁히는 데 쓰되, 점수가 무엇을 재는: Use such guidance and benchmark scores to narrow the candidates, while checking what the scores actually measure. SWE-bench Verified evaluates coding by testing fixes to issues from public repositories; it does not measure the quality of code explanations or review comments. <v0/> (published: 2024-08-13; updated: 2025-02-24). In February 2026, OpenAI, which helped create the benchmark, also stopped reporting its scores. It had reviewed 138 tasks its models consistently failed and found defects in the tests or problem descriptions in 59.4% of them. <v1/> (published: 2026-02-23). Section §10.4 discusses benchmark limitations.
After narrowing the candidates, assign them your own tasks and record the following.
맡길 일과 완료 기준을 정한다. 필요한 파일과 자료, 바꿔도 되는 범위를: Define the work and completion criteria. Prepare the required files and reference materials, specify what may be changed, and provide tests or an output checklist. For a review, include criteria for identifying an issue’s location, triggering conditions, and supporting evidence.
같은 시작 파일과 요청문을 새 세션에 준다. 도구 환경을 고정하고 모델이: Give each candidate the same starting files and request in a new session. Hold the tool environment constant and change one factor at a time, either the model or reasoning effort. If both change, record the result as a comparison of combinations, as in the HTML example. For recurring tasks, run the same configuration several times to assess variability.
기준 충족 여부와 실행 시간, 사람의 검토 및 수정 시간, 비용이나 사용: Consider whether criteria are met alongside execution time, human review and revision time, and cost or usage. Also record the date, tool version, model ID, and reasoning effort. Among candidates that meet the requirements, choose according to your time and cost priorities.
작고 확인하기 쉬운 일은 저렴한 모델이나 낮은 추론 강도로 시작해 부족하: For small, easily checked tasks, you can start with a cheaper model or lower reasoning effort and increase it if needed. For tasks whose failures are hard to recover from or whose difficulty is uncertain, you can start with a stronger candidate and lower the settings while maintaining your criteria. Anthropic describes both starting points. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20). OpenAI recommends comparing configurations on identical inputs and retaining the lightest one that meets the quality criteria. <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20). In the code-change example, even the cheapest configuration met the criteria, so the remaining decision about increasing the settings depended on waiting time.
기준에 못 미쳤다고 바로 모델을 바꿀 필요는 없다. 정렬 규칙을 다르게: Falling short of the criteria does not immediately require a different model. If the model misunderstood a sorting rule, add example inputs and expected outputs. If it missed relevant files, check the reference materials and access permissions first. Adjust reasoning effort or the model if the same failures persist after improving the materials and instructions. The criteria and records you retain can be reused when new models appear. 동아리 행사를 알리는 웹페이지를 AI와 함께 만든다고 생각해 보자. 사용: Imagine building a web page with AI to announce a club event. The user provides the event name, time, location, and registration link and asks for a page that is also easy to read on a phone. The agent reads the existing page files, finds event details in a reference document, and checks the revised page in a browser. Requests to change colors or shorten text arrive during the work, as does a correction changing the event time from 2 p.m. to 3 p.m.
대화가 길어질수록 처음의 요청에 여러 버전의 파일과 화면 점검 결과, 새: As the conversation grows, different file versions, screen-check results, and new decisions accumulate alongside the initial request. If the finished page shows the old time, we need to identify where the process went wrong: whether the agent read the latest announcement, selected the corrected information, and reflected it on the actual page. Both the capacity to hold input and the ability to use the information it contains are involved.
아래에서는 이 가상의 제작 과정을 따라 컨텍스트를 어떻게 구성하고 정리할: The discussion below follows this hypothetical process to explain how to organize and maintain context. The final event time is 3 p.m. and the location is Room 301. The existing registration link must remain unchanged, and only <v0/> may be modified. These conditions continue to apply while the design is adjusted.
1. 컨텍스트 윈도에는 무엇이 들어가는가: 1. What goes into a context window?
앞선 3.3절에서 설명한 컨텍스트(context)는 모델이 현재 응답을: As explained in Section 3.3, context is the information supplied to a model for use in generating its current response. The context window is the maximum number of tokens it can handle in one processing operation. Models process text in units called tokens. Tokenization varies by language, wording, and tokenizer, so texts with the same character count can occupy different amounts of space.
대화형 AI에서는 사용자의 질문과 AI의 답변이 먼저 눈에 들어온다. 코: In conversational AI, the user’s questions and the AI’s answers are most immediately visible. A coding agent’s input also includes baseline instructions and tool descriptions. Reading files or checking a screen adds results that inform later decisions. GitHub’s official documentation explains that system instructions, tool definitions, messages, and tool results share the context. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18; product: GitHub Copilot; consult the official documentation for client-specific differences).
In building the event page, these components appear as follows.
모델의 판단에 주는 정보: Information it provides for model decisions
도구 사용과 응답 방식에 관한 기본 규칙: Baseline rules for tool use and responses
작업 중 따라야 하는 기본 동작과 제약: Default behavior and constraints to follow during the task
<v0/>에 적힌 수정 범위와 파일 규칙: The modification scope and file rules in <v0/>
이번 저장소에서 공통으로 지킬 조건: Conditions shared across work in this repository
행사 안내 작성, 색상 변경, 오후 3시로 정정: Write the announcement, change colors, and correct the time to 3 p.m.
현재 목표와 사용자의 최신 결정: The current goal and the user’s latest decisions
파일 읽기와 편집, 브라우저 확인 도구의 설명: Descriptions of tools for reading and editing files and checking the browser
어떤 작업을 어떤 입력으로 요청할 수 있는지: Which operations can be requested and with which inputs
읽은 파일과 검색 자료: Files read and retrieved reference materials
현재 구현과 수정의 근거: The current implementation and the basis for changes
파일 내용, 검색 결과, 화면 점검 결과: File contents, search results, and screen-check results
실제로 무엇을 읽고 수정하고 확인했는지: What was actually read, modified, and verified
선택한 배치, 남은 모바일 화면 점검: The selected layout and remaining mobile checks
다음 행동을 정하는 데 필요한 작업 이력: Task history needed to determine the next action
제품은 이 정보들을 각자의 방식으로 메시지에 담는다. 파일의 일부 구간만: Products package this information into messages in different ways. They may supply only selected file ranges or shorten lengthy tool output. Tool definitions explain which functions can be called and how, while execution results describe what a call established. Both occupy input space, but they contribute differently to decisions.
정보가 들어오는 순서도 살펴볼 수 있다. 세션을 시작할 때 기본 지침과: We can also examine the order in which information arrives. Baseline and project instructions load when a session starts; user requests add goals and conditions. Reading a file adds current code, and checking a screen adds inspection results. A correction received during the task may leave both old and current values in the conversation history. The model must also be able to recognize which information has been updated.
모델이 학습으로 얻은 지식, 디스크에 저장된 파일, 현재 입력으로 전달된: Knowledge acquired during training, files stored on disk, and information supplied in the current input are distinct. A file becomes evidence for the current decision when the agent reads it and receives its contents. Earlier messages are likewise included either in full or as summaries, depending on how the tool constructs the next input. Alongside the conversation visible on screen, users should check the current usage and compaction state reported by the tool.
2. 긴 컨텍스트가 도움이 되는 작업과 토큰 예산: 2. Tasks that benefit from long context and token budgeting
긴 컨텍스트는 여러 자료의 관계를 함께 살펴보는 작업에 유용하다. 최종: Long context is useful for examining relationships among multiple sources. The final announcement specifies what must change, the current HTML shows where to change it, and screen-check results show the display state. Consulting them together connects requirements, implementation, and verification results when deciding the next revision.
이전 판단의 근거를 유지하는 데도 공간이 필요하다. 여러 대안을 비교한: Retaining the reasons behind earlier decisions also takes space. A choice made after comparing alternatives has a rationale. Keeping that rationale makes it easier to apply the same criteria in later revisions. If only the final choice is passed on, alternatives already considered may be discussed again. This continuity helps sustain multistep code changes and research.
토큰 예산을 세울 때는 이미 사용 중인 공간과 앞으로 필요한 공간을 함께: Token budgeting should consider both the space already in use and the space needed next. Baseline instructions and conversation history occupy part of the window, with newly read files and tool results added to it. Room is also needed to generate a response. The following table uses hypothetical amounts to illustrate this relationship. Here, 1K means 1,000 tokens, and the total budget is assumed to be 100K.
예시에서 이미 들어간 정보: Information already included in the example
사용자 요청, 이전 응답과 결정: User requests, earlier responses, and decisions
읽어 온 HTML과 관련 문서: HTML and related documents already read
현재 사용량을 빼면 남은 공간은 55K다. 다음 응답과 처리를 위해 15: Subtracting current usage leaves 55K of space. Reserving 15K for the next response and processing leaves a planned allowance of 40K for new materials. The 15K reserve is an operating assumption for this calculation. The actual reserve should reflect how the model and service account for output and reasoning tokens, as well as the expected size of the next task.
남은 공간의 의미는 다음 행동에 따라 달라진다. 짧은 문구를 고칠 때보다: The significance of remaining space depends on the next action. Reading a long document or running a check that returns many results requires more headroom than changing a short phrase. Comparing usage before and after reading files reveals which materials occupy a large share. Recording where usage rises sharply during a task can help budget similar work later.
필요한 자료가 예산 안에 들어오고 결과도 안정적이라면 그 맥락을 유지하며: If the necessary materials fit within the budget and results remain stable, the task can continue with that context intact. When reducing input, preserve the evidence needed for decisions first. Start by defining which materials must be compared together for the current task, then distinguish information to reread later from information to retain throughout. Sections 5.1 and 5.5 discuss model-specific limits and usage costs.
3. 공간 안에 들어간 정보도 놓칠 수 있다: 3. Information can be missed even when it fits
컨텍스트 운영에서는 용량과 활용 능력을 따로 살펴야 한다. 한도를 넘으면: Context management requires examining capacity and utilization separately. If input exceeds the limit, it must be reduced or compacted. Even within the limit, we must independently check whether relevant information influences the result. A model’s maximum token count describes capacity alone.
Liu 등의 「Lost in the Middle」은 긴 입력에서 관련 정: Liu and colleagues’ “Lost in the Middle” varied the position of relevant information in long inputs and compared performance on question answering and key-value retrieval. The models tested tended to perform worse when relevant information appeared in the middle rather than at the beginning or end. Introduced in Section 3.3, the study shows that position within the input can affect information use. Its findings must be interpreted within the scope of the models and tasks studied. <v0>Nelson F. Liu et al., Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts</v0> (TACL, 2024, volume 12, pp. 157–173).
예를 들어 행사 시각의 정정 뒤로 디자인 논의가 길게 이어지면, 최종 정: For example, if a long design discussion follows the correction to the event time, establishing the final information requires tracing relationships across messages. The order of the old announcement and correction, and which value is final, becomes important. If the old time appears in the output, begin by checking whether the necessary evidence was supplied. Narrowing down the cause of the observed error requires examining omitted input, judgments about recency, and implementation.
유사한 내용의 자료가 많이 섞인 상황도 검토할 만하다. 폐기한 시안과 다: Situations containing many similar sources also deserve examination. Discarded drafts and records from other tasks require the agent to distinguish information relevant to the current goal. Practitioners’ term “attention distraction” can be understood as referring to failures in selecting and combining information. Analysis is more useful when it records specifically which condition was missed and which source was used incorrectly.
관련 정보를 찾아낸 뒤의 추론에도 한계가 있다. Du 등은 필요한 정보를: Reasoning after information has been found also has limits. Du and colleagues reported cases where reasoning performance declined as input length grew even under conditions designed to ensure retrieval of the necessary information. Their mathematics, question-answering, and coding tasks included conditions that replaced unnecessary content with whitespace or prevented the model from attending to it. These findings support evaluating retrieval separately from the use of retrieved evidence. <v0>Yufeng Du et al., Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval</v0> (Findings of EMNLP, 2025, pp. 23281–23298).
실제 작업에서는 근거가 입력에 포함되었는지, 최신 기준을 선택했는지, 최: In practice, check in sequence whether the evidence entered the input, whether the latest criteria were selected, and whether they were reflected in the final output. File-reading records provide clues for the first step; comparing requirements with results provides evidence for the last. Identifying the failed stage helps determine whether to reread materials, organize the current state, or fix the implementation.
4. 무엇을 보여 주고 무엇을 나중에 읽게 할 것인가: 4. What to show now and what to read later
입력에 넣을 자료는 다음 판단과의 관련성을 기준으로 고른다. 요구사항을: Choose input materials according to their relevance to the next decision. The final specification takes priority when checking requirements; current code and related interfaces when changing implementation; and verification conditions and execution records when inspecting results. Adding materials as each stage requires them also makes their role in decisions clearer.
관련 파일을 아직 모를 때는 목록과 검색 결과로 범위를 좁힌 뒤 내용을: When the relevant files are not yet known, use listings and search results to narrow the scope before reading their contents. Start at a location found through search, then examine connected functions or other places displaying the same information. Anthropic presents retrieving materials when needed and providing detail progressively as practical approaches to context design. <v0/> (published: 2025-09-29; practical recommendations from the product developer).
자료를 현재 입력에서 제외할 때는 다시 찾을 경로를 남긴다. 원본 파일을: When excluding material from the current input, retain a route for finding it again. Keeping original files and recording relevant ranges and update times enables later comparisons. Link verification records to the code version or screen state they checked. After changes, recheck affected items and update the records. Selecting evidence that matches the current state must accompany adjustments to input size.
프로젝트 지침 파일에는 반복해서 필요한 규칙을 둘 수 있다. <v0/>와: Project instruction files can hold recurring rules. <v0/> and <v1/> are files stored on disk; they become part of the context when a tool reads them into model input. They are appropriate for conditions referred to across tasks, such as permitted modification scope, build commands, and file-saving rules. Keeping ongoing investigations and unresolved issues in separate records makes shared rules and task state easier to manage.

파일 분리의 효과는 로딩 방식에 따라 달라진다. Claude Code 문: The effect of splitting files depends on how they are loaded. Claude Code’s documentation explains that files imported from <v0/> are loaded together with it. In this case, splitting files helps organize and maintain instructions, while input usage depends on the amount of content loaded together. Deferring loading until needed requires an appropriate rule scope or reference mechanism.
