자료를 읽을 때마다 현재 판단에 필요한 정보인지, 원문을 계속 유지해야: Whenever material is read, consider whether it is needed for the current decision, whether the full original must remain in context, or whether it can be reread later. Section 6.3 discusses systems that automate selecting and supplying information. Even with such systems, users must verify that important constraints and current evidence are provided for the task.
5. 같은 작업을 이어 가기 위한 컨텍스트 압축: 5. Context compaction for continuing the same task
파일을 선별해 읽더라도 작업을 오래 이어 가면 대화와 실행 결과가 쌓인다: Even with selective file reading, conversation and execution results accumulate over a long task. Keeping completed investigations and discarded alternatives in full leaves less room for subsequent work. Context compaction frees space by replacing earlier input with a smaller representation. What matters is how to preserve the state needed to continue the task.
Claude Code의 <v0/>는 대화 이력을 요약하고, 사용자가 보존: Claude Code describes <v0/> as summarizing conversation history, with users able to specify what to preserve. <v1/> starts a new conversation. Compaction can organize the history of the same task so it can continue, while a new conversation allows context to be assembled around a new goal. Both operate on conversational context; modifying project files is a separate operation. <v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-18; product: Claude Code).
행사 페이지의 압축 전 이력에는 옛 공지, 색상 비교, 이전 HTML과: Before compaction, the event-page history contains an old announcement, color comparisons, earlier HTML, and several screen-check results. A summary can focus on final decisions, applicable constraints, and outstanding checks. For example, retain the latest event details, the chosen vertical layout and its rationale, and the requirement to preserve the registration link. The record should be specific enough to make clear what the next revision needs.
원문에서 다시 확인할 수 있는 내용에는 경로를 남긴다. HTML의 세부: For details that can be checked against the original, retain their locations. For example, read HTML details and exact link addresses from the latest file, while putting decision rationales not evident from the file into the summary. Information that will be difficult to access again needs fuller preservation. This approach shortens the summary while retaining a way to recover missing information.
압축 뒤에도 기본 지침과 다시 읽는 자료는 공간을 차지한다. Claude: Baseline instructions and reread materials still occupy space after compaction. Claude Code’s documentation explains that root-level <v0/> and certain other instructions are reinjected, while some lower-level instructions load when needed. Comparing usage immediately after compaction with usage after rereading files reveals what fills the space. If the workflow repeatedly loads large instructions or files, the way materials are supplied also needs adjustment. <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-18; product: Claude Code; reinjection scope follows the documentation).
압축 결과의 표현 방식은 제품마다 다르다. OpenAI Responses: Products represent compaction results differently. The OpenAI Responses API can return encrypted compacted state, distinct from a human-readable summary. Such state must be passed to the next request in the form specified by the API. Progress notes that users read and edit are maintained separately. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18; product: Responses API). In each tool, check whether work continues to follow the necessary decisions and constraints after compaction.
6. 요약과 상태 외부화로 남겨야 할 것: 6. What to retain through summaries and external state
도구의 자동 압축과 함께, 사람이 검토할 수 있는 진행 기록을 파일로 남: Alongside automatic compaction, progress can be recorded in files that people can review. Here, we call this a state summary. Saving conversational information outside the context, in progress files, decision records, or verification lists, is called externalizing state. Later sessions can read these records to reconstruct the work.
상태 요약은 다음 작업자가 목표와 현재 상황을 파악하고 첫 행동을 정할: Write a state summary so that the next worker can understand the goal and current situation and determine a first action. Focus on current decisions, their reasons, and remaining issues, distinguishing completed work from items still needing verification. A record is easier to use for handoff when it makes clear what to verify first. Preserve conversational chronology only as needed to explain decision backgrounds.
다음은 앞의 제작 사례에서 작업을 잠시 멈출 때 남길 수 있는 인계 메모: The following is an example handoff note that could be left when pausing work on the event page.
메모에는 구현과 검증의 상태를 각각 적는다. 파일을 수정한 단계라면 무엇: Record implementation and verification status separately. If a file was edited, describe the change; if the screen was inspected, add the conditions and findings. This separation lets the next session continue verification. Also distinguish user corrections, agent hypotheses, and actual observations.
기록 형식은 맡길 역할에 따라 선택한다. 진행 파일에는 현재 단계와 다음: Choose record formats according to their role. A progress file records the current stage and next action; a decision record explains why an alternative was chosen; a verification list records completion criteria and their status. Git supplies file-change history. Adding conditions established before implementation and the reasons for decisions provides a basis for reconstructing the work. Small tasks can keep all this in one short progress file.
Anthropic의 장기 작업 지침은 진행 메모, 구조화된 테스트 상태와: Anthropic’s long-running-task guidance describes continuing work in a fresh context using progress notes, structured test status, and Git history. Record formats can be chosen to suit task size and the tools used. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18; official Claude Platform documentation).
상태 파일은 결정이나 구현이 바뀔 때 함께 갱신한다. 여러 기록의 내용이: Update state files whenever decisions or implementation change. If records disagree, establish the authoritative reference first, then reconcile related records. Dates and supporting evidence make outdated parts easier to locate. Include reading state records and comparing them with actual files in the next session’s workflow. Section 7.4 covers detailed designs for storing and restoring memory and checkpoints.
7. 새 세션을 시작하는 편이 나은 경우: 7. When starting a new session is preferable
작업 목표가 달라지면 필요한 자료와 판단 기준도 달라진다. 이전 목표에: A change in goals changes the necessary materials and criteria. If much conversation about the previous goal remains, consider selecting the information needed for the new task and starting a new session. Carry over completed results and shared rules, while organizing input around materials relevant to the new goal.
같은 프로젝트 안에서도 이런 전환이 일어난다. 구현을 마친 뒤 사용자의: Such transitions occur even within the same project. Moving from implementation to investigating a user’s question changes the required materials and tools. The completed output and investigation goal can become the starting point for new work. While continuing to fix one bug, however, recent observations and attempted fixes remain important evidence. Preserving that history and continuing the task is more natural in this case.
오래된 가정이 반복될 때도 세션 구성을 점검할 수 있다. 정정된 조건이: Repeated reliance on outdated assumptions is another reason to examine session structure. If corrected conditions keep being missed, first compare the latest materials, current implementation, and progress records. If old assumptions persist after discrepancies are resolved, select the latest state and pass it to a new conversation. Record which materials were reorganized and how results changed to inform future operating decisions.
재시작 뒤에도 프로젝트 파일과 설정은 이어진다. 오래된 값이 코드나 지침: Project files and settings persist across restarts. Old values left in code, instructions, or external memory may be read again by the new session. When preparing a restart, therefore, check both conversation history and saved state. Continuing rules, updated evidence, and files requiring changes must agree to provide a clear starting point.
새 세션에는 다음 목표, 최신 상태 기록과 원문 경로를 전달한다. 먼저: Provide the new session with its next goal, the latest state records, and original-source locations. It can first read the records and compare them with current files, then verify unconfirmed items. Anthropic’s long-running-task guidance likewise discusses choosing between restoring state from files and using compaction. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18).
이전 대화를 닫기 전에는 인계 메모만으로 다음 행동을 정할 수 있는지 읽: Before closing the old conversation, read the handoff note to check whether it is sufficient to determine the next action. Add decision rationales or original-source locations wherever understanding still requires searching earlier messages. Distinguishing the state to reconstruct from items to verify afresh makes continuing work easier.
8. 압축 시점은 사용량과 작업 상태를 함께 보고 정한다: 8. Choose when to compact using both usage and task state
압축 시점을 판단하려면 현재 사용량과 다음 작업에 필요한 공간을 함께 살: To decide when to compact, examine both current usage and the space needed for the next task. A small wording change and analysis of a large file require different headroom. Even at the same usage level, the choice may depend on how much earlier history remains relevant. Finishing a stage also offers a natural point for organizing state.
자동 압축은 긴 세션을 이어 가도록 도구가 제공하는 기능이다. 수동 압축: Automatic compaction is a tool-provided feature for sustaining long sessions. Manual compaction lets the worker specify the current goal and key information to retain while organizing history. The appropriate choice depends on how the tool handles compaction automatically, the remaining work, and preservation requirements. Manual controls can be used to check usage and organize essential state before the next large task.
Salle 등은 OpenCode에서 압축 시점과 전략을 비교했다. Cla: Salle and colleagues compared compaction timing and strategies in OpenCode. For Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4, task scores showed no clear differences across thresholds of 160K–380K tokens; for GPT-5.3-Codex, lower thresholds were disadvantageous on PaperBench. Results for the first two models, which have 1M windows, should be interpreted within this threshold range. The study also reported that the first summary on ProgramBench omitted approximately one-third of restrictive rules on average. Its findings apply to the execution framework and tasks studied. <v0>Jeanne Salle et al., Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly</v0> (released: 2026-10-22; arXiv v1, Sections 4.1 and 4.2; preprint).
압축 시점을 앞당기면 공간을 일찍 확보할 수 있지만, 압축이 거듭되는 동: Earlier compaction frees space sooner, but repeated compaction requires checking whether necessary information survives. The difference between task scores and constraint retention observed in the study shows why this check matters. Evaluation should cover adherence to permitted modification scope and work procedures as well as completed features.
다음 표는 논문과 제품 권고를 종합한 운영 판단안이다. 실제 선택에는 사: The following table synthesizes the paper and product recommendations into a proposed decision guide. Actual choices should also consider the model and tool, materials needed next, and how readily results can be verified.
목표가 같고 공간이 남으며 결과도 안정적임: The goal is unchanged, space remains, and results are stable
현재 단계의 작업과 검증을 이어 간다: Continue the current stage and its verification
반복 설명과 폐기한 대안의 이력이 많이 쌓임: Repeated explanations and discarded alternatives have accumulated
현재 상태를 정리하고 압축을 검토한다: Organize current state and consider compaction
최신 결정과 제약, 미해결 문제를 남긴다: Retain the latest decisions, constraints, and unresolved issues
한 단계를 마치고 큰 자료를 읽을 예정임: A stage is complete and a large input is about to be read
상태 요약 후 공간을 확인한다: Summarize state, then check available space
완료 기준을 기록하고 예상 출력의 여유를 둔다: Record completion criteria and reserve room for the expected output
필요한 결과만 남기고 새 세션을 연다: Retain only the needed results and open a new session
새 목표에 필요한 입력을 구성한다: Assemble input relevant to the new goal
근거 파일을 바로잡고 재시작을 검토한다: Correct the source files and consider restarting
현재 코드와 진행 기록의 일치 여부를 확인한다: Check that current code and progress records agree
압축 후 근거가 빠진 것으로 의심됨: Evidence may have been lost during compaction
원문을 다시 읽고 결과를 재검증한다: Reread the original and verify the result again
요약에서 빠진 조건과 근거를 보완한다: Restore conditions and evidence omitted from the summary
작업의 경계는 사용자가 보존할 정보를 정리하기 좋은 시점이다. 검토한 대: Task boundaries offer useful points for organizing what to preserve, because considered alternatives can be distinguished from adopted decisions and remaining issues recorded. If enough space remains and the task will finish soon, it can simply be completed. If a large input is next, use the record to decide whether to compact. This connects the current stage with the next action.
9. 작업 전환 때 적용할 확인 기준: 9. Checks to apply when switching tasks
평소에는 큰 자료를 읽기 전, 한 단계를 끝냈을 때와 컨텍스트를 전환한: It helps to define questions to ask before reading large inputs, after finishing a stage, and after changing context. The following list applies the preceding decision criteria to practical work.
현재 목표를 확인한다. 지금 수행할 단계와 완료 조건을 정하고, 그 판단: Confirm the current goal. Define the stage to perform and its completion conditions, then identify the materials needed to judge it.
최신 기준과 입력을 확인한다. 적용할 명세와 현재 파일, 변경 범위가 모: Check current criteria and inputs. Verify that the applicable specification, current files, and modification scope reached the model. Inspect both file-reading records and the contents actually supplied.
다음 행동에 필요한 여유를 확인한다. 새로 읽을 자료와 예상되는 도구 결: Check headroom for the next action. Allocate space for new materials, expected tool results, and the response.
이어받을 상태를 남긴다. 최신 결정과 이유, 제약, 미해결 문제와 원문: Record state to carry forward. Include the latest decisions and their reasons, constraints, unresolved issues, and original-source locations. Distinguish confirmed facts from hypotheses and completed verification from outstanding checks.
계속 진행, 압축, 새 세션 중 선택한다. 현재 목표와 이력의 필요성,: Choose whether to continue, compact, or start a new session. Base the choice on the current goal, the need for history, and available space. Give a new session both the state to restore and its first action.
전환 뒤 실제 결과를 대조한다. 최신 요구사항과 산출물, 변경 범위와 검: Compare actual results after the transition. Check current requirements against the output, modification scope, and verification records. If they differ, reread the necessary evidence and update the state.
컨텍스트 운영은 현재 작업에 필요한 정보를 선택하고, 변화한 상태를 반영: Context management selects information needed for the current task, reflects changes in state, and supports the next decision. A large window expands the range of materials that can be consulted together. Maintaining current decisions and necessary evidence within it remains an ongoing responsibility. Compaction and restarts organize this flow; their effects can be assessed through requirement satisfaction and total task cost.

<v0>용어: open-weight는 오픈소스가 아니다</v0>: <v0>Terminology: open-weight is not the same as open source</v0>
<v0>가중치 공개 여부와 호스팅 방식은 별개의 선택이다</v0>: <v0>Weight availability and hosting are separate choices</v0>
<v0>상황에 맞게 고르는 순서</v0>: <v0>A process for choosing what fits your situation</v0>
바이브 코딩 도구를 쓰다 보면 “이 코드와 데이터를 외부 API로 보내도: Using vibe-coding tools raises the question, “May this code and data be sent to an external API?” Models such as GPT, Claude, and Gemini do not disclose their weights and run only on servers operated by their providers or partner cloud services. In contrast, models such as gpt-oss, DeepSeek-R1, and Llama offer downloadable weights that users can run themselves. The two approaches differ in where data goes, cost structure, customization scope, and operational responsibility as well as performance. Task-specific model selection (§5.1), routing (§5.4), and cost management (§5.5) are covered separately. This section focuses on access to weights, data control, and hosting responsibility.
용어: open-weight는 오픈소스가 아니다: Terminology: open-weight is not the same as open source
가중치(weights)는 학습으로 정해진 모델 내부의 숫자 값이다. 이: Weights are numerical values within a model determined through training. Here, a closed-weight model does not disclose its weights and is available only through a provider’s API or service, while an open-weight model publishes downloadable weights that users can run themselves. The Open Source AI Definition 1.0 (OSAID), announced by the Open Source Initiative (OSI) on October 28, 2024, requires the freedoms to use, study, modify, and share, together with Data Information, the complete Code for training and execution, and model Parameters (<v0/>; <v1/> (published: 2024-10-28)). OSI calls publishing weights without training code and data information “Open Weights” and distinguishes it from open-source AI (<v2/> (published: 2025-01-29)). Ai2’s Olmo 3 exemplifies disclosure of all three components: it publishes Dolma 3, a training dataset of approximately six trillion tokens, and checkpoints throughout training, releasing all models under Apache 2.0 (<v3/> (published: 2025-11-20)).
같은 open-weight라도 사용 조건은 라이선스마다 다르다. gpt-: Even among open-weight models, permitted uses depend on the license. gpt-oss uses Apache 2.0 (<v0>OpenAI, gpt-oss-120b model card</v0> (accessed: 2026-11-15)), and DeepSeek-R1 uses the MIT license (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)), both broadly permitting commercial use and modification. The Llama 4 Community License, however, requires separate Meta authorization for businesses with more than 700 million monthly active users in the month before release. It also requires “Built with Llama” attribution, a “Llama” prefix for models improved using Llama, and compliance with its acceptable-use policy (<v2/> (effective: 2025-04-05)). Such use restrictions differ from OSAID’s requirement of freedom to use for any purpose without permission; this comparison is the interpretation offered in this section. Before asking whether a model is open-weight, therefore, check whether its license fits your intended use. Also read the model card describing intended uses and limitations, training data, and evaluation results (<v3/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)).
가중치 공개 여부와 호스팅 방식은 별개의 선택이다: Weight availability and hosting are separate choices
가중치를 공개했는지와 누가 모델을 실행하는지를 나누면 다음과 같은 조합이: Separating whether weights are available from who runs the model yields the following combinations.
제공사나 클라우드 사업자가 실행: Run by the provider or a cloud service
제공사 API(OpenAI API, Anthropic API 등), 클라: Provider APIs (OpenAI API, Anthropic API, etc.) and cloud hosting (such as Azure OpenAI models in Microsoft Foundry)
가중치가 없으므로 해당 없음: Not applicable because weights are unavailable
관리형 API(Amazon Bedrock의 gpt-oss 등): Managed APIs (such as gpt-oss on Amazon Bedrock)
개인 PC, 연구실 서버, 임대 GPU(Ollama, vLLM 등): Personal PCs, laboratory servers, or rented GPUs (using Ollama, vLLM, etc.)
Microsoft는 Foundry에서 판매하는 모델(Azure OpenA: Microsoft states that models sold through Foundry, including Azure OpenAI models, are hosted in its Azure environment and that user prompts and outputs are not shared with model providers such as OpenAI. However, Microsoft employees may review data flagged by abuse monitoring (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)). Conversely, AWS announced on August 5, 2025 that gpt-oss would be available through Amazon Bedrock (<v1/> (published: 2025-08-19)). In that case the model is open-weight, but users do not operate GPUs. Of the criteria below, data control and operational burden depend mainly on who runs the model; customization and version retention depend mainly on whether the user has its weights.
With an external API, code and data included in prompts are transmitted to the provider. OpenAI states that since March 1, 2023, it has not used API data for training without user consent, but abuse-monitoring logs are retained for up to 30 days by default. Zero Data Retention, which excludes customer content from these logs, requires prior approval. Data stored to provide features such as Files, Vector stores, and Batches remains until the user deletes it (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)). Anthropic likewise states that inputs and outputs from commercial products such as its API are not used for training by default (<v1/> (published: 2026-08-18)). These commitments rest on policy documents and may change. They also do not satisfy an institutional rule that prohibits external transmission itself. The US NTIA identifies using a model without sharing data with third parties as a benefit of open-weight models (<v2/> (published: 2024-07-30; Executive Summary)).
직접 실행이 저절로 안전한 것은 아니다. JFrog는 Hugging Fa: Running a model yourself is not automatically safe. JFrog found approximately 100 malicious models on Hugging Face; models in pickle format can execute embedded code as soon as they are loaded (<v0/> (published: 2024-02-27)). Prefer safetensors files from trusted distributors (<v1/> (published: 2023-05-23)). Models also differ in behavior. In an evaluation by CAISI, part of NIST, agents based on DeepSeek R1-0528 were 12 times more likely to follow malicious instructions than the US models compared, and responded to 94% of malicious requests under jailbreak techniques, versus 8% for the US models. Since the comparison also included an open-weight model, gpt-oss, this does not establish a problem with all open-weight models; it supports evaluating models individually (<v2/> (published: 2025-09-30)). NTIA also notes that open-weight models have substantially fewer built-in safeguards and that developers releasing weights cannot control or observe end-user behavior (<v3/>). Self-hosting requires users to provide the abuse monitoring and safety filters otherwise handled by a provider.
API는 보통 토큰 수에 따른 종량제라 사용량이 적거나 불규칙할 때 유리: APIs generally charge by token usage, making them advantageous for low or irregular demand; §5.5 covers specific prices. Self-hosting incurs GPU, electricity, and staffing costs even without requests, so cost per token depends on GPU utilization. Serving software also affects cost. The vLLM paper reported two to four times the throughput of previous systems at the same latency (<v0>Woosuk Kwon et al., Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention</v0> (published: 2023-09-12)). Required memory can be estimated as parameter count × bytes per parameter. A 70B model requires approximately 140GB at 16 bits or 35GB at four bits. These estimates cover weights only; additional memory is needed for the KV cache, which grows with conversation length, and the execution environment. In practice, gpt-oss-120b runs on one 80GB GPU and gpt-oss-20b in 16GB of memory (<v1>OpenAI, gpt-oss-120b model card</v1>). Using an open-weight model through a managed API lets users begin with usage-based billing and no GPUs while retaining the option of self-hosting later.
Epoch AI는 2024년 11월 open 모델이 프런티어 성능에 도달: In November 2024, Epoch AI estimated that open models took approximately one year to reach frontier performance (<v0>Ben Cottier et al. (Epoch AI), How far behind are open models?</v0> (published: 2024-11-04)). Its May 2026 analysis found that, since January 2026, leading open-weight models had lagged frontier closed models by an average of four months. On Epoch’s aggregate Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), the gap was eight points, which Epoch described as similar to the difference between GPT-5 and GPT-5.5 (<v1/> (published: 2026-05-29)). The gap depends on what is measured: six to seven months for cybersecurity capabilities (<v2/> (published: 2026-10-16)), and, in Håvard Tveit Ihle’s personal analysis, four to six months on public benchmarks versus eight to ten months on private benchmarks (<v3/> (published: 2026-05-28)). The best open-weight model also differs from the model you can actually run. Full DeepSeek-R1 has 671 billion parameters; personal PCs generally run the accompanying distilled models ranging from 1.5B to 70B (<v4>DeepSeek, DeepSeek-R1 repository</v4>). Ultimately, test candidates on the actual work to be assigned, recording the model version, prompt, execution environment, and number of repetitions (§10.4).
가중치가 있으면 모델 자체를 바꿀 수 있다. 특정 분야 데이터로 추가 학: Access to weights allows modification of the model itself. Common approaches include fine-tuning, further training on domain-specific data; quantization, reducing numerical precision to save memory; and distillation, training a smaller model on a larger model’s outputs. By freezing existing weights and training only small low-rank matrices, LoRA reduced trainable parameters 10,000-fold and GPU memory threefold compared with full fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B (<v0>Edward J. Hu et al., LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models</v0> (published: 2021-06-17)). The gpt-oss-120b model card also states that it can be fine-tuned on a single H100 node. Closed-weight models can be adjusted only through prompts, instruction files, and provider-supported fine-tuning, although much customization in vibe coding takes place at the context level (§6.3). Version retention differs too. OpenAI states that, barring safety or compliance issues, it gives at least six months’ notice before retiring generally available models and three months for specialized variants, while preview models may be retired with about two weeks’ notice. For example, o1-preview’s retirement was announced on April 28, 2025, and took effect on July 28 (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)). Prompts and agent settings tuned to one model must be rechecked after a model change. Open-weight models can keep running at the same version as long as their files are retained, making experiments easier to reproduce.
직접 실행하면 GPU 확보, 서빙 소프트웨어 업데이트, 모니터링, 보안,: Self-hosting makes the user responsible for securing GPUs, updating serving software, monitoring, security, and license compliance. The burden differs greatly between a local model for one person and a service for an entire team; §17.2 covers organizational operations. Pay particular attention to exposing servers. vLLM’s documentation states that its api-key option protects only /v1 routes, leaving routes such as /invocations and /tokenize accessible without a key. It recommends placing a reverse proxy, such as nginx, in front of the server to receive and forward requests while exposing only permitted routes (<v0/> (version: v0.19.1)). An authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-48746) allowing access without an API key was reported in vLLM’s OpenAI-compatible server. This attack applies when the server is exposed directly without a standards-compliant reverse proxy (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)). Getting started individually is straightforward. According to Ollama’s documentation, running Codex CLI with the oss option uses the local gpt-oss:20b model; other models can be specified with -m, and a context window of at least 32K tokens is recommended (<v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-15)).
위 명령은 문서에 나온 사용법을 옮긴 것이며, 이 원고를 쓰면서 실행한: The commands above reproduce documented usage; they were not executed as part of writing this manuscript. Local-model speed and quality vary greatly with PC specifications and the model, so test them on your own work first.
제공사 서버, 약관이 보관을 정함: Provider servers; retention governed by terms
고정비 중심, 가동률이 단가 좌우: Primarily fixed costs; unit cost depends on utilization
open-weight 최고 수준(평균 약 4개월 격차): Leading open-weight performance (approximately four months behind on average)

Even for sensitive data, self-hosting cannot be assumed safer without the ability to operate servers securely. Conversely, if an API’s contract and retention settings provide the required control, reducing the operational burden may be reasonable.
다음은 가상 사례다. 공개 전 실험 데이터를 다루는 연구실이 규정상 원본: Consider a hypothetical case. If a laboratory handling unpublished experimental data is prohibited from sending raw data to external services, it can assign work involving raw data to an open-weight model on a laboratory server, while sending general coding questions without that data to a closed-weight API (§5.4, routing).
이 선택은 한 번으로 끝나지 않는다. 성능 격차와 제공사 정책은 몇 개월: The choice is not permanent. Performance gaps and provider policies change over periods of months. Record the model and version, license, evaluation conditions, data-retention policy, responsible operator, and verification date, then reassess periodically. 모델 라우팅은 무엇이며, 왜 필요한가?: What is model routing, and why is it needed?
여러분들이 인공지능(AI)을 활용하여 보고서를 작성하거나 소프트웨어를 개: Think back to writing a report or developing software with artificial intelligence (AI), and consider two questions.
AI를 활용하는 과정에서 작업의 성격에 따라서 모델과 추론 수준을 다르게: Do you change the model and reasoning level according to the nature of the task?
모든 요청을 고성능 프론티어 모델에 보낼 필요가 있을까?: Does every request need to go to a powerful frontier model?
이번 절에서는 위 두 가지 질문에 대한 하나의 접근으로 모델 라우팅에 대: This section explores model routing as one approach to these questions.
보고서를 작성하는 과정 하나에서도 여러 가지의 하위 작업들이 존재하며,: Even writing one report involves subtasks requiring different amounts of cognitive effort. Developing ideas and planning a report require substantial effort, whereas correcting simple typos requires little. Since AI is also designed to think and make judgments in ways resembling people, the required reasoning level varies with the task.
많은 AI 기업들은 하나의 모델만 제공하는 것이 아니라 높은 성능을 보이: Many AI companies offer a range of models, from higher- to lower-performing ones, and describe appropriate tasks for each; see Section 1 of this chapter. For example, the OpenAI Developers website explains which tasks suit different models, from frontier models downward, and can recommend a model when users provide information about their task.
그림 1: 작업 유형과 우선순위를 입력하면 모델과 추론 수준을 추천하는: Figure 1: OpenAI’s model-selection guide recommends a model and reasoning level based on task type and priorities. Source: <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-22)
사실 고성능을 보여주는 프론티어 모델과 저성능 모델의 비용과 속도가 동일: If powerful frontier models and less capable models had identical costs and speeds, there would be little reason to worry about which model to use for a task. As Section 1 showed, however, models differ in cost and speed as well as capability. Project time and budgets are limited, so tasks need appropriately chosen models.
만약 요청하고자 하는 작업의 특성에 따라서 사용자의 요청을 적절한 모델로: Assigning user requests to suitable models based on their characteristics can bring substantial time and cost benefits. Otherwise, simple requests may waste resources on expensive, high-performing models, while complex requests assigned to inexpensive, less capable models may exceed those models’ abilities.
이러한 문제의식에서 출발하여 많은 관심을 받고 있는 것이 모델 라우팅(m: These concerns have drawn attention to model routing <v0/>: selecting and assigning the model best suited to a user’s request. This decision can be made before or after generation. Pre-generation routing does not send input directly to an arbitrary AI model; it assigns the work to the most suitable model based on the input and query characteristics. Post-generation selection is called cascading and is often discussed alongside routing. Cascading starts with a small, fast model and, if a quality assessment finds its result insufficient, progressively escalates to larger models capable of more complex work. Routing and cascading choose at different points but share the goal of assigning work to an appropriate model. The two approaches are not mutually exclusive and can be combined <v1/>.
먼저 모델 라우팅과 관련하여 Moslem과 Kelleher는 모델 라우팅: Moslem and Kelleher classify routing strategies into six paradigms: (1) difficulty-aware routing, (2) human preference aligned routing, (3) clustering-based routing, (4) reinforcement learning routing, (5) uncertainty-based routing, and (6) cascading <v0/>. Consult their paper for details of each approach.
Routes requests by estimating their complexity.
Routes requests using preference data derived from human feedback.
비지도 학습을 활용하여 사용자의 유사한 요청을 그룹화하여 모델을 라우팅한: Uses unsupervised learning to group similar user requests and route them.
정책 최적화(policy optimization), 밴딧(bandit m: Uses reinforcement learning, including policy optimization and bandit methods, to route requests.
Routes requests based on estimated model confidence.
순차적인 다중 모델 접근 방식으로, 작고 빠른 모델에 작업을 할당한 후: A sequential approach using multiple models: assign work to a small, fast model, assess the quality, and then route it to a larger model capable of handling more complex tasks if needed.
이러한 6가지 유형들은 사용자의 작업에 적합한 모델을 할당하기 위한 접근: These six categories organize approaches to assigning suitable models to users’ tasks. They are primarily selection strategies and often rely on rules or classifiers trained specifically for routing <v0/>. They do not have a general-purpose AI model directly plan the work and choose its models. Recent advances, however, have produced approaches in which a general-purpose AI model makes that decision itself. Shen and colleagues demonstrated that an AI model can plan tasks and connect them to suitable models rather than perform every task directly <v1/>. Routing through general-purpose AI models may be more useful than the preceding approaches when you use AI for your own work or software development.
앞서 기술한 내용을 토대로 모델 라우팅이 무엇인지는 알게 되었을 것이라고: The preceding discussion should clarify what model routing means. Applying it to your own work also requires learning its procedures and methods. This section uses OpenRouter, which supports routing among various AI models, to examine Auto Router, where AI analyzes a request’s type and difficulty and assigns a suitable model, and fallback strategies for handling errors.

All three problems are linked to the tokens entering and leaving each request, so an action aimed at one can worsen the other two. This section explains how to measure and manage cost, response speed, and usage limits together when using the models selected in §5.1–§5.4 in a real service. Routing and switching to alternative models are covered in §5.4; here, the model is assumed to have been chosen.
이 꼭지에 나오는 단가, 응답 시간, 토큰 수는 따로 출처를 밝힌 부분을: Except where a source is explicitly given, unit prices, response times, and token counts in this section are hypothetical values for illustration. Actual values vary by model and date, so focus on calculation methods and the sequence of decisions rather than the numbers themselves.

요청 한 건의 비용은 캐시되지 않은 입력 토큰, 캐시된 입력 토큰, 출력: The cost of one request is the sum of uncached input tokens, cached input tokens, and output tokens multiplied by their respective unit prices. Since the three prices differ, the cost impact of an equal increase in tokens depends on which category grows.
추론형 모델은 답하기 전에 만든 추론 토큰도 출력 토큰으로 요금을 매긴다: Reasoning models also bill reasoning tokens generated before an answer as output tokens. OpenAI’s documentation explains that reasoning tokens occupy the context window and are billed as output. If the output limit is reached first, input and reasoning costs may be incurred without a visible answer (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). A short visible answer can therefore be expensive; check the reasoning-token count separately in the response’s usage information.

Every request begins with the same 12,000 tokens of system instructions and textbook content, followed by a 200-token student question. For illustration, assume prices per million tokens of $1 for input, $0.25 for cached input, and $4 for output.
A. 매번 그대로 보내기: A. Send everything unchanged each time
B. 교재 부분을 캐시로 재사용하기: B. Reuse the textbook portion through caching
C. B에 더해 답변을 300토큰 안팎으로 정하기: C. In addition to B, target answers of around 300 tokens
한 달 6만 건은 학생 200명이 하루 10번씩 30일 동안 질문한다고: The monthly total of 60,000 requests assumes 200 students asking ten questions a day for 30 days. With the same model and question volume, operational changes alone brought cost below one-third of A’s. Conversely, when costs suddenly rise in production, investigate changes of this kind before focusing on the price list.
캐시에도 비용이 붙을 수 있다는 점은 따로 확인한다. OpenAI는 캐시: Check separately whether caching itself incurs charges. OpenAI discounts cached input reads by up to 95%, but models from GPT-5.6 onward separately charge for newly written cache tokens (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). The example above is simplified and excludes cache-write charges.
비용이 갑자기 늘었을 때 확인할 것: What to check when costs suddenly rise
입력이 길어졌는지 본다. 더 긴 자료를 넣었거나, 대화가 길어지면서 이전: Check whether input grew. Longer materials may have been added, or an expanding conversation may be resending the entire history with each request.
캐시가 쓰이고 있는지 본다. OpenAI의 프롬프트 캐시는 프롬프트의 앞: Check whether caching is being used. OpenAI’s prompt cache applies only when the prompt prefix matches an earlier request. For GPT-5.6 and later models, the minimum cacheable length is 1,024 tokens (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). Put recurring instructions and materials first and changing questions last. A changing value such as today’s date or a user name at the very beginning prevents a cache match.
출력이 길어졌는지 본다. 답변 길이 기준이 없거나 추론 토큰이 늘었을 수: Check whether output grew. There may be no answer-length criterion, or reasoning-token usage may have increased.
재시도가 늘었는지 본다. 실패한 요청을 다시 보낸 만큼 비용과 사용량 한: Check whether retries increased. Each resent request consumes both money and rate-limit capacity; see “Rate limits and 429 errors” below.

The first is covered in §5.1–§5.4; the second and third are this section’s focus.

사용자가 체감하는 응답 속도: Response speed as experienced by users
사용자가 느끼는 응답 속도는 두 값으로 나누어 본다. 하나는 요청을 보낸: User-perceived speed can be divided into two measures: time to first token (TTFT), from sending a request until the first character appears, and generation speed, the tokens produced per second afterward. Generation speed here measures only the period after the first token, unlike Artificial Analysis’s Output Speed, which includes the initial wait.
예를 들어 첫 응답 시간이 0.8초이고 생성 속도가 초당 80토큰인 모델: For example, assume a model with a TTFT of 0.8 seconds and a generation speed of 80 tokens per second. A 600-token answer takes approximately 8.3 seconds; a 300-token answer takes approximately 4.6 seconds. The answer-length criterion that reduced cost in the textbook-chatbot example thus also nearly halved total response time.
입력이 길다, 요청이 몰려 대기가 길다, 추론형 모델이 답하기 전에 추론: Long input, queues caused by request surges, or reasoning before answering
입력 줄이기, 캐시, 동시에 보내는 요청 수 조절: Reduce input, use caching, and control concurrent requests
답이 끝날 때까지 오래 걸린다: The answer takes a long time to finish
답변 길이 기준, 요약형 답변: Set an answer-length criterion or use concise summaries
캐시는 비용과 첫 응답 시간을 함께 줄인다. OpenAI Cookbook: Caching reduces both cost and time to first response. The OpenAI Cookbook explains that caching applies automatically to prompts longer than 1,024 tokens and can reduce latency by up to 80% for long prompts exceeding 10,000 tokens (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)).
스트리밍은 답이 완성되기를 기다리지 않고 만들어지는 대로 보여 주는 방식: Streaming displays an answer as it is generated instead of waiting for completion. In the example above, without streaming the user sees a blank screen for 8.3 seconds; with streaming, reading begins after 0.8 seconds. Cost and total response time remain unchanged, while the period spent looking at a blank screen shrinks.
배치 처리는 반대로 속도를 내주고 비용을 얻는 방식이다. OpenAI의: Batch processing makes the opposite trade-off, exchanging speed for lower cost. OpenAI’s Batch API groups requests for asynchronous processing, advertises 50% lower cost than the synchronous API and separate, higher rate limits, and states that each batch completes within 24 hours (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). This suits generating assignment feedback in bulk, but not live classroom questions.
모델을 직접 운영하는 경우(§5.3)에는 서버가 여러 요청을 한꺼번에 묶: When self-hosting models (§5.3), how the server groups requests affects cost. PagedAttention, the research underlying vLLM, manages variable-sized per-request memory, the KV cache, in blocks analogous to operating-system pages, reducing waste and batching more requests together. It reported two to four times the throughput of systems such as FasterTransformer and Orca at the same latency (<v0>Woosuk Kwon et al., Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention</v0> (published: 2023-09-12; SOSP 2023)). Processing more requests on the same hardware lowers per-request cost, but overly large batches can increase individual waiting times.
응답 시간은 평균만 보면 놓치는 것이 있다. 요청 100건을 응답 시간: Average response time can hide important differences. Sort 100 requests by response time: the 50th value, the median or p50, represents the typical experience, while the 95th value, p95, reflects the experience of the slowest 5%. A reasonable average with a long p95 suggests that some requests spend a long time in queues or contain unusually long inputs.
AI providers limit how much an account may send within a period. OpenAI applies limits such as requests per minute (RPM), requests per day (RPD), tokens per minute (TPM), and tokens per day (TPD); reaching any one of them blocks requests. For example, with a limit of 20 requests per minute, twenty short requests of only 100 tokens each can exhaust the request allowance far below the token limit. Limits apply at organization and project level, rather than per user (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)).
한도는 계정의 사용 등급에 따라 달라진다. 확인 시점 기준으로 OpenA: Limits vary by account usage tier. As of verification, OpenAI’s paid tiers were Build, Launch, and Grow, with automatic promotion when an organization’s total credit purchases meet the threshold (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)).
막힌 원인에 따라 대응이 다르다: The response depends on the cause of the blockage
분당 또는 일일 요청 수, 토큰 수: Per-minute or daily request or token limits
요청량을 짧은 시간에 급격히 늘림: A sudden surge in request volume
요청량을 줄였다가 천천히 늘리면 풀린다: Reduce volume, then increase it gradually
크레딧 잔액, 지출 한도, 사용 한도: Credit balance, spending cap, or usage allowance
풀리지 않는다. 충전하거나 한도를 바꿔야 한다: No. Add credits or change the limit
표의 근거는 OpenAI의 오류 코드 문서다(<v0/> (확인: 2026: The table is based on OpenAI’s error-code documentation (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). It distinguishes billing-related errors using <v1/> and explains that the broader <v2/> category may be <v3/>. For example, an account without prepaid credits can receive 429 even for a single request. The Python SDK reports 429 as <v4/>, which sounds like excessive request volume, but the error code is <v5/> and repeated attempts will not resolve it. This is why error codes must be checked before retrying.
재시도는 횟수와 간격을 정해 두고: Set retry limits and intervals in advance
429는 “지금은 받을 수 없다”는 신호다. 실패하자마자 다시 보내면 서: A 429 response means “We cannot accept this now.” Immediate retries only increase server load and consume more rate-limit capacity. OpenAI’s documentation and Google’s Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) guidance recommend the following approach.
오류 코드를 먼저 확인한다. 크레딧, 지출 한도, 사용 한도 오류처럼 사: Check the error code first. Do not retry errors requiring user action, such as exhausted credits, spending caps, or usage allowances; report them immediately (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)).
응답에 <v0/> 헤더가 있으면 그 시간을 최소 대기 시간으로 삼고, 여: If a response contains a <v0/> header, use it as the minimum wait and add a small random delay so multiple clients do not retry simultaneously (same documentation).
헤더가 없으면 1초, 2초, 4초처럼 대기 시간을 두 배씩 늘리고(지수: Without that header, double the delay, for example one, two, then four seconds, using exponential backoff, and add random jitter. Without randomness, requests that fail together will surge again together.
재시도 횟수에 상한을 둔다. Google SRE Book은 요청 하나당: Cap attempts. The Google SRE Book limits each request to at most three attempts and combines this with a retry budget that permits retries only while they remain below 10% of requests across clients. It explains that a three-attempt cap alone can nearly triple requests in the worst case, whereas adding the 10% ratio cap limits the increase to around 1.1-fold (<v0/> (Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 21)).
막힐 요청은 미리 줄인다. 같은 장은 각 클라이언트가 최근 2분 동안 보: Reduce requests likely to be rejected before sending them. The same chapter introduces adaptive throttling: each client tracks requests sent and accepted over the last two minutes and begins rejecting some of its own requests when sent requests exceed K times accepted requests, for example twice as many. A small service can begin by capping concurrent requests, for example at five.
재시도가 여러 곳에서 겹치지 않게 하는 것도 중요하다. OpenAI의 공: Avoid stacking retries in multiple layers. OpenAI’s official SDK automatically retries eligible 429 and 503 responses. Its documentation recommends disabling SDK retries or including them in the attempt count if the application manages retries itself (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). The OpenAI Python SDK automatically retries certain errors twice by default (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). Wrapping this in three application-level attempts can send one request as many as nine times.
그림 3: 429 또는 503 응답을 받았을 때의 재시도 판단 흐름. 크: Figure 3: Retry decisions after a 429 or 503 response. Do not retry credit or spending-limit problems; otherwise, respect waiting intervals and retry only within the attempt limit. The cap follows the example in Chapter 21 of the Google SRE Book.
운영 신호에 따른 대응 규칙: Response rules based on operational signals
앞에서 다룬 숫자는 그 자체보다 무엇이 바뀌었는지 알려 주는 신호로 쓸: The numbers discussed above are more useful as signals of change than in isolation. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework includes MEASURE, which analyzes and monitors AI risks, and MANAGE, which regularly allocates resources to respond to measured risks, among its core functions (<v0/> (published: 2023-01-26; Section 5)). Although the framework does not directly address cost and response time, I consider its structure of ongoing measurement linked to predefined responses applicable to this section’s operating rules.
요청마다 남길 기록: What to log for each request
어느 모델이 비용을 쓰는지: Which model is consuming the budget
입력, 캐시된 입력, 출력, 추론 토큰 수: Input, cached-input, output, and reasoning-token counts
토큰 수와 단가로 계산: Calculated from token counts and unit prices
첫 응답 시간, 전체 응답 시간: Time to first response and total response time
재시도 예산을 넘었는지: Whether the retry budget was exceeded
입력과 출력 중 무엇이 늘었는지, 같은 자료를 반복해 보내는지, 재시도가: Whether input or output grew, identical materials are being resent, or retries increased
입력 정리, 답변 길이 기준, 반복되는 앞부분은 캐시: Organize input, set answer-length criteria, and cache recurring prefixes
프롬프트 앞부분에 매번 바뀌는 값이 들어갔는지: Whether changing values were introduced into the prompt prefix
바뀌지 않는 내용은 앞에, 바뀌는 내용은 뒤에: Put stable content first and changing content last
입력 길이, 대기열 길이, 추론형 모델인지: Input length, queue length, and whether the model reasons before answering
입력 줄이기, 캐시, 동시 요청 수 조절, 스트리밍: Reduce input, use caching, control concurrency, and stream responses
오류 코드, 동시 요청 수, 재시도 방식: Error codes, concurrency, and retry behavior
크레딧이나 지출 한도 문제면 충전하고 알림. 속도 문제면 동시 요청 상한: For credit or spending-cap problems, add credits and notify the user. For rate-related issues, cap concurrency, increase waiting intervals, and apply a retry budget. Batch nonurgent work
요청이 몰리는 시간대, 급하지 않은 작업이 겹쳤는지: Request peaks and overlapping nonurgent work
중요한 요청 먼저 처리, 나머지는 미루거나 배치로, 사용자 안내: Prioritize important requests, defer or batch others, and inform users
월 예산이 예상보다 빨리 줄어듦: The monthly budget runs out faster than expected
사용자별, 기능별 한도, 값싼 모델로 나누어 보내기(§5.4): Per-user and per-feature limits; route some requests to cheaper models (§5.4)
Google SRE Book은 요청마다 중요도(criticality)를: The Google SRE Book describes assigning each request one of four criticality levels, CRITICAL_PLUS, CRITICAL, SHEDDABLE_PLUS, and SHEDDABLE, and rejecting lower-criticality requests first when capacity is insufficient. SHEDDABLE_PLUS is the default for batch work that can be retried minutes or hours later (<v0/> (Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 21)). In an educational service, live classroom questions could receive the highest priority, while bulk assignment feedback or advance summaries receive lower priority. Sending low-priority work to batches from the outset saves both cost and rate-limit capacity.
Use streaming to display the first characters sooner.
When waits grow, show the remaining time or queue position.
한도에 걸리면 빈 화면이나 알아보기 어려운 오류 대신 “요청이 많아 잠시: When limits are reached, give an actionable message such as “We are receiving many requests. Please try again shortly,” rather than a blank screen or an obscure error.
다른 모델로 대신 답했다면 그 사실을 알릴지 미리 정한다. 같은 서비스: Decide in advance whether to disclose responses from an alternative model, since answer quality may vary within the same service.
서비스가 커지면 이 규칙들을 코드 곳곳에 흩어 두기보다 모델 호출이 모두: As a service grows, these rules are easier to manage in one gateway through which all model calls pass than scattered throughout the code. The open-source LiteLLM provides one OpenAI-format interface for more than 100 LLM providers, with project- and user-level cost tracking and spending management, load balancing, retries, and fallback models (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-11)). 마지막으로 함께 토론할 질문을 남긴다. AI 서비스의 예산과 서버 자원이: Finally, consider this discussion question. With limited budgets and server resources, should an AI service give every user the same powerful model? Or is it fairer and more efficient to route requests among cheaper and more capable models according to importance and difficulty?
같은 수업을 듣는 학생들이 요청 시각이나 분류에 따라 다른 품질의 답변을: Is it fair for students in the same course to receive different-quality answers depending on request timing or classification?
요청의 중요도는 누가, 어떤 기준으로 정해야 하는가?: Who should determine request criticality, and by what criteria?
대체 모델로 답했거나 답변을 짧게 줄였다면 사용자에게 그 사실을 알려야: Should users be told when an alternative model answered or an answer was shortened?

- Use streaming and measure time to first token and total response time in seconds.

한 대학원 연구실이 여러 기상 관측소의 기온 데이터를 모아 분석한다고 하: Suppose a graduate laboratory is analyzing temperature data collected from several weather stations. This illustrative example is shared across Chapter 6. Each station supplies a CSV with dates and temperatures, and the laboratory has a small program that reads the files and calculates monthly mean temperatures. One row from the Busan station contains “-” instead of a temperature, indicating a day without an observation. The program stops with a single English error message, halting calculations for the other stations too. The researcher managing the data asks a coding agent the following.
같은 연구실 동료라면 이 한 문장으로 충분할 수 있다. 어떤 파일이 문제: That sentence might suffice for a colleague in the same laboratory, who knows which file caused trouble and can ask questions when uncertain. An agent is different: it opens files, changes code, and runs tests on its own, then stops when it judges the work complete. The request leaves several questions unanswered. What should be validated? Should a row containing “-” be skipped or reported as an error? What constitutes completion? What happens if a file uses a unit other than Celsius? The agent fills these gaps with assumptions, and only after receiving the result does the researcher discover that it differs from what was wanted.
소프트웨어 공학에서 요구사항(requirement)은 사용자가 문제를 풀: In software engineering, a requirement is a condition or capability a user needs to solve a problem or achieve an objective, or one a system must possess to satisfy a contract, standard, or other formal document. The IEEE Computer Society’s Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK) introduces this definition and describes a requirement, at its most basic, as a property software must exhibit to solve a real-world problem. <v0>Hironori Washizaki, ed., Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK Guide) Version 4.0</v0> (2024; Chapter 1, Section 1.1). Requirements engineering systematically handles these requirements: identifying needs, reconciling conflicts, documenting specifications, validating them, and managing changes. The international standard ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 specifies processes for developing requirements throughout the system and software life cycle and the contents of the associated documentation. <v1/> (published: 2018-11).
요구사항은 프롬프트와 겹치는 부분이 있지만 다루는 질문이 다르다. 프롬프: Requirements overlap with prompts but address different questions. A prompt determines how to instruct a model for the current run. Requirements establish why the work is being done, what counts as success, and what is permitted, remaining the basis for assessment until completion. Even if a prompt is revised repeatedly, unchanged requirements allow results to be judged consistently. Prompting techniques were covered in §3.1, and methods and tools for writing a spec before code in §3.4. Whereas §3.4 examined when to use a spec, this section examines how to create one and what to include so the agent knows when to finish and people can assess the result.
이 절에서 정한 내용은 6장의 나머지 절에서 다시 쓰인다. 완료 기준은: The decisions made here are reused throughout Chapter 6. Completion criteria become stopping conditions in §6.2; specifications and change records become context for the next run in §6.3; and agreed points for stopping to ask become human-intervention branches in §6.4.
요구사항 엔지니어링은 문서 한 장을 쓰는 일로 끝나지 않는다. 그 과정을: Requirements engineering involves more than writing one document. Sources divide its activities somewhat differently. SWEBOK describes elicitation, analysis, specification, validation, and management. <v0>Hironori Washizaki, ed., Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK Guide) Version 4.0</v0> (2024; Chapter 1). This section follows those five stages.
ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 groups the same activities into processes. Its first edition, published in 2011, divides requirements work into two main processes and additional activities. The main processes are stakeholder requirements definition and requirements analysis. The former elicits, defines, analyzes, and maintains stakeholders’ requirements; the latter transforms them into technical requirements the system must satisfy. Requirements activities within other technical processes, including design, verification, and validation, and requirements management, including change management and measurement, are added to these (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2011, first edition published: 2011-12-01; Chapter 6).
두 문헌의 구분은 요구하는 쪽과 만드는 쪽이 나뉘어 있고 문서가 여러 단: Both sources assume development in which requesters and builders are separate and documentation passes through multiple stages. When assigning a small task to an agent, the requester and assessor are often the same person, and one document may suffice. This section therefore retains SWEBOK’s five stages while emphasizing what particularly matters for agent work at each stage. The following table maps them to the two sources and identifies the narrower focus used here.
이해관계자를 작업을 맡기는 사람으로 좁히고, 바로 쓸 수 있는 질문 목록: Treat the person assigning the task as the stakeholder and provide immediately usable questions.
이해관계자 요구사항의 분석과 유지, 요구사항 분석 프로세스: Analysis and maintenance of stakeholder requirements; requirements analysis process
Focus on reconciling conflicts and specifying what is out of scope.
요구사항 정의 활동, 명세 문서(StRS, SyRS, SRS): Requirements-definition activities and specification documents (StRS, SyRS, SRS)
Combine the documentation into one specification for the agent.
다른 기술 프로세스의 검증과 확인: Verification and validation within other technical processes
Focus on recording completion criteria together with assessment methods.
요구사항 관리 (변경 관리, 측정): Requirements management, including change management and measurement
Retain change records and checks of related clauses.
Both sources view requirements work as iterative rather than something completed once. In practice, stages do not flow in only one direction: writing a specification often leads back to asking questions.
요구는 처음부터 완성된 모습으로 주어지지 않는다. 부탁하는 사람도 자신이: Needs do not arrive fully formed. The requester often does not yet know everything they want. The first step is therefore to identify gaps through questions. These questions apply to any task.
이 결과를 누가, 어디에 쓰는가?: Who will use this result, and where?
입력은 어떤 모양이고, 어디에 있는가?: What form does the input take, and where is it located?
실패하거나 예상하지 못한 입력이 오면 어떻게 하는가?: What should happen on failure or unexpected input?
고쳐도 되는 것과 고치면 안 되는 것은 무엇인가?: What may be changed, and what must remain unchanged?
아직 정하지 못한 것은 무엇인가?: What has not yet been decided?
말로 묻는 것만으로 부족하면 실제 자료를 함께 본다. 문제가 된 파일 하: If verbal questions are insufficient, examine actual materials together. One problematic file and one example of the desired result can reveal needs that did not emerge in discussion. Another approach is to have the agent ask about unclear points and missing cases before starting work. Some tools introduced in §3.4 provide this questioning stage as a feature.
분석과 조정: 부딪치는 요구와 범위 정하기: Analysis and negotiation: resolving conflicts and defining scope
모은 요구를 나란히 놓으면 서로 부딪치는 것이 보인다. “문제 있는 파일: Putting collected needs side by side reveals conflicts. “Calculate as much as possible even from problematic files” is difficult to reconcile with “Never include incorrect values.” Decide which takes priority and what will not be done this time. Defining what is out of scope matters as much as defining what is in scope, because otherwise the agent will make those decisions itself.
명세: 판정할 수 있는 문장으로 쓰기: Specification: writing statements that can be assessed
합의한 내용을 문서로 적는다. 에이전트에게 맡길 작업이라면 적어도 목표,: Document what has been agreed. For agent tasks, include at least the goal, constraints, completion criteria, and stopping conditions. Good requirements have several properties. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 lists necessity, implementation independence, lack of ambiguity, verifiability, and traceability for individual requirements, and completeness and consistency for the set. Three are especially important for agents: each statement should have one clear meaning, compliance should be checkable, and requirements should not contradict one another. “Filter out strange values” leaves both “strange” and whether to discard or report them undefined. “Raise NOT_A_NUMBER if a temperature field contains a nonnumeric value” can be checked directly by supplying a file. After drafting, search for words such as “appropriately,” “well,” “sufficiently,” and “strange,” and replace any that remain with assessment criteria.
검증: 완료 기준을 판정 방법으로 바꾸기: Verification: turning completion criteria into checks
완료 기준은 누가 무엇으로 판정할지와 함께 적는다. 자동 테스트로 판정할: Record who will assess each completion criterion and how. Turn criteria suitable for automated assessment into tests. SWEBOK calls agreeing on tests in advance acceptance criteria-based specification. It proposes agreeing before coding on the tests that must pass, with at least one failing on the current code to establish a reason for change. <v0>Hironori Washizaki, ed., Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK Guide) Version 4.0</v0> (2024; Chapter 1, Section 4.3). In the temperature example, three of the initial four tests failed, providing exactly this starting point. For criteria difficult to express as tests, specify the assessor, assessment questions, and evidence. Automated checks are fast and repeatable but cover only predefined cases. Human judgment can assess qualities difficult to test, but takes time and may vary by person. Make human assessment questions particularly concrete.
변경 관리: 바꾼 이유를 남기고 연결된 조항을 함께 보기: Change management: recording reasons and checking related clauses
요구는 일하는 도중에도 바뀐다. 명세를 고칠 때는 언제, 무엇을, 왜 바: Needs change during work. When revising a specification, record when, what, and why it changed, and who decided. Other people or agents can then understand the reason later. When one clause changes, inspect related clauses too. Broadening what is permitted while leaving a prohibition unchanged creates contradictory statements within the specification.
에이전트에게 맡길 때 더 챙길 것: Additional considerations when delegating to an agent
사람이 AI와 대화하며 코드를 만들 때는 요구사항이 뒤늦게 생기는 일이: Requirements often emerge late when people develop code through conversation with AI. The vibe-coding video study introduced in §3.4, accepted at ESEC/FSE 2026, likewise found that many participants developed new requirements after seeing output. <v0>Yi-Hung Chou et al., Building Software by Rolling the Dice: A Qualitative Study of Vibe Coding</v0> (published: 2025-12-30). Conversational tools can accommodate this because people inspect each result and revise the next request. Delegating several stages at once to an agent reduces these opportunities. Establish the following three things before work begins.
첫째, 완료 기준을 에이전트가 바꿀 수 없는 곳에 둔다. Anthropi: First, put completion criteria where the agent cannot change them. Anthropic engineer Justin Young documented a failure in long development work split across agent sessions: later agents saw existing progress and declared the work complete. He created a file listing every feature to implement, initially marking all as failing. Subsequent agents could change a status to passing only after testing the feature and were forbidden to delete or modify tests <v0/> (published: 2025-11-26). If agents can change the criteria, they can lower the bar instead of completing the work.
둘째, 행동의 범위와 권한을 정한다. OpenAI의 에이전트 구축 안내서: Second, define the scope of actions and permissions. OpenAI’s agent-building guide recommends assigning each tool a low, medium, or high risk rating based on whether it is read-only, reversible, requires particular permissions, or has financial consequences <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
셋째, 멈추는 조건과 사람에게 넘기는 시점을 정한다. 같은 안내서는 반복: Third, define stopping conditions and human handoff points. The same guide recommends termination conditions, retry limits, and human checks before irreversible or consequential actions. Human developers generally stop and ask when documentation does not cover a situation; agents may continue. Specifications for agents should therefore state what they may decide independently and where they must stop.
앞 절의 단계를 기온 데이터 작업에 그대로 적용해 보자. 데이터는 설명용: Apply the preceding stages to the temperature-data task. The observations are fabricated for illustration. Each of the Seoul, Busan, and Jeju stations supplies one CSV covering August 1–5, 2026. The first row contains column names (<v0/>), followed by one row per day. The fourth line of the Busan file contains “-” instead of a temperature.
First, ask the researcher the elicitation questions.
이 함수의 결과를 누가, 어디에 쓰는가?: Who uses this function’s output, and for what?
The researcher uses it to calculate monthly mean temperatures by station.
입력 파일은 어떤 모양인가?: What does an input file look like?
The first row is <v0/>; dates use <v1/>, and temperatures are numerical Celsius values.
빈 파일, 기온 열이 없는 파일, 기온 칸에 숫자가 아닌 값이 있는 파일: Empty files, files without a temperature column, and files with nonnumeric values in temperature fields.
문제 파일을 만나면 어떻게 하는가?: What should happen when a problematic file is encountered?
Report the problem. Do not silently skip problematic rows.
고쳐도 되는 것과 안 되는 것은?: What may and may not be changed?
The reading function may change. The assessment test file must not change.
How to handle files recorded in other units.
마지막 답이 분석과 조정 단계의 핵심이다. 연구원은 미국 관측소에서 화씨: The final answer is central to analysis and negotiation. The researcher knows that files using Fahrenheit may arrive from a US station, but has not decided whether to convert them to Celsius. Since conversion is straightforward, omitting this fact from the specification may lead the agent to convert automatically, making a decision that belongs to the researcher. Place it outside the current scope and require the agent to stop and ask when such a file arrives.
Organizing the answers yields the following specification.
“Input validation” in the original request has become three named error types. Automated tests assess the first completion criterion using four cases: a valid file, an empty file, a file without a temperature column, and a file containing “missing” in a temperature field. The prohibition on changing tests is needed for the reason illustrated by Young’s case above. The second criterion cannot be assessed through string comparison and is written as a question for a person. Without it, the agent could meet the first criterion with a one-line error containing neither filename nor line number.
저자는 이 명세를 실제로 Codex에게 맡겨 보았다(Codex Deskt: The author actually assigned this specification to Codex (Codex Desktop 0.171.0-alpha.13, model gpt-6-luna, Windows, executed: 2026-11-20). The only instruction was “Follow the rules in AGENTS.md and carry out the work in SPEC.md.” AGENTS.md contained short rules to read the specification and progress record before starting, run tests after each change, and act according to the assessment. One run cannot support generalization, but it showed where each clause was used. Because the assessment script could not find Python in the agent’s environment, a person ran it in a terminal and recorded the result.
에이전트는 먼저 명세와 진행 기록을 읽겠다고 밝힌 뒤 코드를 고쳤다. 명: The agent first stated that it would read the specification and progress record, then changed the code. The three lines under required work became three corresponding code errors. Predetermined error names kept the specification, tests, and code consistent.
작업 도중 화씨로 기록된 덴버 관측소 파일(<v0/>)을 넣고 모든 관측: During work, the researcher added a Denver-station file recorded in Fahrenheit (<v0/>) and requested averages for all stations. The agent checked its unit before calculating, found the disallowed <v1/> column, and said it had stopped calculating averages as instructed. It asked how to handle the Denver file. This was the out-of-scope clause taking effect.
연구원이 화씨를 섭씨로 바꿔도 된다고 정하고, 허용한 기온 열에 <v0/: The researcher permitted Fahrenheit-to-Celsius conversion, added <v0/> to allowed temperature columns, and documented the conversion rule. The agent noticed that a sentence under prohibited work still forbade unit conversion. Because the clauses conflicted, it stopped rather than deciding independently. After the researcher added the exception “However, the Fahrenheit conversion specified under required work is permitted,” the agent implemented conversion, and all five tests, including the added Fahrenheit case, passed at once. This demonstrated the practical need to check related clauses during change management.
마지막으로 사람이 둘째 완료 기준을 판정했다. 프로그램은 <v0/>를 출: Finally, a person assessed the second completion criterion. The program printed <v0/>. The author immediately recognized which file needed correction but was unsure whether 4 was a line number and what was wrong on that line. The automated assessment passed, while the human assessment passed only halfway. A subsequent specification could make the readability criterion more concrete: “Include the filename, line number, and problematic value in the error message.” This is why a separate human-assessed criterion was needed.
실행에서 쓰인 곳: Where it was used in execution
고치고 테스트하고, 통과하자 멈춰서 사람의 확인을 기다림: Edited and tested, then stopped after passing to await human confirmation
명세, 진행 기록, 바꾼 기록: Specification, progress records, and change records
새 대화의 에이전트가 기록만 읽고 상황을 이어받음: A fresh agent session reconstructed the situation from records alone
화씨 파일과 부딪친 조항 앞에서 멈추고 사람에게 물음: Stopped and asked a person when encountering the Fahrenheit file and conflicting clauses
최근 동향: 명세를 누가 쓰고 누가 판정하나: Recent developments: who writes and assesses specifications?
요구사항, 설계, 작업 목록을 코드보다 먼저 쓰고 사람이 검토하게 하는: Section §3.4 covered tools that write requirements, designs, and task lists before code for human review, and their differences. Here, the focus is on who establishes completion criteria and who assesses them.
Anthropic의 Prithvi Rajasekaran은 오래 걸리는 애: Anthropic’s Prithvi Rajasekaran described an experiment dividing lengthy application development among three agents responsible for planning, generation, and evaluation. The planning agent expanded a brief request into a product specification. Before code was written for each unit of work, the generator and evaluator agreed on what would constitute completion, which the author called a sprint contract. Each evaluation criterion had a threshold; failing even one meant that unit of work failed. Subjective criteria such as design quality became questions such as “Does the whole feel coherent?” for the evaluator to score <v0/> (published: 2026-03-24). Rather than people setting completion criteria once at the start, agents established them for each work unit. Turning hard-to-test criteria into assessment questions parallels the second criterion in the temperature example.
OpenAI의 Ryan Lopopolo는 사람이 코드를 직접 쓰지 않고: OpenAI’s Ryan Lopopolo described a team that delegated product development to Codex without writing code themselves. People set priorities, translated user feedback into acceptance criteria, and checked results. Instead of prescribing implementation details, they defined mandatory conditions and enforced them through automated checks <v0/> (published: 2026-02-11). Specifying what must hold without constraining how it is achieved aligns with implementation independence, one property of good requirements in the standard. As the author acknowledges, this is the experience of one team and repository and cannot simply be generalized.
연구에서도 에이전트를 위한 요구사항을 따로 다루기 시작했다. Pierre: Research has also begun treating requirements for agents as a distinct topic. Pierre Dantas and colleagues systematically reviewed 38 studies on specification, verification, and enforcement for LLM agents and identified specification as a bottleneck. They named translating natural-language requirements into formal specifications without losing meaning as a major open problem and rated the certainty of evidence for seven of nine key claims as very low. <v0>Pierre Dantas et al., Toward Safe LLM Agents: A Survey of Specification, Verification, and Enforcement</v0> (published: 2026-10-20). The manuscript remains under review, and experiments have not yet sufficiently established which ways of specifying agent requirements are effective.
교육에서 요구사항 엔지니어링 활용하기, 그리고 정리: Requirements engineering in education, and a summary
요구사항을 먼저 정하고 일을 시작하는 순서는 교육 설계에서 익숙한 방식과: Defining requirements before starting work resembles a familiar approach in educational design. Backward design, proposed by Wiggins and McTighe, first identifies desired learning outcomes, then determines evidence for assessing whether learners achieved them, and only afterward plans learning activities. They advise teachers to think like assessors before designing units and lessons. <v0>Jay McTighe and Grant Wiggins, Improve Curriculum, Assessment, and Instruction Using the Understanding by Design Framework</v0> (2014). Starting with activities can produce a busy course without clear evidence of learning. Starting an agent task by prescribing procedures can produce a similar problem: many files change, but there is no criterion for deciding whether the work is finished.
문제 파일을 걸러 내고 알리는 함수: A function that rejects problematic files and reports why
자동 테스트, 오류 메시지 판정 질문: Automated tests and questions for assessing error messages
CSV 형식, 테스트 수정 금지: CSV format and prohibition on changing tests
화씨 파일이면 멈추고 묻기: Stop and ask when a Fahrenheit file arrives
저자는 2026년 2학기에 섬 지역 고등학생을 위한 교과 A의 수업 자료: The author made similar decisions repeatedly while developing materials for Subject A for island high-school students in the second semester of 2026. Because participating schools were spread across several islands, examples were to represent regions evenly, and comparisons that might make students from particular regions uncomfortable were excluded. These were learner-informed constraints. When slides and student activity materials disagreed, the final activity materials were designated authoritative, establishing one reference document for assessment. Reasons were also recorded for leaving polished slides untouched and preserving blank space under quizzes, intentionally included to prevent answers from showing through. Recording prohibited changes and their rationale preserves decisions even when another person revises the materials. “Use consistent font sizes” became easier to check when rewritten as “Body text at least 28 points; sources 20 points.” Aligning terminology across the contents, slide titles, and summary slides addressed consistency across requirements. When dividing lessons, the author rewrote learning objectives before slides: the first step of backward design.
교원 연수 과정을 설계할 때는 따라야 할 위쪽 기준이 더 분명하다. 저자: Teacher-training design has more explicit upstream criteria. When the author designed training for AI lead teachers, the commissioning organization’s standard plan and teacher-competency framework served that role. After writing each course’s content, the author mapped every item to a provision in these references and supplemented unsupported areas. This is traceability: every requirement should lead back to an upstream source. Learning elements were selected only within the standard plan’s scope, and generic descriptions replaced tool names so that changing tools during delivery would not conflict with the proposal. These requirements specify what to achieve without binding the implementation. The planning rationale was rewritten around the current year’s project objectives rather than copied from last year’s framework, then each sentence was checked against course content. Revising downstream documents when upstream criteria change is change management; checking supporting evidence is verification.
교육 현장에서 AI에게 일을 맡기는 경우는 앞으로 더 늘어날 것이다. 교: Delegating work to AI will become more common in education. Teachers collaborate with AI on learning materials, assessment items, and draft feedback; schools and education offices use it for training and curriculum documents. Requirements engineering can be applied at three levels.
첫째, 교사가 AI에게 일을 맡길 때 명세를 먼저 쓰는 습관이다. 성취기: First, teachers can develop the habit of writing a specification before assigning work to AI. Achievement standards and learning objectives become goals, rubrics become completion criteria, and learner levels and teaching conditions become constraints. Distinguishing automatically checkable criteria, such as length, format, and concepts covered, from human judgments, such as suitability for students or language disadvantaging a group, clarifies what to inspect in the result. Decisions AI must not make, such as judgments about students or grades, belong under prohibited work and stopping conditions.
Second, check traceability in documents governed by upstream criteria. Curricula, training programs, and proposals must follow sources such as achievement standards and competency frameworks. Adding a step to map every sentence in an AI draft to its supporting criterion helps prevent plausible but unsupported content.
셋째, 학생 교육이다. 학생이 AI에게 과제를 맡기기 전에 무엇을 원하는: Third, teach students this approach. Having students state what they want, what counts as finished, and how to check the result before delegating an assignment to AI is itself an exercise in problem definition and assessment design. It transfers the thinking backward design asks of teachers into students’ ways of working with AI.
기온 데이터 예시에서 던진 질문을 다른 작업에 옮겨 쓸 수 있는 틀로 정: The questions from the temperature example can be generalized into the following template for other tasks. A small, disposable task may need only a goal and completion criteria. Fill in more fields as more people share the result or errors become harder to reverse.
이 절의 내용에는 한계가 있다. 명세를 자세히 쓸수록 쓰고 검토하는 시간: This section has limitations. More detailed specifications take more time to write and review; disproportionate documentation for a small change can leave people reading documents longer than code. The temperature specification is a small, single-function example; larger work requires specifications divided into work units. How much specifications improve agent outcomes also remains insufficiently established. The questions and template here synthesize standards, official guidance, and practical cases; the author’s execution record describes one run using one tool.
명세에 완료 기준과 멈추는 규칙을 적었으니, 다음 질문은 그 기준으로 에: Having specified completion criteria and stopping rules, the next question is how to run an agent’s iterations against them and when to stop. Section §6.2 continues this discussion.
