6장의 공통 예시에서는 관측소별 기온 파일을 읽는 함수에 입력 검사를 넣: Chapter 6’s shared example assigns a coding agent the task of adding input validation to a function that reads station temperature files. Simply telling it to “keep fixing it until the tests pass” leaves unspecified what to check, how many revisions to allow, and which failures require stopping. The agent may repeat unsuccessful changes or report completion while leaving parts unchecked. Passing tests also establishes correctness only within their coverage.
이 절의 질문은 세 가지다. 1) 에이전트에게 다시 시도하게 할지 멈추게: This section asks three questions. (1) What determines whether the agent should retry or stop? (2) How many retries should be allowed, and why? (3) Should retries use the same model? Section 6.1 covers writing completion criteria, 6.3 covers information supplied on each attempt, and 6.4 covers approvals and branches after success or stopping. General model selection, routing, and cost management follow Sections 5.1, 5.4, and 5.5.
루프 엔지니어링이 다루는 반복: The repetition addressed by loop engineering
코딩 에이전트는 한 번 호출되면 모델이 도구를 부르고 그 결과를 읽는 과: A coding agent repeatedly calls tools and reads their results within one invocation. Lulla and colleagues call this an agent loop, distinguishing it from loop engineering, which constructs the outer structure that starts an agent loop, verifies its result, and starts it again. Running tests and revising changes within one session belongs to the agent loop; starting a new session after each failed build belongs to loop engineering. Synthesizing practitioner materials, they define loop engineering as designing control structures that repeatedly invoke coding agents on schedules or events, with each run bounded by machine-assessable termination conditions (<v0>Jai Lal Lulla et al., Loop Engineering: Building Blocks, Adoption, and Impact</v0> (arXiv v3, 2026-10-22; Sections 2.1–2.2)).
Lulla 등에 따르면 이 용어는 2026년 6월 초 실무자들의 글에서: According to Lulla and colleagues, the term first appeared in practitioner writing in early June 2026 and spread rapidly (<v0>Jai Lal Lulla et al., Loop Engineering: Building Blocks, Adoption, and Impact</v0> (arXiv v3, 2026-10-22; abstract, Section 2.2)). Addy Osmani describes it as designing a system to replace the person who would otherwise give an agent its next instruction (<v1/> (published: 2026-06-07)). A simple outer-loop example is Geoffrey Huntley’s shell loop <v2/>, which continually feeds the same instruction into fresh sessions without a stopping condition (<v3/> (published: 2025-07-14)). Here, loop engineering means adding termination conditions, retry limits, and records to such outer repetition.
Lulla 등이 검토한 실무자 자료는 잘 설계된 루프의 구성 요소로 기계: Practitioner materials reviewed by Lulla and colleagues identify machine-assessable stopping conditions, state files, verifiers separate from implementation agents, token budgets, and human handoff points as components of well-designed loops. The same study surveyed 36,710 GitHub repositories and identified 217 operating autonomous agent loops. They committed loop-starting configurations, but none of their files specifying termination conditions or budgets matched the researchers’ detection rules (Table 2). The authors acknowledge that repository data can reveal stopping conditions only when written into committed prompts or scripts. They conclude that systematic evidence for the benefits claimed in practitioner materials remains lacking (<v0>Jai Lal Lulla et al., Loop Engineering: Building Blocks, Adoption, and Impact</v0> (arXiv v3, 2026-10-22; Sections 3–4)). Advice to include stopping conditions predates this terminology: Anthropic notes that agents often stop when work is complete, but maximum-iteration limits are commonly added to maintain control (<v1/> (published: 2024-12-19)). The remaining question is what to count and how to choose the limit.
6장은 이 작업 하나를 6.1절부터 6.4절까지 따라간다. 프로그램은 관: Chapter 6 follows one task from Sections 6.1 through 6.4. A program calculates monthly mean temperatures from station CSV files with columns <v0/> and <v1/>; the agent modifies the reading function. The specification (<v2/>) and completion criteria were established in Section 6.1 and are adopted here. The function must report designated errors for empty files, missing temperature columns, and nonnumeric values, such as the Busan file’s missing value <v3/>. The computer-assessed criterion requires all four tests, one valid case and these three failures, to pass. A person separately assesses whether an error message identifies what to correct. The agent must not modify tests or the specification and must stop and ask when encountering an unapproved temperature unit, such as Fahrenheit <v4/>. Chapter 6’s authors assigned this task to Codex once (executed by Sori Yun, 2026-11-20; Codex Desktop 0.171.0-alpha.13, model gpt-6-luna, Windows). Observations were fabricated for illustration.
재시도 한도를 정하려면 먼저 무엇을 한 번으로 셀지 정해야 한다. 공통: Before setting a retry cap, define what counts as one attempt. The shared example includes a grader (<v0/>) that runs tests and decides the outcome. One attempt consists of one code revision followed by one grader run; three attempts are allowed. The initial assessment of unmodified code is recorded as the baseline and does not count. Changing the specification or data folder resets the grader’s counter to zero, effectively granting three new attempts under the changed conditions. Different tools count different things even when the limit is three. aider sends up to three requests asking the model to correct lint or test errors, excluding the initial edit; lint automatically checks code syntax and formatting (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-19; version: v0.86.0; <v2/>)). The AWS SDK’s standard retry mode, however, defaults to three total attempts, including the first request (<v3/> (accessed: 2026-11-21)). A limit without a defined unit invites different interpretations.
매 시도에서 검사 전체를 다시 실행하는 이유는 이미 통과한 테스트가 이번: Rerunning the full test suite on every attempt checks whether the latest change broke previously passing tests. Keep each revision small. The shared example’s instructions (<v0/>) require focusing on failed tests after a retry decision; the exercise below likewise fixes empty files, missing columns, and nonnumeric values separately. This makes it possible to identify which change resolved which failure. In long-running-agent experiments, Anthropic observed agents attempting too many features at once or marking incompletely tested features as finished. To reduce this, feature lists began with every item marked failing, agents worked on one feature at a time, and instructions prohibited deleting or editing tests (<v1/> (published: 2025-11-26)). The shared specification likewise prohibits modifying the <v2/> folder.
다시 할지 멈출지를 판정하는 규칙: Rules for deciding whether to retry or stop
채점기는 시도가 끝날 때마다 채점 결과를 보고 판정을 하나 내린다. 아래: After each attempt, the grader examines the test results and issues one decision. Below is the decision logic from the shared grader, with messages shortened. <v0/> is the current assessment result, and <v1/> is three.
판정은 위에서부터 차례로 확인하므로 순서가 결과를 바꾼다. 테스트 파일이: Conditions are checked from top to bottom, so their order affects the outcome. If tests have changed, the agreed completion criteria have changed too, requiring human input even if more tests pass. Processing an unapproved unit likewise requires a human decision regardless of test results. Passing is checked before the attempt limit because an attempt that reaches the cap should still succeed if all checks pass. Passing does not itself finish the task: the specification still requires human confirmation. Section 6.4 uses a graph to show who decides what after grading.
공통 예시를 Codex로 실행했을 때 채점기는 출발점에서 테스트 4개 중: In the shared Codex run, the baseline passed one of four tests. When a Fahrenheit file from Denver arrived, Codex stopped and asked how to handle it; human approval for conversion increased the test count to five (Section 6.4). The grader returned pass on the first graded attempt after revision. Asked to make another change after passing, Codex refused to edit and cited the rule requiring it to await human confirmation. A person then assessed whether the error message alone identified what needed correction. The filename was clear, but the message did not establish whether 4 was a line number or what was wrong there (Section 6.1). The grader’s pass covered only the computer-assessed completion criteria.
한편 채점기는 Codex가 아니라 사람이 실행했다. Codex의 실행 환: A person, not Codex, ran the grader. Because <v0/> was unavailable in Codex’s environment, its progress notes listed ungraded revisions as attempts 1 and 2, while the grader recorded only the baseline and the human-run attempt 1. The grader counts attempts only when it executes. Before starting a loop, therefore, verify that the grader actually runs in that environment, and use its records, not the agent’s notes, to count attempts. Since the first post-change assessment passed, this run produced neither retry nor stop outcomes.
그래서 같은 작업과 채점기로 네 가지 조건을 만들어 실습했다. 에이전트: I therefore created four conditions using the same task and grader. Prepared changes were applied sequentially instead of invoking an agent, so the exercise tested decision rules and record handling, not a model’s debugging ability. The shared example files contained the final code; the baseline was reconstructed to reproduce the original execution screenshot and baseline grading result. The environment was Windows 11, Python 3.14.4, and pytest 9.2.0 (executed: 2026-11-20).
실습에는 에이전트를 부르고 채점 결과로 다음 행동을 정하는 바깥 프로그램: The exercise used a separate controller, an outer program that invokes the agent and chooses the next action from grading results. It calls the grader unchanged and adds two rules. First, if the grader did not run or no tests executed, stop without grading, marked unable to check. The shared grader does not treat zero tests as passing, but returns retry; this was observed when pytest was unavailable. Otherwise, an agent could exhaust its attempts making ungraded revisions. Second, even after a retry decision, stop for no progress if the failed-test list is unchanged from the previous attempt. If the revision did not affect the result, remaining attempts do not justify continuing the same way. After stop or stop-and-ask outcomes, the controller restores the working folder to the eligible attempt with the fewest failures. Attempts that changed tests or processed unapproved units are excluded. Time budgets are checked outside grading too: before each attempt, the controller stops if total elapsed time exceeds the budget, 30 minutes by default. A cost budget can be added at the same point when an actual model is connected.
한 번에 하나씩 고친다: Fix one issue at a time
시도 3의 코드가 사람의 확인을 기다림: Code from attempt 3 awaits human confirmation
세 번째 수정이 이미 되던 기능을 망가뜨린다: The third revision breaks previously working behavior
실패가 가장 적었던 시도 2의 코드로 되돌림: Restore attempt 2, which had the fewest failures
두 번째 수정이 주석만 바꾼다: The second revision changes comments only
덴버 화씨 파일이 들어온 상태에서, 두 번째 수정이 허락 없이 화씨를 섭: With the Denver Fahrenheit file present, the second revision converts it to Celsius without permission
시도별 실패 수는 테스트 4개 가운데 통과하지 못한 수이고, 첫 값은 출: Failure counts show how many of the four tests did not pass; the first value is the baseline. In the second condition, the third revision added numeric validation but changed the return type from tuples to lists and counted data rows rather than file lines. The previously passing valid-file test failed again, increasing failures from one to two. With no attempts remaining, the grader returned stop, and the controller restored attempt 2, which had the fewest failures. The last attempt is not necessarily the best. An Anthropic experiment iterated frontend design generation and evaluation 5–15 times, and its experimenters often preferred intermediate results to the last one (<v0/> (published: 2026-03-24)). In the third condition, the grader alone returned retry, but the controller stopped because the failed-test list was unchanged.
네 번째 조건은 사람에게 물어야 하는 경우다. 실제 실행에서는 Codex: The fourth condition requires human input. In the actual run, Codex stopped and asked about the Fahrenheit file. This condition instead assumes the agent silently converts it to Celsius. More tests pass, but the specification permits only <v0/>, and the data user must decide whether to accept Fahrenheit files. The grader detected that the function read an unapproved column without error and returned stop and ask. The controller restored attempt 1, before conversion was added.
왜 세 번째 실패에서 멈추는가: Why stop after the third failure?
공통 예시의 채점기는 기회를 3번으로 두고, 세 번째 시도까지 통과하지: The shared grader allows three attempts and hands control to a person with a stop decision if none passes. This is the common rule across Chapter 6’s four sections. Some tools also default to three, but AWS SDK and aider count different things, and the documentation and code examined did not explain the choice. The Google SRE book does provide a rationale: after three requests to overloaded servers all fail, the entire data center may be overloaded, making another retry unlikely to help (<v0/> (Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 21, “Deciding to Retry”)). That judgment concerns transient failures potentially resolved by repeating the same request.
코드 수정 루프의 실패는 성격이 다르다. 시도마다 다른 수정을 넣고, 앞: Failures in code-revision loops differ. Each attempt makes a different change, and an incorrect diagnosis can send subsequent attempts in the same wrong direction. Research has examined repeated revisions. Chen and colleagues’ Self-Debugging experiments let models use execution results to fix their own code up to ten times, but reported that most successful debugging finished within three rounds (<v0>Xinyun Chen et al., Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug</v0> (ICLR 2024; Section 5, experimental setup)). Adnan and Kuhn modeled the effect of debugging across attempts for 18 models on HumanEval, a benchmark of Python functions generated from descriptions, using exponential decay. They concluded that most models lost 60–80% of their debugging capability within two or three attempts (<v1/> (arXiv v2, 2025-07-13; published in Scientific Reports, volume 15)). Recounting the 14 models with at least good exponential-model fits in their Table 1, the estimated attempts until the effect fell to at most 20% of its initial value were two for five models, three for five, four for three, and five for one. These are decay-model estimates, not directly observed counts. Olausson and colleagues found that including repair costs can leave little or no benefit from self-repair, while feedback from a stronger model increases its benefit (<v2>Theo X. Olausson et al., Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?</v2> (ICLR 2024)).
이 근거들을 종합하면 3은 출발점으로 쓸 만한 값이지만, 어떤 작업에서든: Taken together, these findings make three a reasonable starting point, but do not establish it as optimal for every task. The results came from short-code benchmarks with the models studied, and decay rates differed across models. Transfer to repository-level agents editing multiple files remains unverified. I also found no explanation that tool and practitioner retry counts were determined through measurement. For example, Greyling’s repository calls more than five nonconverging automatic fixes on the same PR an infinite fix loop, citing weak verifiers, symptom-focused diagnoses, and unstable tests mistaken for regressions (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-19)). The cases in Section 4.4 also preset their limits: two retries per slide for PPTAgent and three iterations for PaperBanana.
그래서 공통 예시의 한도 3은 출발점으로 두고, 기록이 쌓이면 다시 정한: Use the shared example’s limit of three as a starting point, then revise it as records accumulate. After each loop, record the successful attempt number or stopping decision. If nearly all successful tasks finish within two attempts, reducing the limit to two can bring human handoff forward. Conversely, additional successes in a comparison allowing four attempts could justify considering an increase. Compare time and cost per attempt alongside the time a person needs to take over. Reassess the cap when switching models, since decay rates may change.
한도는 제어 코드에서 센다. Claude Code의 <v0/>은 매 턴이: Count limits in control code. After each turn, Claude Code’s <v0/> has a separate small model inspect the conversation to determine whether conditions are met. This evaluator neither runs commands nor reads files. A condition such as “Stop after 20 turns” can limit execution length, but the evaluator also judges that condition by reading the conversation (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-19; Claude Code 2.1.328)). For exact limits, a script attached to the Stop hook, executed when Claude finishes responding, can count attempts and run tests directly. If Stop hooks extend a turn eight consecutive times, Claude Code ignores the next block and ends the turn; every tool call resets that count (<v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-19; Claude Code 2.1.328; Stop input)). This safeguard breaks repeated blocking without tool use. The task’s attempt limit must be counted separately in a script.
한도에 도달한 뒤에도 선택지가 하나만 있는 것은 아니다. Adnan과 K: Reaching the limit does not leave only one possible response. Within a fixed six-attempt budget, one initial generation and five debugging attempts, Adnan and Kuhn cleared conversation history at points of sharply declining effectiveness and restarted from the original problem alone. All nine models in Table 2 improved accuracy at at least one of the two intervention points. For example, llama3.1:8b improved from 72.56% to 82.32%. However, codestral:22b and devstral:24b performed slightly worse at the earlier intervention point (<v0/> (arXiv v2, 2025-07-13; Table 2)). Olausson and colleagues’ findings support another option: asking a stronger model to diagnose the cause. Under the shared rules, a restart or model change still counts as one revision-and-grading attempt. Thus, after three failed attempts, the task is handed to a person rather than extending the run. The following design example considers when to use these options; Section 6.4 covers paths after human handoff.
다음 시도에 어떤 모델을 쓸 것인가: Which model should handle the next attempt?
루프에서는 시도할 때마다 모델을 다시 고를 수 있다. 모델을 실행해 응답: A loop can choose a model again for each attempt. Running a model to generate a response is inference; a company offering inference as a service is a provider. Multiple providers may host the same open-weight model, and OpenRouter connects multiple models and providers through one API. A query to OpenRouter’s public API at 2026-11-19 06:18 UTC found gpt-oss-120b available from 21 providers through 24 endpoints, the access points through which providers serve a model. Prices per million tokens ranged from $0.15 to $0.95 for output and $0.03 to $0.35 for input (<v0/> (queried: 2026-11-19 06:18 UTC; currency: USD, per million tokens)). Output prices differed by more than sixfold between the cheapest and most expensive endpoints for the same model.
이 차이는 루프에서 세 가지 문제로 이어진다. 첫째, 비용이 시도 횟수만: This creates three issues in loops. First, costs accumulate across attempts. Token counts differ, and models or providers may change, so actual task cost is the sum of each attempt’s cost. Record cost per attempt and specify providers when setting limits. Second, changing providers complicates comparisons. Endpoints for the same named model differed in quantization, which represents weights using fewer bits, and maximum output length; these settings can affect results. By default, OpenRouter weights providers using measured prices, throughput, latency, and reliability, then randomly selects one according to those weights for each request. On failure it selects again from the remaining providers; follow-up requests in the same conversation stay with one provider while its prompt cache, temporarily retained processed input, remains active (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-21)). To compare attempts, record the model and provider that actually responded, and pin the provider during comparisons using <v1/> and <v2/>.
셋째, 오류가 났을 때 다른 모델이나 공급자로 넘어가는 폴백(fallba: Third, fallbacks to another model or provider respond to request errors, not failed checks. OpenRouter’s <v0/> fallback advances when the first model returns an error, including provider downtime, rate limiting, moderation refusals, and input-length validation errors (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-21)). A valid response whose code fails tests is not such an error and triggers no fallback. The loop controller must decide whether to switch models based on checks. OpenRouter describes its Auto Code router as penalizing failures more heavily and changing direction sooner after failed tests or recurring errors. It prioritizes reasoning-effort changes over model changes, switching models when signals implicate the model (<v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-21)). This is the company’s description of its design; its effectiveness was not tested here.
비싼 모델을 필요할 때만 부르는 방식은 연구에서도 다룬다. FrugalG: Research also studies calling expensive models only when needed. FrugalGPT proposed cascades that try models in a predefined order (<v0/> (arXiv, 2023-05-09)), while RouteLLM trained a router to choose a stronger or weaker model for each query (<v1>Isaac Ong et al., RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data</v1> (arXiv v4, 2025-02-23)). Both reported lower costs while maintaining response quality on their evaluated tasks. Varangot-Reille and colleagues survey routing strategies more broadly (<v2>Clovis Varangot-Reille et al., Doing More with Less: A Survey on Routing Strategies for Resource Optimisation in Large Language Model-Based Systems</v2> (arXiv v3, 2025-07-21)). These studies choose models for individual queries; they do not measure switching models between attempts at the same task in a loop.

If both fail, attempt 3 starts fresh with a stronger model or higher reasoning effort, receiving only the specification and failure records rather than the preceding conversation. If it also fails, hand off to a person. This example is informed by the studies and documentation above; its effectiveness was not measured. Section 6.3 examines what information to pass to a fresh attempt.

The controller records each attempt in a state file (<v1/>) and, when the loop ends, creates a handoff record for a person or later run. The following is its handoff record for the second condition above.
이 기록을 받은 사람은 남은 실패 하나와 세 번째 수정이 무엇을 깨뜨렸는: The recipient can begin with the remaining failure and what the third revision broke. Preserving changes and results by attempt avoids repeating the same revision from scratch. Practitioner guidance also recommends recording attempt counts in a state file (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-19)). Section 6.3 covers selecting information for the next attempt; Section 6.4 covers approval of passing results and escalation of stopped ones.

Following the temperature data task used throughout Chapter 6, this section explains how to decide what to show the agent, when to show it, and what to leave in files outside the context window. §5.2 compares context window sizes and the timing of compaction or restarts. §7.4 explains how to implement compaction and session resumption as harness features, and §13.2 discusses maintaining repository instructions as documents that both people and agents read.
새 대화의 에이전트는 무엇을 아는가: What does an agent in a new conversation know?
§6.1에서 소개한 기온 데이터 작업은 6장 저자 중 윤소리가 실행했다(: Sori Yun, one of the Chapter 6 authors, carried out the temperature data task introduced in §6.1 (Codex Desktop 0.171.0-alpha.13, model gpt-6-luna, Windows; run on 2026-11-20). A person playing the role of a researcher asked a coding agent to add input validation to a function that reads station CSV files. During the task, they introduced a Denver station file containing temperatures in Fahrenheit. At 20:25, the agent found a <v0/> column that the specification did not permit, stopped calculating the average, and asked the person to decide how to handle the Denver file.
1분 뒤 같은 폴더에서 새 대화를 열었다. 대화가 길어져 새로 시작하거나: One minute later, they opened a new conversation in the same folder. This step simulated starting over after a long conversation or resuming work the next day. They asked the agent in the new conversation the following question.
<v0/> is a progress log in which the agent was instructed to add one row for each attempt. At this point, it contained only the first attempt: the agent had added handling for empty files, a missing <v1/> column, and numeric conversion errors in <v2/>, but had not run the checks because its execution environment could not find the <v3/> command. The field for human decisions was empty.
새 대화의 에이전트는 13초 만에 기록을 읽고, 세 가지 오류 처리를 추: Within 13 seconds, the agent in the new conversation read the log and summarized the situation: handling for three kinds of errors had been added, but there was no check result yet and completion had not been confirmed. That was accurate within the scope of the log. Because the log stated that the checks had not run, the agent did not mistakenly claim that the task was finished. But when asked what the person needed to decide, it replied, “The log does not mention finding a temperature column outside the allowlist.” It had no way to know about the decision that had stopped the previous conversation just one minute earlier: whether to convert the Denver file to Celsius.
원인은 기록 규칙에 있었다. 작업 규칙 파일 <v0/>에는 “시도할 때마: The cause lay in the logging rule. The task instruction file, <v0/>, said only, “Add one row to the table in <v1/> for each attempt.” Stopping at the Denver file was not an attempt to change the code, so it was not recorded. The information remained in the previous conversation, which the new conversation could not see. What the new conversation knew was exactly what the rules had required the agent to record.
긴 작업을 다루는 하네스 설계에서도 같은 문제를 다룬다. Anthropi: Harness designs for long tasks address the same problem. Anthropic’s Justin Young identified a central challenge in dividing a lengthy development task across sessions: each new session begins without remembering any of the previous work. His harness therefore has the first session create a progress file, a feature list, and an initial git commit. Later sessions check their working directory, then read the git log, progress file, and feature list before starting work <v0/> (published: 2025-11-26). The same problem arises with compaction, which summarizes a conversation so work can continue in a new context window. The Claude Code documentation recommends putting instructions in an instruction file because instructions given only in conversation may disappear after compaction. It explains that the project root’s <v1/> is read back from disk after compaction <v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-22; Claude Code documentation, no version specified). Once context has been cleared or reduced, what remains is what was written to files.
그렇다고 앞 대화 전체를 다음 대화에 그대로 넣는 것이 답은 아니다. C: Passing the entire previous conversation into the next one is not necessarily the answer. Chroma’s Kelly Hong and colleagues tested the relationship between input length and performance across 18 models. In their LongMemEval experiment, they compared inputs containing only the relevant conversation history, averaging about 300 tokens, with inputs containing the full history, about 113,000 tokens, for the same 306 questions. The report states that all models performed substantially better with only the relevant portions <v0/> (published: 2025-07-14). The author counted the GPT-4.1 results in the repository linked from the report, using its LLM judgments without modification. With only relevant history, averaging 269 tokens, the model answered 267 of 306 questions correctly (87.3%); with the full history, averaging 112,673 tokens, it answered 191 correctly (62.4%) <v1/> (<v2/>, commit af80a08, accessed: 2026-11-22). This was a question-answering experiment about conversation history, so its results cannot be transferred directly to coding agents. It does, however, provide a reason to select the information needed for the next round rather than pass along the entire history.
맥락이 들어오는 네 시점: Four points at which context enters a task
코딩 에이전트의 컨텍스트에 정보가 들어오는 시점은 네 가지로 나눌 수 있: Information can enter a coding agent’s context at four points: information supplied whenever a run starts, information loaded when needed, information included in a reduced form, and information stored outside the context window for later reading. The author developed this classification from tool documentation and the sources discussed below.
첫째는 실행을 시작할 때마다 들어가는 지침 파일이다. Codex는 작업을: The first category is instruction files loaded whenever a run starts. Codex reads <v0/> before beginning work. At the start of each run, it concatenates files from the user’s global configuration folder and from the project root down to the current folder. Files closer to the current folder come later and take precedence. It stops adding content once the combined size reaches the configured limit, 32 KiB by default <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-22; no publication date given). Claude Code loads all <v2/> files in the working folder and its parent folders at startup, and loads a subfolder’s <v3/> when it reads files in that subfolder. The documentation recommends keeping each file under 200 lines, explaining that longer files consume more context and reduce instruction adherence <v4/> (accessed: 2026-11-22). Content at this layer takes up context on every run and influences every decision.
둘째는 필요할 때 불러오는 것이다. Anthropic의 Applied A: The second category is information loaded when needed. Anthropic’s Applied AI team describes keeping lightweight identifiers, such as file paths, and loading the necessary material during execution instead of supplying all related material at the outset. Claude Code loads <v0/> initially, then finds and reads other files as needed using tools such as glob and grep <v1>Prithvi Rajasekaran et al., Effective context engineering for AI agents</v1> (published: 2025-09-29). Skills also belong to this layer. In Claude Code, a skill’s description is always in context, but its body enters context only when the skill is invoked <v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-22). §7.3 explains how to create and connect skills. In the temperature data task, the specification <v3/> and progress log <v4/> are not loaded automatically. The first rule in <v5/> tells the agent to read both before starting. The instruction file loaded on every run stays short and acts as an index pointing to further reading.
셋째는 줄여서 넣는 것이다. 앞에서 말한 압축은 컨텍스트 윈도가 찰 무렵: The third category is information included in a reduced form. Compaction, discussed above, summarizes a conversation as the context window fills and starts a new window with that summary. A subagent may spend tens of thousands of tokens exploring a problem but typically return only a 1,000–2,000-token summary to the main agent <v0>Prithvi Rajasekaran et al., Effective context engineering for AI agents</v0> (published: 2025-09-29). The temperature data task also has this layer. Instead of retaining the full test output, the grader <v1/> writes only the names of failed tests to <v2/>, and <v3/> tells the agent to consult only that file when the verdict is to retry. This path was not used in the recorded run because the first grading attempt passed.
넷째는 컨텍스트 윈도 밖에 남겨 두었다가 다음 회차에 읽는 것이다. 앞의: The fourth category is information left outside the context window and read in a later round. Young’s progress file, feature list, and git commits are examples. The same Anthropic article calls the practice of maintaining records outside the context window, such as notes or task lists, structured note-taking <v0>Prithvi Rajasekaran et al., Effective context engineering for AI agents</v0> (published: 2025-09-29). The temperature data task has three such records: <v1/>, written by the agent; <v2/>, written by the grader; and the change history in <v3/>, written by the person.
LangChain은 컨텍스트를 다루는 전략을 쓰기(write), 고르기(: LangChain groups context management strategies into four categories: write, select, compress, and isolate <v0/> (published: 2025-07-02). In the classification above, the second point corresponds to selecting, the third to compressing and isolating, and the fourth to writing. The first point establishes the defaults before these strategies are applied. The following table classifies the files in the temperature data task accordingly.
실행을 시작할 때마다 자동으로: Automatically at the start of every run
규칙 여섯 줄. 고칠 수 있는 파일, 채점 명령, 판정별 행동을 정함: Six rules specifying which files may be changed, the grading command, and the action for each verdict
명세와 바꾼 기록. 화씨 변환을 허용한 결정이 여기에 남음: Specification and change history, including the decision to allow Fahrenheit conversion
시작할 때 읽고, 시도할 때마다 씀 (규칙 1, 6): Read at startup and updated after each attempt (rules 1 and 6)
에이전트 (사람이 정한 것 칸은 사람): Agent; the person fills in the human decisions field

판정이 다시 시도일 때만 읽음 (규칙 4): Read only when the verdict is to retry (rule 4)

새 대화가 이어받는 내용은 무엇을 적으라고 정했는지에 따라 정해진다. 기: What a new conversation inherits depends on what the agent was told to record. In the temperature data task, two gaps in the logging rules became apparent.
첫째 빈틈은 앞에서 본 멈춘 일이다. 에이전트가 멈추고 사람에게 결정을: The first gap was the pause described above. The moment when the agent stopped and handed a decision to the person was the task’s most important state change, but it went unrecorded because it was not an attempt.
둘째 빈틈은 실행이 끝난 뒤 두 기록을 나란히 놓으면 보인다. 에이전트가: The second gap becomes visible when we compare the two logs after the run. The final version of the agent’s <v0/> contains two attempt rows. In both, the verdict field says that checks could not run because the <v1/> command was not found, and the next action field says to restore the Python environment and run <v2/>. In the same folder, the grader’s <v3/> records a baseline at 20:19 (1 of 4 tests passed) and a passing verdict at 20:50 (all 5 tests passed). Because Python could not be found in the agent’s execution environment, the person ran the grader in a terminal. After being told that the checks had passed, the agent followed the rules and made no further changes. With no new attempt, nothing was added to <v4/>. Had a third conversation begun, an agent reading only the progress log would have been told to repeat checks that had already finished. The two logs also count attempts differently. <v5/> counts the agent’s code changes (2), whereas the grader counts grader runs after the specification or data folder changes, or after the person resets the counter (1). §6.2 discusses how to define an attempt.
두 빈틈은 같은 구조에서 나왔다. 기록 규칙이 에이전트가 행동할 때만 쓰: Both gaps came from the same structure. The rules required logging only when the agent acted, so pauses and actions by the person or grader went unrecorded. The following is an improvement proposed by the author based on this run. It has not been tested in a new run.
첫째 줄은 판정을 에이전트가 옮겨 적은 기록이 아니라 채점기가 직접 남긴: The first line directs the agent to read verdicts from the grader’s own record rather than from the agent’s transcription. A progress log written by the agent is a self-report. For facts that a tool can produce, such as verdicts, pointing to the tool’s file reduces omissions and transcription errors. Young likewise explained that he used a JSON feature list because models were less likely to inappropriately edit or overwrite JSON files than Markdown files <v0/> (published: 2025-11-26). Deciding who may write or change each record is also part of the design.
둘째 규칙은 기록할 사건을 시도에서 멈춤과 사람의 개입으로 넓힌다. 멈춘: The second rule expands the events to be recorded from attempts alone to pauses and human intervention. Recording a pause lets the next conversation know what to ask the person. Recording results supplied by the person keeps the progress log current. Human decisions should also be added to the specification’s change history, rather than left only in the progress log. The progress log describes the current task’s state; the specification preserves the criteria for future tasks (§6.1).
다른 작업에 옮겨 쓸 때는 다음 질문으로 진행 기록의 항목을 점검할 수: When adapting this approach to another task, use the following questions to review the fields in the progress log.
지침 파일에는 무엇을 둘 것인가: What belongs in the instruction file?
매번 들어가는 지침 파일이 실제로 도움이 되는지에 대한 연구 결과는 엇갈: Research findings are mixed on whether instruction files loaded on every run actually help. In experiments with multiple LLMs and coding agents, Thibaud Gloaguen and colleagues reported that repository-level instruction files did not improve task success overall and increased inference costs by more than 20% on average. This held for both LLM-generated instruction files and files committed by developers <v0>Thibaud Gloaguen et al., Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?</v0> (v3 published: 2026-09-29). By contrast, Jai Lal Lulla and colleagues ran 124 PR tasks from 10 repositories with and without <v1/>. They reported that including the file reduced median runtime by 28.64% and output tokens by 16.58%, with similar task completion outcomes <v2>Jai Lal Lulla et al., On the Impact of AGENTS.md Files on the Efficiency of AI Coding Agents</v2> (v2 published: 2026-03-30). Because the studies measured different outcomes, neither result establishes that the other is wrong. Both are cited here using their public arXiv versions.
두 연구에서 함께 확인되는 점은 에이전트가 지침 파일의 내용을 잘 따른다: Both studies found that agents followed the contents of instruction files closely. Gloaguen and colleagues concluded that agents adhered well to instructions, but repository overviews recommended by model providers did not help, whereas specifying nonstandard coding practices was useful. An agent that follows instructions closely also follows outdated or incorrect instructions. The following criteria can guide what belongs in an instruction file.
첫째, 코드를 읽어서는 알 수 없는 것을 쓴다. 저장소 구조나 사용 기술: First, write down what cannot be learned by reading the code. Agents can discover the repository structure and technologies by opening files, but they cannot discover which files must not be changed or which commands are specific to the project. All six lines of <v0/> in the temperature data task contain this kind of information. They specify that only <v1/> and <v2/> may be changed, that <v3/> must run after each change, and what to do for each verdict. There is no project overview.
둘째, 지켜졌는지 확인할 수 있게 쓴다. Claude Code 문서는 “: Second, make instructions verifiable. The Claude Code documentation recommends concrete instructions such as “Run <v0/> before committing” rather than “Test your changes.” It also advises enforcing mandatory steps with hooks rather than instructions <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-22). An instruction is a sentence the agent is expected to follow, not an enforcement mechanism. §6.4 and Chapter 7 discuss how to enforce rules.
셋째, 도구마다 다른 파일 이름은 한 원본으로 모은다. Claude Co: Third, maintain a single source when tools use different file names. Claude Code reads <v1/> rather than <v0/>, so its documentation recommends creating a <v3/> that imports <v2/>, allowing both tools to use one source. In the temperature data task, <v4/> likewise contains only the line <v5/>. With two sources, it is easy to update one and leave the other inconsistent.
넷째, 주기적으로 낡거나 서로 부딪치는 지침을 지운다. Claude Co: Fourth, periodically remove outdated or conflicting instructions. The Claude Code documentation warns that when two rules conflict, the model may arbitrarily choose one. In the temperature data task, the agent stopped rather than choosing for itself when two clauses in the specification conflicted (§6.1). A rule in <v0/> told it to ask the person whenever an action fell under the prohibited actions. Without such a rule, contradictions can be silently resolved in favor of one side.
넷째 기준이 왜 필요한지는 이 책의 저장소에서도 확인된다. 저장소의 <v: This book’s own repository illustrates why the fourth criterion is needed. Its <v0/>, created on July 12, 2026, said that chapter files were in the <v1/> folder. The folder was deleted in commit <v2/> on September 21, but <v3/> remained unchanged until October 30, when commit <v4/> consolidated the writing instructions into <v5/> and replaced <v6/> with the single line <v7/>. For 39 days, any agent reading the file was being directed to work on the assumption that a nonexistent folder existed. The revised <v8/> still says that chapter files consist of a lead paragraph and section includes, and that adding a section requires updating the chapter’s includes. An inspection of <v9/> (commit <v10/>) on 2026-11-22 found no chapter files under <v11/>; instead, <v12/> lists section files directly by chapter. The instructions printed by <v13/>, the tool for creating a new section, also still say to add an include to <v14/>.
지침 파일은 코드처럼 실행되지 않기 때문에, 내용이 낡아도 빌드나 테스트: Instruction files are not executed like code, so outdated content does not cause a build or test failure. Stale instructions therefore remain hidden until someone encounters a problem while following them. One approach is to search instruction files and tools for old paths in the same commit that moves or deletes a folder. Running <v0/> in this repository finds the paths still present in <v1/> and <v2/>. But a conceptual reference without a path, such as “chapter files” in <v3/>, will not appear in that search. Structural changes therefore call for rereading the instruction files as well as searching them.
이 절의 실행 기록은 한 도구로 한 번 실행한 작업에서 새 대화로 한 번: The execution record in this section covers one task run with one tool and one handoff to a new conversation. It illustrates how gaps in logging rules affect a handoff, but it does not measure how much revised rules would improve the result. The proposed changes need to be tested by rerunning the same task with the revised rules.
기록할 항목을 늘리면 에이전트가 기록에 쓰는 시간과 다음 회차가 읽을 분: Adding log fields increases both the time the agent spends writing records and the amount the next round must read. As the progress log grows, selecting the relevant information becomes a burden for the next round, much as in the Chroma experiment above. For a short task like the temperature data example, simply adding pauses and the basis for verdicts may be enough. For work spanning several days, a feature list and commit history, as in Young’s harness, may be more useful.
에이전트가 쓴 기록은 자기 보고이므로 틀릴 수 있다. 판정처럼 도구가 남: An agent’s record is a self-report and may be wrong. For facts that tools can record, such as verdicts, treat the tool’s record as authoritative and have the agent’s log point to it. Studies have measured different effects from instruction files. If the goal is to improve performance by adding instructions, follow Gloaguen and colleagues’ recommendation to measure their effect before adopting them.

§6.1에서 완료 기준을 정하고 §6.2에서 실행, 검증, 수정을 반복하: Once we define completion criteria in §6.1 and design a loop of execution, verification, and revision in §6.2, an agent can carry a single task through to completion. Real development work involves several stages: reading requirements, making a plan, changing code, running tests, submitting a PR, and deploying. As the number of stages grows, questions arise that a single loop cannot answer. Can the agent submit a PR as soon as the tests pass? Who takes over if three rounds of changes still fail? Does a person need to check the result before deployment?
에이전트에게 “끝까지 알아서 해 줘”라고 맡기면 이 질문의 답은 에이전트: If we tell the agent to “handle everything through to completion,” it answers these questions during execution. The same request may follow a different sequence on each run, and the person may discover missing steps only after receiving the result. Writing down the stages, the conditions for moving between them, and the points of human intervention before execution makes those answers part of the design.
상태와 전이로 흐름을 적는다: Describe the workflow as states and transitions
이 절에서 그래프 엔지니어링(graph engineering)은 에이전트: In this section, graph engineering means explicitly designing an agent’s work as states and transitions between states. A graph represents states as nodes and transitions as edges connecting them. This section uses the following components.
작업 단계나 판단 상태: A work stage or decision state
한 노드에서 다음 노드로 넘어가는 조건: The condition for moving from one node to the next
한 노드에서 조건에 따라 경로가 나뉘는 지점: A point where the path splits according to a condition
검증 뒤 통과, 실패, 한도 초과: After verification: pass, fail, or limit exceeded
사람의 승인이나 판단을 받는 노드: A node for human approval or judgment
더 나가는 전이가 없는 상태: A state with no outgoing transition
에스컬레이션(escalation)은 에이전트가 정해진 한도 안에서 해결하: Escalation means stopping work that the agent cannot resolve within the specified limits and handing it over to a person.
그래프 엔지니어링은 표준으로 정립된 방법론이 아니다. 이 이름은 2026: Graph engineering is not an established, standardized methodology. The name spread on X, formerly Twitter, in July 2026. Peter Steinberger posted, “Are we still talking loops or did we shift to graphs yet?” A few hours later, Hamel Husain published a post titled “Loop Engineering Is Dead. Enter Graph Engineering.” [Wording and dates are based on the secondary source <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-15).]
이름은 새롭지만 다루는 기법은 새롭지 않다. Anthropic은 워크플로: The name is new, but the techniques are not. Anthropic distinguishes workflows, “systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths,” from agents, “systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage” (<v0/> (published: 2024-12-19; accessed: 2026-11-15)). The author interprets graph engineering as deciding, between these two approaches, which parts of the flow to fix in code and which to leave to the agent’s judgment. State machines, which describe systems in terms of states and transitions, have also long been used in software engineering. Drawn as a graph, the loop in §6.2 is a cycle that returns from a verification node to an execution node.
다음은 코딩 에이전트에게 기능 하나를 추가하는 작업을 맡기는 상황을 그래: The following hypothetical graph illustrates a task in which a coding agent adds a feature. The retry limit of three is an illustrative choice.
“요구사항, 계획, 변경, 검증, 완료”처럼 단계만 순서대로 적은 흐름에: A sequence listing only “requirements, planning, editing, verification, completion” leaves out where to go when verification fails, when to stop, and who checks the result. Drawing the graph reveals that the verification node needs three outgoing arrows, each with its own condition. A table listing the condition, the output passed to the next node, and the limits and stopping criteria for each transition makes gaps easier to spot.
완료 기준이 없으면 요구사항 단계로 돌려보낸다(§6.1): Return to the requirements stage if completion criteria are missing (§6.1)
작업 목록을 작성했다: A task list has been written
작업 목록의 변경을 마쳤다: All changes on the task list are complete
테스트가 실패했고 실패 횟수가 3회 미만이다: Tests failed, and the failure count is below three
실패 횟수가 3회에 도달했다: The failure count has reached three
같은 흐름을 코드로 강제할 수도 있다. LangGraph는 LangCha: The same workflow can also be enforced in code. LangGraph is an open-source Python library from LangChain that defines agent workflows as nodes and edges and saves state during execution. The following excerpt implements the branches after verification and the human approval node from the graph above. Test execution is simulated by taking results from a predefined list in sequence.
<v0/>는 검증 노드가 끝난 뒤 <v1/> 함수의 반환값에 따라 다음: After the verification node finishes, <v0/> selects the next node using the return value of <v1/>. The three verification rows in the transition table correspond to the three lines in <v2/>. <v3/> pauses graph execution at that point and waits for external input. A checkpointer saves the graph’s state, and a thread ID assigned to each run identifies which execution to resume. When the person responds, the graph is invoked again with <v4/> and continues from the same point (<v5>LangChain, LangGraph documentation: Interrupts</v5> (accessed: 2026-11-15)).
다음은 이 그래프를 세 가지 검증 결과로 실행한 기록이다. 실행 환경은: The following records show runs of this graph with three different sequences of verification results. The environment was Python 3.13.13, langgraph 1.2.22, and langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.2. The runs took place on 2026-11-15.
A와 B는 검증을 통과한 뒤 승인 노드에서 멈췄고, 사람의 응답을 넣어: A and B passed verification and paused at the approval node. They finished only after receiving a human response and resuming. A received approval, and B received rejection. C ended in escalation after the third failure, without going through the approval node.
<v0/>를 쓸 때 주의할 점이 있다. LangGraph 문서에 따르면: There is an important caveat when using <v0/>. According to the LangGraph documentation, resuming causes the runtime to rerun the paused node from the beginning. If code with external effects, such as PR creation, appears before <v1/> inside the approval node, that code may execute again on resumption. Put actions that affect external systems in a separate node after approval.
라이브러리를 쓰지 않아도 같은 흐름을 명세나 지침 파일(§6.3)에 적어: The same workflow can be written in a specification or instruction file (§6.3) and given to an agent without using a library. Here is an example.
두 방식은 강제하는 주체가 다르다. 지침으로 적은 흐름은 에이전트가 따르: The two approaches differ in who enforces the flow. A workflow expressed as instructions relies on the agent to follow it; nothing prevents the agent from skipping a step. In a graph defined in code, the runtime controls transitions, so execution cannot reach completion without passing through the approval node. Instructions may be sufficient for a personal project whose results can be checked immediately. If unreviewed changes must not reach external systems, enforce transitions through code or tool permission settings. Chapter 7 explains how to configure harness permissions and hooks.
모든 전이에 승인 노드를 넣으면 사람이 모든 단계를 확인할 수 있다. 그: Adding an approval node to every transition lets a person check every step. But frequent approval requests encourage people to approve without reading. Anthropic explains that repetitive confirmation requests create friction and that users sometimes tune them out (<v0/> (published: 2026-04-09; accessed: 2026-11-15)). More approval nodes do not automatically mean greater safety; their locations need to be chosen carefully.
저자는 전이를 되돌리기 어려운 정도와 영향 범위를 기준으로 세 가지로 나: The author divides transitions into three categories based on how difficult they are to reverse and how widely their effects extend.
되돌리기 쉽고 결과를 바로 확인할 수 있다: Easy to reverse, with results that can be checked immediately
외부 시스템 변경, PR 제출, 배포: Changes to external systems, PR submission, deployment
영향 범위가 커서 실행 전에 확인이 필요하다: Effects are broad enough to require review before execution
새로운 원인 가설 없이 같은 오류가 반복되는 경우, 검증할 방법이 없는: The same error recurs without a new hypothesis about its cause; results cannot be verified
재시도로 해결되지 않으므로 흐름 자체를 고친다: Retries will not resolve the problem, so revise the workflow itself
세 번째 구분은 §6.2의 중단 조건과 이어진다. 루프의 한도에 도달해: The third category connects to the stopping conditions in §6.2. A task escalated after reaching the loop’s limit may require changes to the graph before it is run again. For example, if the verification node cannot reach a verdict because no tests exist, add a test-writing node before the editing node.
승인을 받는 단위도 정할 수 있다. 앞의 Anthropic 글은 Clau: The unit of approval can also be chosen. The Anthropic article above explains that Claude.ai and Claude Desktop let users set each action to always allow, require approval, or block. According to the same article, Claude Code’s Plan Mode shows the entire plan before execution rather than requesting approval for each action, shifting human oversight from individual steps to the overall strategy. In graph terms, this places one approval node after planning instead of one at every editing node. The approaches can be combined: approve the plan once, then place separate approval nodes before PR submission and deployment, which affect external systems.
승인 노드에는 사람이 판단에 쓸 자료도 함께 넘긴다. “PR을 제출할까요: An approval node should also pass along the information the person needs to decide. Someone asked only “Should I submit the PR?” must either find and inspect the changes themselves or approve without checking. Showing a change summary, test results, and remaining risks together puts the necessary information in one place. The “Output passed on” column in the transition table serves this purpose.
적용 예: 코드가 공개되지 않은 논문의 모델 구현: Application: implementing a paper’s model without released code
연구에서는 다른 논문의 모델을 비교 대상으로 써야 하는데 그 논문의 코드: Research sometimes requires using another paper’s model as a baseline even though its code has not been released. When a coding agent is asked to implement the model from scratch using only the paper, the workflow can also be expressed as a graph. The following is an example.
논문 변환 노드는 PDF를 에이전트가 읽기 쉬운 텍스트(예: Markdo: The paper conversion node turns the PDF into text that the agent can read easily, such as Markdown. The model implementation node translates the paper’s architecture and equations into code, while the training implementation node writes the loss function, optimizer, and data loading code. Keeping these nodes separate makes it possible to choose which code to revise after a later failure.
스모크 테스트(smoke test)는 본격적인 학습을 돌리기 전에 코드가: A smoke test is a short check that the code works at a basic level before full training begins. This example checks two things. The first is whether gradients flow to every parameter. After backpropagating the loss once, check that each parameter has a gradient that is nonzero and finite. The second is whether the model can fit a tiny dataset. Train repeatedly on a single batch containing a few examples and check whether the loss falls close to zero. Andrej Karpathy recommends overfitting a single batch of roughly two examples. If that fails, there is a bug somewhere in the code, and you should not move on (<v0/> (published: 2019-04-25; accessed: 2026-11-15)).
코딩 에이전트 예시에서는 검증에 실패하면 항상 같은 수정 노드로 돌아갔다: In the coding agent example, every verification failure returned to the same revision node. In this example, the return node depends on the kind of failure. The following table gives illustrative transition conditions for the diagnosis node. The mappings from symptoms to causes are starting points chosen by the author, not an exhaustive list.
일부 파라미터의 그라디언트가 없거나 0이다: Some parameters have missing or zero gradients
순전파 경로에서 빠진 층, 계산 그래프가 끊긴 연산: Layers omitted from the forward path; operations that break the computation graph
손실 계산, 학습률, 수치 안정성: Loss calculation, learning rate, numerical stability
그라디언트는 흐르지만 작은 배치에 맞추지 못한다: Gradients flow, but the model cannot fit a small batch
손실 함수, 옵티마이저 설정, 데이터와 레이블의 짝: Loss function, optimizer settings, pairing of data and labels
논문에 필요한 설정이 없거나, 같은 원인으로 3회 실패했다: The paper omits a required setting, or the same cause has led to three failures
원인 진단 노드를 두는 이유는 재시도가 헛돌지 않게 하기 위해서다. 모델: The diagnosis node prevents wasted retries. If the problem is in the model architecture, changing only the training code will reproduce the same failure. Recording the diagnosis as an output passed to the next node makes it possible to count failures with the same cause and apply the retry limit from §6.2.
The hyperparameter tuning node is reachable only after the smoke tests pass. There is a reason to fix this order in the graph. If tuning starts while implementation bugs remain, changes to the learning rate or regularization may find settings that merely conceal the bugs’ symptoms.
이 흐름에서 사람이 개입하는 노드는 두 곳이다. 첫째는 사람 판단 노드다: This workflow has two human intervention nodes. The first is the human judgment node. When the paper omits hyperparameters or preprocessing methods, allowing the agent to fill them in arbitrarily changes the comparison conditions without leaving a record. The agent should present candidate values and their rationale, and the person’s chosen values should be recorded. The second is the human review node before tuning. The search space and compute budget affect the fairness of the comparison. Before tuning starts, a person checks whether the baseline model and their own method receive the same budget and whether tuning uses validation data rather than test data.
스모크 테스트를 통과했다고 해서 구현이 논문의 모델과 같다는 뜻은 아니다: Passing the smoke tests does not establish that the implementation matches the paper’s model. Smoke tests check only whether the code is in a trainable state. If the paper reports results on a public dataset, a node that attempts to reproduce those results can be added before tuning. This example does not measure how much expressing the workflow as a graph changes implementation time or result accuracy.
모든 작업에 그래프가 필요하지는 않다. 파일 하나를 고치고 결과를 바로: Not every task needs a graph. For a task that changes one file and allows immediate checking, the loop in §6.2 is sufficient. Graphs are useful when work has multiple stages with failure paths or approval points between them.
다음 단계를 미리 알 수 없는 작업에서는 흐름을 지나치게 고정하면 에이전: For tasks whose next steps cannot be known in advance, fixing the flow too tightly can prevent the agent from taking a necessary path. Investigating a bug of unknown cause is one example. In such tasks, fix only the major stages, such as investigation, revision, and approval, and the approval points between them. Leave the progression within the investigation stage to the agent.
이 절의 내용은 주로 제조사 문서와 실무자의 글에 기댄다. 저자는 그래프: This section relies primarily on vendor documentation and practitioners’ writing. The author did not find a comparative study testing whether graph-based workflow design improves results. §16.2 discusses connecting multiple agents as nodes and designing branches, merges, and shared state.
After designing the workflow, check the following items.
Every node has a defined output to pass to the next node.
Every outgoing transition from a branching node has an explicit condition.
Every path reaches a terminal state, such as completion or escalation.
되돌리기 어려운 전이 앞에 승인 노드가 있고, 승인 노드에 사람이 판단할: An approval node precedes each transition that is difficult to reverse, and it receives the information the person needs to decide.

Workflow
1. Planning: List the files to change and the tasks to perform, then show the list.
2. Editing: Make changes in task list order.
3. Verification: Run pytest.
   - If all tests pass, go to step 4.
   - If tests fail, record the cause, make a fix, and verify again.
   - After three failures, stop and report a summary of attempted fixes and failure logs.
4. Approval: Before creating a PR, show the change summary and test results, then wait for approval.
